readSections: Kolyvagin's article is not publicly available and was NOT read. Following the maintainer's instruction on the issue, two public texts that develop Kolyvagin's method were read instead, completely in the ranges stated. (1) K. Rubin, Euler systems, author's 1999 draft of Annals of Mathematics Studies 147 (Princeton, 2000), https://swc-math.github.io/notes/files/99RubinES.pdf (187 pp., SHA-256 de47655dc35066fd01f2e76a37076ad03dee62e816130586c7674e520be73d50, fetched 29 September 2026): Introduction, Chapters I, II, IV, V and IX, Chapter III §§1–2 and §5, and Appendix B. Chapters VI–VIII, which go beyond Kolyvagin's article, were not extracted. (2) B. H. Gross, 'Kolyvagin's work for modular elliptic curves', in L-functions and Arithmetic (Durham 1989), LMS Lecture Note Series 153 (1991), 235–256, doi:10.1017/CBO9780511526053.009, read on a scan (https://wstein.org/papers/bib/gross-kolyvagins_work_on_modular_elliptic_curves.pdf, SHA-256 60b310c58a3494860c5967a03569a7d30033e9074d9d3d9a0d5bc2dfedd46b32) in full. Item locators name the text they come from. The review also read the author's final version of Rubin's book (https://www.wstein.org/people/rubin/book/hEulerSystems.pdf, xi+227 pp., the published pagination) at every passage cited by a source issue.

sourceVersions.citation: K. Rubin, Euler systems, 1999 draft of Annals of Math. Studies 147 (stand-in for Kolyvagin 1990, which is not public)
B. H. Gross, Kolyvagin's work for modular elliptic curves, LMS Lecture Note Ser. 153 (1991) 235–256, scanned copy
K. Rubin, Euler systems, author's final version in Annals of Math. Studies layout (xi+227 pp., the published pagination; printed page = PDF page − 6); read in review for the source issues

summary: Kolyvagin's "Euler systems" introduced the Euler-system method. A norm-compatible family of cohomology classes over abelian extensions (cyclotomic units, or Heegner points on a modular elliptic curve) is turned, by Kolyvagin's derivative operators, into classes with controlled ramification at auxiliary primes. Global duality then bounds a Selmer group, and so an ideal class group or a Tate–Shafarevich group. No public copy of the article is known. As the maintainer instructs, this extraction reads two public texts that develop the method, and records which. The first is Rubin's Euler systems (1999 draft of Annals of Math. Studies 147): Introduction, Chapters I (Galois cohomology and duality), II (definition and main results), III §§1–2 and §5 (cyclotomic units; Kato's Euler system for elliptic curves), IV (Kolyvagin's derivative classes), V (bounding the Selmer group), IX (variants, including anticyclotomic Euler systems) and Appendix B. The second is Gross's exposition of Kolyvagin's Heegner-point argument (1991), which proves that if the Heegner point y_K has infinite order then E(K) has rank one and Ш(E/K) is finite, in the clean case p ∤ y_K with full GL₂ image, and quotes Kolyvagin's general bound. Rubin's Chapters VI–VIII (twisting, Iwasawa theory, p-adic L-functions) go beyond Kolyvagin's article and are not extracted. The atlas plans this method in detail. EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.0–ES.5 plans the abstract machinery, HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.0–HE.7 the Heegner-point argument, RankZeroOneBSD BSD.3 the analytic-rank-one theorem, and SelmerIwasawaCohomology the cohomological background. After review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90), of 411 items, 304 are planned, 14 are in the libraries (continuous cohomology, inflation–restriction, the connecting map, coinduced modules, the cyclotomic character, L(E,s), the canonical-height torsion criterion) and 93 are missing. All 93 go as sources of existing layers: EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems (58), HeegnerPointEulerSystems (21), KatoEulerSystems (3), EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture (3), RankZeroOneBSD (2), SelmerIwasawaCohomology (1), PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras (3), PadicHodgeRegulators (1) and ModularIwasawaMainConjectures (1). No new roadmap is needed.

items.name: Thaine's bound on class-group exponents
items.statement: (Thaine 1986, [Th]) If F is a real abelian extension of Q, then using cyclotomic units in the fields F(μ_ℓ) for a large class of rational primes ℓ one constructs explicitly a large collection of principal ideals of F, enough to bound the exponent of each Galois-eigencomponent of the ideal class group of F in terms of the cyclotomic units of F.
items.note: Overview claim, stated informally (no hypotheses on p or the character are given here). The stronger order bound (Kolyvagin's refinement) is what the atlas plans: EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L1 says 'Apply ES.4's Poitou–Tate descent bound to the actual class-group/Selmer comparison. The conclusion controls length, not merely exponent.' Rubin notes Thaine's results were already known as a corollary of Mazur–Wiles [MW], but with a much simpler proof. In Rubin's framework this is the Euler system of cyclotomic units (Ch. III §2).

items.name: Kolyvagin's first Heegner-point bound (exponent)
items.statement: (Kolyvagin [Ko1]) Suppose E is a modular elliptic curve over Q with sign +1 in the functional equation of its L-function. Heegner points on E over anticyclotomic extensions of prime conductor of an imaginary quadratic field K give cohomology classes over K; together with duality theorems of Galois cohomology these bound the exponent of the Selmer group of E over Q.
items.note: Overview claim; [Ko1] is 'Finiteness of E(Q) and Ш(E,Q) for a subclass of Weil curves' (Izv. 1988). The rank-zero finiteness endpoint is RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.4 ('Given L(E,1)≠0 … Apply GZ.8 and HE.7 to the base-change Heegner point … prove rank E(Q)=0'), with the Heegner classes of HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.3 ('Apply the existing finite and p-adic Kummer maps to P_c'). The structure of the proof is said to parallel Thaine's.

items.name: Kolyvagin's Euler system of cyclotomic units bounds orders
items.statement: (Kolyvagin [Ko2], 'Euler systems') In Thaine's setting, using cyclotomic units in the fields F(μ_r) for a large class of integers r (not only primes), one bounds the orders (not just the exponents) of the Galois-eigencomponents of the ideal class group of the real abelian field F.
items.note: This is the passage crediting Kolyvagin's original article (the target paper [Ko2] = Grothendieck Festschrift II, Prog. Math. 87, 435–483) with introducing Euler systems. Planned as EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L1: 'The conclusion controls length, not merely exponent.' Rubin proves this in Ch. III §2 from his general Theorem II.2.2.

items.name: Kolyvagin's order bound for the Selmer group via Heegner points
items.statement: (Kolyvagin [Ko2]) For E a modular elliptic curve over Q as above, a larger collection of Heegner points (over ring class fields of squarefree conductor) gives a bound for the order of the Selmer group of E; by the Gross–Zagier theorem [GZ], which links Heegner points with the L-function of E, this bound is closely related to the order predicted by the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture.
items.note: Overview claim with no precise statement in this range; Rubin's book deliberately does not cover the Heegner-point Euler system (p. viii; Ch. IX discusses a modified definition that does). The index bound is planned in HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.6 ('prove the length bound by the index of the bottom class') and the full finiteness in HE.7 ('a non-torsion Heegner point in the stated modular setting yields rank one and finite entire Sha'); the link with the BSD leading term is RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.5 ('Relate the height of a non-torsion Heegner point to the squared index of its class').

items.name: Euler system (informal)
items.statement: Let T be a finite-dimensional p-adic representation of the Galois group of a number field K. An Euler system for T is a collection of cohomology classes c_F ∈ H¹(F,T), for a family of abelian extensions F of K, with properties relating c_{F′} and c_F when F ⊂ F′. (Thaine's situation: T = lim← μ_{pⁿ} twisted by an even Dirichlet character; Kolyvagin's: T the Tate module of a modular elliptic curve.)
items.locator: Rubin, Introduction, This book, pp. vii–viii
items.note: Informal preview of Definition II.1.1 (outside this range). ES.2 plans it: 'Define systems over an explicit directed family of finite abelian extensions … Build the module of compatible classes as an equalizer/submodule … The ES norm relation uses corestriction.' Rubin stresses (p. viii) that his definition does not include Kolyvagin's Heegner points.

items.name: Euler systems bound Selmer groups of Hom(T, μ_{p^∞})
items.statement: The existence of an Euler system for T leads to bounds on the orders of Selmer groups attached to the Galois module Hom(T, μ_{p^∞}) = W*, over K and over Z_p^d-extensions K_∞ of K; the bounds depend only on the given Euler system.
items.locator: Rubin, Introduction, This book and Organization, pp. viii–ix
items.note: Overview of Theorems II.2.2/II.2.3 and II.3.x (outside this range). ES.4 plans the error-tolerant Rubin interface: 'In Rubin II.2.2 retain both n_W and n_W* and every auxiliary-field hypothesis'; ES.8 the Iwasawa version. The proof goes via Kolyvagin's derivative classes (Ch. IV) and Theorem I.7.3 of this range. Rubin notes independent results of Kato [Ka2] and Perrin-Riou [PR5].

items.name: Euler systems form a module; scaling worsens the bound
items.statement: If there is an Euler system for T then there is a whole family of them: the collection of Euler systems is a Z_p-module (and a Gal(K̄/K)-module). Multiplying an Euler system by p gives a new Euler system but a worse bound on the associated Selmer groups.
items.locator: Rubin, Introduction, This book, p. viii
items.note: ES.2: 'Build the module of compatible classes as an equalizer/submodule … A system allowed by the definition may be zero.' ES.5 acceptance: 'scaling a system by varpi changes its index as predicted and cannot preserve a false sharpness claim.' Motivates the 'best possible' Euler system of Ch. VIII.

items.name: Kato's Euler system for modular elliptic curves
items.statement: Kato [Ka3] has constructed an Euler system for a modular elliptic curve over Q (from Beilinson elements in the K-theory of modular curves), very different from Kolyvagin's system of Heegner points; it is used in Chapter III §5 to study Selmer groups of modular elliptic curves.
items.locator: Rubin, Introduction, This book and Organization, pp. viii–ix
items.note: Cited, not constructed, in this book. KatoEulerSystems:L2: 'Apply these regulators to the actual pairs of Siegel units on modular curves … obtain classes in H^1 … prove … the p-direction norm relation and the away-from-p Euler relation.'

items.name: P(τ|B; x)
items.statement: If O is a ring, B a free O-module and τ an O-linear endomorphism of B, P(τ|B; x) = det(1 − τx | B) ∈ O[x].
items.note: Mathlib's Matrix.charpolyRev (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Charpoly/Coeff.lean:291) is det(1 − X•M) for a matrix; Rubin's P(τ|B;x) is this for the matrix of τ in a basis (basis-independent). Used for the Euler factors P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; Fr_q^{-1}) in Ch. II.

items.name: Cyclotomic character ε_cyc
items.statement: For p fixed and F of characteristic ≠ p: ε_cyc : G_F → Z_p^× gives the action of G_F on μ_{p^∞}.
items.note: ε_cyc is Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter p (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307), defined on ring automorphisms of a field L. The Galois-character form of ω and ⟨ε⟩ is not in the library (TauCeti.teichmuller in TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100 is the residue-field Teichmüller lift, a different map); only ε_cyc is library. ω and ⟨ε⟩ are the separate item 'Teichmüller character ω and ⟨ε⟩' (planned in DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3).

items.name: F(B), the field cut out by B
items.statement: If F is a field and B a G_F-module, F(B) is the fixed field of the kernel of G_F → Aut(B), the smallest extension of F whose absolute Galois group acts trivially on B.
items.note: Used for the fields K(W_M), K(μ_M) of Chapters II–IV. The finite-level Galois dictionary (fixed fields of open normal subgroups) is planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-9-the-galois-interface-hilbert-90-and-kummer-theory: 'Finite Galois intermediate fields K ⊆ L ⊆ Kˢ correspond to open normal subgroups of G_K'.

items.name: p-adic representation; V, W, W_M
items.statement: Suppose K is a field, p a rational prime, and O the ring of integers of a finite extension Φ of Q_p. A p-adic representation of G_K = Gal(K̄/K) with coefficients in O is a free O-module T of finite rank with a continuous O-linear action of G_K. With D = Φ/O, set V = T ⊗_O Φ, W = V/T = T ⊗_O D, and W_M = M^{-1}T/T ⊂ W for M ∈ O, M ≠ 0 (the M-torsion in W). T determines V and W, W determines T = lim← W_M and V.
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1: 'Construct continuous representations on finite projective coefficient modules … For field coefficients construct invariant lattices using compactness.' The triple T, V, W and the torsion quotients W_M are the coefficient systems of all later sections; ES.0 plans 'propagation under T→T/varpi^m, inclusion into V and passage to V/T'.

items.name: Rank-one representations O_ρ and Tate twists
items.statement: For a continuous character ρ : G_K → O^×, T = O_ρ (free rank one, G_K acting by ρ); every one-dimensional representation arises this way. For ρ = ε_cyc (O = Z_p): T ≅ Z_p(1) = lim← μ_{pⁿ}, V ≅ Q_p(1), W ≅ (Q_p/Z_p)(1) = μ_{p^∞}. For general O: O(1) = O ⊗ Z_p(1), Φ(1) = Φ ⊗ Q_p(1), D(1) = D ⊗ Z_p(1).
items.note: R01.1 plans twists ('Include restriction, induction, duals, twists and coefficient extension'). The Kummer coefficient μ_n exists as TauCeti.KummerCoeff (TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Coefficients.lean:107) at finite level only; the inverse-limit Z_p(1) is not in the library.

items.name: Dual representation T*
items.statement: If T is a p-adic representation of G_K then so is T* = Hom_O(T, O(1)); also V* = Hom_O(V, Φ(1)) = Hom_O(T, Φ(1)) = T* ⊗_O Φ and W* = V*/T* = Hom_O(T, D(1)).
items.note: R01.1 plans duals and twists. The Selmer groups bounded by Euler systems are those of W* (Theorem 7.3, Ch. II).

items.name: Dual of a character
items.statement: If ρ : G_K → O^× is a continuous character and T = O_ρ, then T* = O_{ρ^{-1}ε_cyc}.
items.note: Immediate; used in §6.3 (T* = O_{χ^{-1}ε_cyc}). Planned with duals/twists in R01.1.

items.name: Tate module of an abelian variety as a p-adic representation
items.statement: If A is an abelian variety over K and p ≠ char K, T = T_p(A) = lim← A_{pⁿ} (with O = Z_p) has rank_{Z_p} T = 2 dim(A). If A and A′ are isogenous, T_p(A) and T_p(A′) need not be isomorphic as G_K-modules but V and V′ are. If End_K(A) ⊇ O_F for a number field F and 𝔭 | p, one may take Φ = F_𝔭 and T = T_𝔭(A) = lim← A_{𝔭ⁿ}, of rank 2 dim(A)/[F:Q] over O; for a CM elliptic curve with F ⊂ K this gives one-dimensional representations.
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6: 'Construct the inverse-limit Tate module from finite torsion … Prove rank … Prove compatibility with scheme isogenies.' No Tate module in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep empty). Kolyvagin's setting is T = T_p(E).

items.name: H^i(K, B) and H^i(K′/K, B)
items.statement: For a field K and a commutative topological group B with continuous G_K-action, H^i(K, B) = H^i(G_K, B) (continuous cohomology, Appendix B); if the action factors through Gal(K′/K), H^i(K′/K, B) = H^i(Gal(K′/K), B).
items.note: Continuous cohomology is Mathlib's continuousCohomology (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Basic.lean:131, homogeneous-cochain model); Tau Ceti has the explicit low-degree model TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1 (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/LowDegree.lean:674). Specialising to G_K is notation. See rB-def-2.1.

items.name: H¹ with trivial coefficients is Hom
items.statement: H¹(K, Q_p/Z_p) = Hom(G_K, Q_p/Z_p) and H¹(K, Z_p) = Hom(G_K, Z_p) (continuous homomorphisms).
items.note: TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1EquivOfSmulEqSelf (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/LowDegree.lean:840): for a trivial action, H1 G M ≃+ Additive (ContinuousMonoidHom G (Multiplicative M)), for any topological group G and topological module M. Used in §6.1.

items.name: Kummer theory for μ_{p^∞} and Z_p(1)
items.statement: By Kummer theory and Proposition B.2.3: H¹(K, μ_{p^∞}) = K^× ⊗ (Q_p/Z_p), and H¹(K, Z_p(1)) = lim←_n H¹(K, μ_{pⁿ}) = lim←_n K^×/(K^×)^{pⁿ} = K^× ⊗̂ Z_p, where ⊗̂ is the p-adically completed tensor product (char K ≠ p implicit).
items.note: Tau Ceti has only the injective half at finite level: TauCeti.kummerClassMap_injective (TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Kummer.lean:298), K^×/(K^×)ⁿ ↪ H¹(G_K, μ_n); its docstring says surjectivity 'needs Hilbert 90'. Planned: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-9-the-galois-interface-hilbert-90-and-kummer-theory (Hilbert 90 and the Kummer isomorphism) and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0: 'prove the tower-compatible identification H^1(F,Z_p(1)) ≃ lim_m F^×/(F^×)^(p^m)'. Used in §6.3.

items.name: H¹ of W_M
items.statement: Suppose M ∈ O is nonzero. The sequence 0 → W_M → W →(M) W → 0 induces an exact sequence 0 → W^{G_K}/M W^{G_K} → H¹(K, W_M) → H¹(K, W)_M → 0.
items.note: Long exact sequence for discrete coefficients through H¹: the nodes exist in Tau Ceti (TauCeti.ContCohomology.DiscreteShortExact.explicitLongExact_H0C/H1A/H1B, LongExact.lean), but the specialisation to W and M is not stated. ES.0 plans 'propagation under T→T/varpi^m, inclusion into V and passage to V/T'. Used for Lemma 5.4.

items.name: Torsion of H¹(K,T)
items.statement: The bottom row 0 → T → V → W → 0 of (2) induces an exact sequence V^{G_K} → W^{G_K} → H¹(K, T)_tors → 0.
items.note: Proof uses Prop. B.2.4 (ker(H¹(K,T) → H¹(K,V)) = H¹(K,T)_tors). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0 'Integral and rational continuous cohomology'; ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1 'Treat T, V=T[1/p], and V/T separately.'

items.name: Kernel of H¹(K,T) → H¹(K,W)
items.statement: The kernel of the map H¹(K, T) → H¹(K, W) induced by T ↠ T/MT ≅ W_M ↪ W is M H¹(K, T) + H¹(K, T)_tors.
items.note: Diagram chase on (2) plus Prop. B.2.4. ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1: 'Construct cohomology for lattices and their torsion quotients … Treat T, V=T[1/p], and V/T separately.' Used for reductions of Euler-system classes mod M in Ch. IV.

items.name: Unramified module and unramified cohomology
items.statement: K a finite extension of Q_ℓ, I ⊂ G_K the inertia subgroup, K^ur = K̄^I, Fr ∈ Gal(K^ur/K) Frobenius. A G_K-module B is unramified if I acts trivially; H¹_ur(K, B) = ker(H¹(K, B) → H¹(I, B)). T unramified ⇔ V unramified ⇔ W unramified, and if ℓ ≠ p this is equivalent to T*, V*, W* unramified.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2: 'Define unramified, strict, relaxed and Greenberg conditions separately.' ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7: 'Specify topological restricted products, unramified subgroups'.

items.name: Unramified H¹ = coinvariants of Frobenius
items.statement: Suppose B is a G_K-module which is a finitely generated Z_p-module, or a finite-dimensional Q_p-vector space, or a discrete torsion Z_p-module. Then H¹_ur(K, B) ≅ H¹(K^ur/K, B^I) ≅ B^I/(Fr − 1)B^I, the second map induced by c ↦ c(Fr).
items.note: Inflation-restriction (Prop. B.2.5(i), in the library as TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitInfRes_exact) plus Lemma B.2.8 (H¹(Ẑ, T) = T/(γ−1)T, not in the library). ES.1 plans the local descriptions at auxiliary primes 'using the actual Frobenius quotient and inertia maps'; SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1 'calculate their unramified/bad-prime comparison terms'.

items.name: Singular quotient = Frobenius-invariants of H¹(I,B)
items.statement: With B as in Lemma 3.2(i), if the residue characteristic ℓ of K is different from p then H¹(K, B)/H¹_ur(K, B) ≅ H¹(I, B)^{Fr=1}.
items.note: Five-term Hochschild–Serre sequence (Prop. B.2.5(ii)) with H²(K^ur/K, B^I) = 0 since Gal(K^ur/K) ≅ Ẑ has cohomological dimension one. The five-term sequence for discrete modules is planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-5-exact-sequences ('exactness of 0 → H¹(G⧸N, M^N) → H¹(G, M) → H¹(N, M)^{G⧸N} → H²(G⧸N, M^N) → H²(G, M)'); for T and V in ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.2.

items.name: dim H¹_ur(K,V) = dim V^{G_K}
items.statement: Suppose p ≠ ℓ and V is a Q_p[G_K]-module of finite Q_p-dimension. Then dim_{Q_p} H¹_ur(K, V) = dim_{Q_p} V^{G_K}.
items.note: From the exact sequence 0 → V^{G_K} → V^I →(Fr−1) V^I → H¹_ur(K,V) → 0. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1: 'calculate their unramified/bad-prime comparison terms'. Used in Prop. 4.2 and Prop. 6.7.

items.name: dim H¹/H¹_ur = dim H²
items.statement: Suppose p ≠ ℓ and V is a Q_p[G_K]-module of finite Q_p-dimension. Then dim_{Q_p}(H¹(K, V)/H¹_ur(K, V)) = dim_{Q_p} H²(K, V).
items.note: Proof: I has a unique maximal p-divisible subgroup I′ with I/I′ ≅ Z_p ([Fr] §8 Cor. 3), so I and Gal(K^ur/K) have p-cohomological dimension one and Hochschild–Serre gives H¹(K^ur/K, H¹(I,V)) = H²(K,V). Needs full-degree Hochschild–Serre (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7 'full continuous Hochschild–Serre with edge maps') and cd_p (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-11-cohomological-dimension). Used in Prop. 4.2.

items.name: Finite part H¹_f and singular quotient H¹_s (ℓ ≠ p, ∞)
items.statement: For K/Q_ℓ finite with ℓ ≠ p: H¹_f(K, V) = H¹_ur(K, V); H¹_f(K, T) ⊂ H¹(K, T) and H¹_f(K, W) ⊂ H¹(K, W) are the inverse image and image of H¹_f(K, V) under H¹(K,T) → H¹(K,V) → H¹(K,W); for M ∈ O, H¹_f(K, W_M) is the inverse image of H¹_f(K, W) under H¹(K, W_M) → H¹(K, W). For each of V, T, W, W_M, H¹_s(K, ·) = H¹(K, ·)/H¹_f(K, ·), so 0 → H¹_f → H¹ → H¹_s → 0.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2: 'Saturation and the passage from V to T and A are separate lemmas.' ES.0: 'The local condition on a quotient remembers the lattice; it need not be the naive full local cohomology group.' These are the local conditions of every Selmer group in the book.

items.name: H¹_f(K,W) = H¹_ur(K,W)_div
items.statement: Suppose T is a p-adic representation and ℓ ≠ p, ℓ ≠ ∞. Then H¹_f(K, W) = H¹_ur(K, W)_div (maximal divisible subgroup).
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1: 'calculate their unramified/bad-prime comparison terms'.

items.name: H¹_ur(K,T) ⊂ H¹_f(K,T) with finite index
items.statement: For ℓ ≠ p, ∞: H¹_ur(K, T) ⊂ H¹_f(K, T) with finite index, and H¹_s(K, T) is torsion-free.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1 (bad-prime comparison terms).

items.name: Comparison of H¹_f and H¹_ur
items.statement: For ℓ ≠ p, ∞, writing 𝒲 = W^𝓘/(W^𝓘)_div (𝓘 the inertia group), there are natural isomorphisms H¹_ur(K, W)/H¹_f(K, W) ≅ 𝒲/(Fr − 1)𝒲 and H¹_f(K, T)/H¹_ur(K, T) ≅ 𝒲^{Fr=1}.
items.note: Proof via Lemma 3.2 and the image of V^𝓘 in W^𝓘 being (W^𝓘)_div. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1: 'calculate their unramified/bad-prime comparison terms'. These finite groups are the Tamagawa-type error terms carried through Ch. II–V.

items.name: H¹_f = H¹_ur for unramified T
items.statement: For ℓ ≠ p, ∞, if T is unramified then H¹_f(K, T) = H¹_ur(K, T) and H¹_f(K, W) = H¹_ur(K, W).
items.note: Immediate from (iii) since W^𝓘 = W is divisible. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1. Used in Lemma 5.3.

items.name: Local condition at ℓ = p
items.statement: When ℓ = p one allows an arbitrary chosen subspace H¹_f(K, V) ⊂ H¹(K, V) (e.g. 0, H¹(K,V), or the Bloch–Kato subspace H¹_f(K, V) = ker(H¹(K, V) → H¹(K, V ⊗ B_cris))), and defines H¹_f(K, T), H¹_f(K, W), H¹_f(K, W_M) from it exactly as in Definition 3.4.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4: 'Once R09 supplies period rings, define and compare finite Bloch–Kato and ordinary local conditions'. Rubin notes the Euler-system argument does not need a particular choice at p.

items.name: Local conditions at archimedean places
items.statement: If K = R or C then H¹(K, V) = 0, so H¹_f(K, V) = 0 and one defines H¹_f(K, W) = 0, H¹_f(K, T) = H¹(K, T), H¹_f(K, W_M) = ker(H¹(K, W_M) → H¹(K, W)) = W^{G_K}/M W^{G_K}. All of these groups are zero unless K = R and p = 2.
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7 'retaining modified Tate terms at real places when p=2'; SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1 'compact support with modified real-place terms at p=2'.

items.name: H¹_f(K,W_M) is the image of H¹_f(K,T)
items.statement: Suppose M ∈ O is nonzero. Then H¹_f(K, W_M) is the image of H¹_f(K, T) under H¹(K, T) → H¹(K, W_M) induced by T ↠ M^{-1}T/T = W_M.
items.note: So W_M's local condition is the same whether W_M is viewed as a sub of W or a quotient of T (Remark 3.9). ES.0: 'Construct Selmer data … prove propagation under T→T/varpi^m, inclusion into V and passage to V/T'; the atlas calls these 'cartesian' conditions.

items.name: H¹_f(K,W_M) = H¹_ur(K,W_M) for unramified T
items.statement: If ℓ ≠ p, ∞ and T is unramified then H¹_f(K, W_M) = H¹_ur(K, W_M).
items.note: Via (i) and Lemma 3.5(iv). ES.1: 'Prove unramified, finite, singular and transverse local descriptions at an auxiliary q'. Used in Lemma 4.7 and Lemma 5.3.

items.name: Local conditions commute with limits
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_ℓ for some ℓ ≤ ∞ (K = R or C allowed), as in §3.2, and T a p-adic representation of G_K. There are natural exact sequences and isomorphisms H¹_f(K, W) = lim→_M H¹_f(K, W_M), H¹(K, W) = lim→_M H¹(K, W_M), H¹_s(K, W) = lim→_M H¹_s(K, W_M), and H¹_f(K, T) = lim←_M H¹_f(K, W_M), H¹(K, T) = lim←_M H¹(K, W_M), H¹_s(K, T) = lim←_M H¹_s(K, W_M), compatible with 0 → H¹_f → H¹ → H¹_s → 0.
items.note: Local groups are finite (Prop. B.2.7(ii)); inverse limits via Prop. B.2.3 and Lemma 3.8(i). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0: 'Record which ordinary inverse-limit hypotheses hold for each tower used below'; ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1: 'Prove the relevant Mittag–Leffler and lim¹ statements before interchanging cohomology and inverse limit.'

items.name: Local duality for V
items.statement: Suppose K is a finite extension of Q_ℓ (i = 0, 1, 2) or K = R, C (i = 1). Cup product and the local invariant map induce a perfect pairing H^i(K, V) × H^{2−i}(K, V*) → H²(K, Φ(1)) ≅ Φ.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. I §4, Theorem 4.1 (Local duality), p. 8
items.note: Cited from [Mi] Cor. I.2.3 / [Se2] II.5.2 plus Props. B.2.3–B.2.4. ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7: 'Prove derived local and global duality … Give finite, compact and discrete torsion formulations'; SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1 imports 'local invariant/Tate pairings'.

items.name: Local duality for W_M
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 4.1, cup product and the invariant map give a perfect pairing H^i(K, W_M) × H^{2−i}(K, W*_M) → H²(K, O(1)/M O(1)) ≅ O/MO.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. I §4, Theorem 4.1 (Local duality), p. 8
items.note: Finite-module local Tate duality is planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-5-local-coefficients-the-brauer-group-the-local-invariant-and-duality: 'Construct local Tate duality from the evaluation pairing Hom(A,μ_n) × A → μ_n. The exported theorem tateDualityPairing_perfect_mixed …'; the O/MO-linear form is a coefficient refinement.

items.name: Local duality between T and W*
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 4.1, cup product and the invariant map give a perfect pairing H^i(K, T) × H^{2−i}(K, W*) → H²(K, D(1)) ≅ D.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. I §4, Theorem 4.1 (Local duality), p. 8
items.note: Compact/discrete form obtained by limits from (b). ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7: 'Give finite, compact and discrete torsion formulations with the inverse-limit and continuous-dual hypotheses used in passage between them.'

items.name: H¹_f(K,V) and H¹_f(K,V*) are exact annihilators (ℓ ≠ p)
items.statement: Suppose K is archimedean, or nonarchimedean of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p. Then H¹_f(K, V) and H¹_f(K, V*) are orthogonal complements of each other under ⟨ , ⟩_K.
items.note: Orthogonality because the pairing factors through H²(K^ur/K, Φ(1)) = 0; exactness by dimension count via Cor. 3.3(i), Theorem 4.1, Cor. 3.3(ii). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1: 'Prove the annihilator and saturation properties of the particular Selmer local conditions'.

items.name: H¹_f(K,T) and H¹_f(K,W*) are exact annihilators
items.statement: Suppose (a) K archimedean, (b) K nonarchimedean with ℓ ≠ p, or (c) ℓ = p and H¹_f(K, V), H¹_f(K, V*) are chosen to be orthogonal complements. Then H¹_f(K, T) and H¹_f(K, W*) are orthogonal complements under ⟨ , ⟩_K.
items.note: From Prop. 4.2 and ⟨φ(c), d⟩ = ⟨c, φ*(d)⟩. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1 (annihilators of local conditions); ES.0: 'Verify the square relating propagated local conditions and annihilators under local duality.'

items.name: H¹_f(K,W_M) and H¹_f(K,W*_M) are exact annihilators
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 4.3, for every nonzero M ∈ O, H¹_f(K, W_M) and H¹_f(K, W*_M) are orthogonal complements under ⟨ , ⟩_K.
items.note: Uses (i) and Lemma 3.8(i). ES.0 plans exactly this square. Input to Theorem 7.3.

items.name: I^M (tame p-quotient of inertia)
items.statement: If ℓ ≠ p there is an exact sequence 0 → I′ → I → Z_p → 0 with I′ of trivial pro-p-part ([Fr] §8 Cor. 3); for M a power of p, I^M denotes the unique subgroup of I of index M (the inverse image of MZ_p).
items.note: Structure of tame inertia. ES.1: 'Construct the ray-class extensions K(q), their selected local cyclic quotients'; The owner is tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-4-the-tame-quotient-of-the-absolute-galois-group ('The tame character and the twist', API item 'the specialization at one prime ℓ ≠ p'); ES.1 consumes it.

items.name: I/I^M ≅ μ_M
items.statement: Suppose ℓ ≠ p and M is a power of p. There is a canonical isomorphism of Gal(K^ur/K)-modules I/I^M ≅ μ_M, given by σ ↦ (λ^{1/M})^σ/λ^{1/M} for any uniformizer λ of K.
items.note: Proof via Kummer theory Hom(I, μ_M) ≅ (K^ur)^×/((K^ur)^×)^M ≅ Z/MZ (unit group of K^ur is p-divisible). Essentially [Se3] §IV.2 Exercice 2. ES.1: 'Construct the finite–singular comparison including its cyclic-group tensor factor'.

items.name: M̄
items.statement: If M ∈ O is nonzero, M̄ ∈ Z⁺ denotes the smallest power of p which is divisible by M.
items.note: Trivial notation (the p-power exponent of O/MO); no library or atlas phrase. Used in Lemma 4.7 and Ch. IV (μ_{M̄} ⊂ K(q)).

items.name: Finite and singular parts at a prime ℓ ≠ p with μ_{M̄} ⊂ K
items.statement: Suppose ℓ ≠ p, T is unramified, M ∈ O is nonzero and μ_{M̄} ⊂ K. Fix a generator ζ of μ_{M̄} and let σ_ζ ∈ I/I^{M̄} correspond to ζ under Lemma 4.5. Evaluating cocycles on Fr and on σ_ζ induces isomorphisms H¹_f(K, W_M) ≅ W_M/(Fr − 1)W_M and H¹_s(K, W_M) ≅ W_M^{Fr=1}.
items.note: The finite–singular comparison at Kolyvagin (auxiliary) primes. ES.1: 'Construct the finite–singular comparison including its cyclic-group tensor factor; prove independence of a chosen generator after that factor is retained.'

items.name: Local pairing in the finite/singular coordinates
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 4.7(i), with an appropriate choice of sign, the local pairing H¹_f(K, W*_M) × H¹_s(K, W_M) → O/MO corresponds, under the isomorphisms of (i), to the natural pairing W*_M/(Fr − 1)W*_M × (W_M)^{Fr=1} → O(1)/MO(1) followed by ±1 ⊗ ζ.
items.note: Rubin gives no proof: 'can be extracted [from] Chapter I of [Mi], especially Proposition 0.14, Examples 0.8 and 1.6, and Theorem 2.6' (sign left unspecified). ES.1 acceptance: 'local orthogonality and strict/relaxed/transverse modifications have correctly dualized conditions'.

items.name: Selmer groups S^Σ, S_Σ, S
items.statement: K a number field, T a p-adic representation unramified outside finitely many primes, H¹_f(K_v, V) fixed for v | p. For a finite set Σ of places: S^Σ(K, W) = ker(H¹(K, W) → ⊕_{v∉Σ} H¹_s(K_v, W)) (classes with c_v ∈ H¹_f(K_v, W) for v ∉ Σ, no condition at v ∈ Σ), and S_Σ(K, W) = ker(S^Σ(K, W) → ⊕_{v∈Σ} H¹(K_v, W)) (additionally c_v = 0 for v ∈ Σ); S(K, W) = S^∅(K, W) = S_∅(K, W). Likewise S_Σ(K, T) ⊂ S^Σ(K, T) (with ∏_{v∉Σ}) and S_Σ(K, W_M) ⊂ S^Σ(K, W_M).
items.note: Relaxed (S^Σ) and strict (S_Σ) Selmer groups. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2: 'Define unramified, strict, relaxed … define the Selmer group as the kernel of the global-to-local quotient map'; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4: 'a Selmer structure 𝓕 on a discrete Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/K)-module M … à la Rubin's Euler Systems I.§1–2'. Tau Ceti has only the explicit elliptic 2-Selmer group (WeierstrassCurve.Affine.selmerGroup₂), not this general notion.

items.name: Relaxing at p removes the choice at p
items.statement: If Σ contains all primes above p, the Selmer groups S^Σ and S_Σ are independent of the choice of the subspaces H¹_f(K_v, V) for v | p.
items.note: Immediate from Definition 5.1. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2 'Prove changes of local conditions'.

items.name: S^Σ = H¹(K_Σ/K, ·) for large Σ
items.statement: Suppose Σ contains all infinite places, all primes above p, and all primes where T is ramified. If A = T, W or W_M (M ∈ O), then S^Σ(K, A) = H¹(K_Σ/K, A), K_Σ the maximal extension of K unramified outside Σ.
items.note: Uses Lemmas 3.5(iv), 3.8(ii) and inflation-restriction. ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.3: 'Define G_{F,S} … Identify the global restriction maps with the placewise maps'. ES.2 needs cohomology 'indexed by the correct enlarged S(F)'.

items.name: S^Σ(K,W_M) ↠ S^Σ(K,W)_M
items.statement: If M ∈ O is nonzero and Σ is a finite set of primes of K, the map ι_M : H¹(K, W_M) → H¹(K, W) induces a surjection S^Σ(K, W_M) ↠ S^Σ(K, W)_M (in fact ι_M^{-1}(S^Σ(K,W)_M) = S^Σ(K,W_M)). This can fail for S_Σ in place of S^Σ (Remark 5.5).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. I §5, Lemma 5.4 and Remark 5.5, p. 12
items.note: From Lemma 2.2(i). ES.0 'propagation under T→T/varpi^m'; SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2 'lattice-change formulas'.

items.name: S(K,T) as inverse limit
items.statement: For a finite set Σ of primes of K: S^Σ(K, T) = lim←_M S^Σ(K, W_M) and S_Σ(K, T) = lim←_M S_Σ(K, W_M).
items.note: From Prop. B.2.3 and Cor. 3.10. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0 'Record which ordinary inverse-limit hypotheses hold'; ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1 (Mittag–Leffler before interchanging limits).

items.name: S(K,W) as direct limit
items.statement: For a finite set Σ of primes of K: S^Σ(K, W) = lim→_M S^Σ(K, W_M) and S_Σ(K, W) = lim→_M S_Σ(K, W_M).
items.note: Direct limits commute with cohomology of discrete modules and with the local conditions (Cor. 3.10). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2 / tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4 (Selmer groups of discrete modules).

items.name: Finiteness of Selmer groups
items.statement: Suppose M ∈ O is nonzero and Σ is a finite set of primes of K. (i) S^Σ(K, W_M) is finite. (ii) S^Σ(K, T) is a finitely generated O-module. (iii) The Pontryagin dual of S^Σ(K, W) is a finitely generated O-module.
items.note: Enlarge Σ, apply Lemma 5.3 and Prop. B.2.7. ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.3: 'Prove finiteness of finite-coefficient cohomology'. Finiteness of S(K,W_M) is what makes the counting in Theorem 7.3/Remark 7.4 possible.

items.name: Selmer groups of Q_p/Z_p and class groups
items.statement: Let O = Z_p, T = Z_p (trivial action). For v ∤ p, H¹_f(K_v, Q_p/Z_p) = H¹_ur(K_v, Q_p/Z_p) = Hom(Gal(K_v^ur/K_v), Q_p/Z_p). If Σ contains all primes above p: H¹(K, Q_p/Z_p) = Hom(G_K, Q_p/Z_p), S^Σ(K, Q_p/Z_p) = Hom(Gal(K_Σ/K), Q_p/Z_p), S_Σ(K, Q_p/Z_p) = Hom(Gal(H_{K,Σ}/K), Q_p/Z_p) = Hom(A_{K,Σ}, Q_p/Z_p), where H_{K,Σ} is the maximal everywhere-unramified abelian extension of K in which all places of Σ split completely and A_{K,Σ} is the class group modulo the classes of primes in Σ. With H¹_f at v | p chosen to be unramified, S(K, Q_p/Z_p) = Hom(A_K, Q_p/Z_p) (equation (4)).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. I §6.1, Ideal class groups I, eq. (4), p. 13
items.note: Needs global class field theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-11-the-global-class-formation-and-global-artin-reciprocity). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4: 'Recover R06's class-group and p-ramified modules from the Selmer groups of Tate twists'.

items.name: Local conditions for T = O_χ
items.statement: Let χ : G_K → O^× have finite order prime to p, T = O_χ, L/K abelian of degree prime to p with χ factoring through Δ = Gal(L/K); D_χ = D ⊗ O_χ, Φ_χ = Φ ⊗ O_χ. For a place v, restriction gives H¹(K_v, V) ≅ (⊕_{w|v} Hom(D_w, V))^Δ = (⊕_{w|v} Hom(D_w, Φ_χ))^Δ (5), identifying H¹_f(K_v, V) = H¹_ur(K_v, V) = (⊕_{w|v} Hom(D_w/I_w, V))^Δ (6) for v ∤ p; for v | p, (6) is taken as the definition (agreeing with Bloch–Kato).
items.note: Uses Cor. B.5.3(ii). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4 (class-group examples from Selmer groups of twists).

items.name: S(K,W) for a character
items.statement: With χ, T = O_χ, L, Δ as in §6.2 and A_L the ideal class group of L: S(K, W) ≅ Hom(A_L, D_χ)^Δ. (For L = K this is (4).)
items.note: Proof: restriction H¹(K,W) ≅ Hom(G_L, D_χ)^Δ since [L:K] is prime to p; H¹_f(K_v,W) = (⊕ Hom(D_w/I_w, W))^Δ; then class field theory (Hilbert class field). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4.

items.name: p-adic completion B^ and χ-component B^χ
items.statement: For a Z[Δ]-module B, B^ = Hom(Hom(B, Q_p/Z_p), Q_p/Z_p) (continuous homomorphisms when B is topological); B^ = B for a Z_p-module and B^ = B ⊗_Z Z_p for B finitely generated abelian, with a canonical map B → B^. The χ-component is B^χ = {b ∈ B^ ⊗_{Z_p} O : γb = χ(γ)b for all γ ∈ Δ} ≅ (B^ ⊗ O_{χ^{-1}})^Δ (after fixing a generator of O_{χ^{-1}}). Since [L:K] is prime to p, B ↦ B^χ is exact and B^ ⊗_{Z_p} O = ⊕_χ B^χ.
items.note: Also defined in the Introduction (Notation, p. x). Pontryagin duals exist in Mathlib (PontryaginDual, into the circle), but not this Q_p/Z_p double dual. The χ-decomposition for prime-to-p Δ is planned in EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture/SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4 ('Prove the plus/minus, Tate-dual and involution comparisons instead of suppressing them in the notation').

items.name: Local conditions for T* = O_{χ^{-1}ε_cyc} are the local units
items.statement: With U_{L,v} = ∏_{w|v} O_w^× the local units of L ⊗ K_v: restriction and Kummer theory give H¹(K_v, V*) ≅ ((L ⊗ K_v)^×)^χ ⊗ Φ, and for v ∤ p this identifies H¹_f(K_v, V*) with U_{L,v}^χ ⊗ Φ (7) (taken as the definition for v | p, agreeing with Bloch–Kato). Dually H¹(K_v, V) ≅ Hom(((L ⊗ K_v)^×)^χ, Φ) with H¹_f(K_v, V) ≅ Hom(((L ⊗ K_v)^×)^χ/U^χ_{L,v}, Φ) (8), via local class field theory ⊕_{w|v} D_w ≅ (L ⊗ K_v)^×, ⊕_{w|v} I_w ≅ U_{L,v}. The local pairing is the natural one, so H¹_f(K_v, V*) and H¹_f(K_v, V) are orthogonal complements.
items.note: Asserted ('one can check'); uses local class field theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-6-the-local-class-formation-and-finite-local-reciprocity). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4.

items.name: H¹(K,W*) = (L^× ⊗ Q_p/Z_p)^χ
items.statement: With χ, T = O_χ, L, Δ as in §6.2: there is a natural isomorphism H¹(K, W*) ≅ (L^× ⊗ Q_p/Z_p)^χ.
items.note: Restriction to L (degree prime to p) plus Kummer theory H¹(L, μ_{p^∞}) = L^× ⊗ Q_p/Z_p (Example 2.1). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4; Kummer isomorphism tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-9-the-galois-interface-hilbert-90-and-kummer-theory.

items.name: Units–class-group exact sequence for S(K,W*)
items.statement: With notation as in §6.2–6.3 (O_L the ring of integers of L): there is an exact sequence 0 → (O_L^× ⊗ Q_p/Z_p)^χ → S(K, W*) → A_L^χ → 0.
items.note: Proof via X_L = {y ⊗ p^{-n} : ord_w(y) ≡ 0 (mod pⁿ) for every w} and 0 → O_L^× ⊗ Q_p/Z_p → X_L → A_L^{(p)} → 0. This is the Selmer-group form of the class group used by the cyclotomic-unit Euler system (Ch. III §2). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4: 'Recover R06's class-group and p-ramified modules from the Selmer groups of Tate twists'.

items.name: Leopoldt implies S_{Σ_p}(K,W*) finite
items.statement: With notation as above, if Leopoldt's conjecture holds for L then S_{Σ_p}(K, W*) is finite, Σ_p the set of primes of K above p.
items.note: Leopoldt: the p-adic completion of O_L^× injects into (L ⊗ Q_p)^×, so (O_L^× ⊗ Q_p/Z_p)^χ → ⊕_{v|p} H¹(K_v, W*) has finite kernel; then Prop. 6.3(ii) and finiteness of the class group. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4 ('p-ramified modules').

items.name: S(Q,W*) = A_L^χ for odd χ
items.statement: With notation as above, suppose K = Q. If χ is odd (χ(complex conjugation) = −1) then S(Q, W*) ≅ A_L^χ.
items.note: (O_L^×)^χ is finite for odd χ, so (O_L^× ⊗ Q_p/Z_p)^χ = 0. Used for the Stickelberger Euler system (Ch. III §4). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4: 'including the even-positive/odd-negative restrictions'.

items.name: Local condition for abelian varieties
items.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over K, T = T_p(A), V = V_p(A), W = A_{p^∞}. For every place v there is a natural injective Kummer map A(K_v)^ ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p ↪ H¹(K_v, V_p(A)) (9), A(K_v)^ the p-adic completion; for v | p, H¹_f(K_v, V_p(A)) is defined as its image (agreeing with Bloch–Kato).
items.note: HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.3: 'Apply the existing finite and p-adic Kummer maps … satisfy the finite/crystalline or ordinary local condition at the coefficient prime'; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4 (Kummer sequence for [m]).

items.name: Orthogonality of Kummer images
items.statement: Let A* be the dual abelian variety; V_p(A)* = V_p(A*). Defining H¹_f(K_v, V_p(A*)) in the same way, H¹_f(K_v, V_p(A)) and H¹_f(K_v, V_p(A*)) are orthogonal complements under ⟨ , ⟩_{K_v}; a polarization of A with the Weil pairing gives V_p(A*) ≅ V_p(A) identifying the two subspaces.
items.note: Stated without proof (Tate local duality for abelian varieties). HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.3 'Weil-pairing self-duality'; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4 lists 'local Tate duality' among Cassels prerequisites.

items.name: S(K, A_{p^∞}) is the classical p^∞-Selmer group
items.statement: The Selmer group S(K, A_{p^∞}) is the usual p-power Selmer group of A, sitting in an exact sequence 0 → A(K) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p → S(K, A_{p^∞}) → Ш(A/K)_{p^∞} → 0, with Ш(A/K)_{p^∞} the p-part of the Tate–Shafarevich group.
items.note: Proof: for v ∤ p, A(K_v)^ is finite and H¹_f(K_v, V_p(A)) = 0 by Cor. 3.3(i) and Remark 3.7, so for all v the local condition is the Kummer image. This is the bridge from Rubin's Selmer groups to Kolyvagin's Mordell–Weil/Sha conclusions. Planned: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4 ('0 → E(K)/mE(K) → Sel_m(E/K) → Ш(E/K)[m] → 0') and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2. Tau Ceti has only the explicit 2-Selmer group (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil/SelmerGroup.lean).

items.name: Bloch–Kato conditions are orthogonal
items.statement: If V is potentially semistable at a place v | p, the Bloch–Kato subspaces H¹_f(K_v, V) and H¹_f(K_v, V*) are orthogonal complements ([FPR] Prop. I.3.3.9(iii), [BK] Prop. 3.8).
items.note: Cited. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4: 'Once R09 supplies period rings, define and compare finite Bloch–Kato and ordinary local conditions'. §7 assumes this orthogonality at v | p as a standing hypothesis.

items.name: Localization maps loc_Σ, loc^s, loc^f
items.statement: For finite sets of places Σ_0 ⊂ Σ: loc_Σ : H¹(K, W_M) → ⊕_{v∈Σ} H¹(K_v, W_M); loc^s_{Σ,Σ_0} : S^Σ(K, W_M) → ⊕_{v∈Σ−Σ_0} H¹_s(K_v, W_M); loc^f_{Σ,Σ_0} : S_{Σ_0}(K, W_M) → ⊕_{v∈Σ−Σ_0} H¹_f(K_v, W_M).
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2 ('kernel of the global-to-local quotient map, with semilocal direct sums'); ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7 ('construct the localization morphism of continuous cochain complexes').

items.name: Relaxed/strict Selmer exact sequences
items.statement: Suppose M ∈ O is nonzero and Σ_0 ⊂ Σ are finite sets of places of K. There are exact sequences 0 → S^{Σ_0}(K, W_M) → S^Σ(K, W_M) →(loc^s_{Σ,Σ_0}) ⊕_{v∈Σ−Σ_0} H¹_s(K_v, W_M) and 0 → S_Σ(K, W*_M) → S_{Σ_0}(K, W*_M) →(loc^f_{Σ,Σ_0}) ⊕_{v∈Σ−Σ_0} H¹_f(K_v, W*_M).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. I §7, Theorem 7.3(i) (Poitou–Tate duality), p. 17
items.note: Immediate from the definitions. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2 'primitive/imprimitive exact sequences'.

items.name: Poitou–Tate orthogonality of localized Selmer images
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 7.3 (and the standing assumption of §7 that H¹_f(K_v, V), H¹_f(K_v, V*) are orthogonal complements for v | p), the images loc^s_{Σ,Σ_0}(S^Σ(K, W_M)) and loc^f_{Σ,Σ_0}(S_{Σ_0}(K, W*_M)) are orthogonal complements of each other under Σ_{v∈Σ−Σ_0} ⟨ , ⟩_v.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. I §7, Theorem 7.3(ii) (Poitou–Tate duality), p. 17
items.note: Proof: for Σ large (Lemma 5.3), the Poitou–Tate sequence ([Mi] Thm. I.4.10, [T1] Thm. 3.1) S^Σ(K,W_M) → ⊕_{v∈Σ} H¹(K_v,W_M) → S^Σ(K,W*_M)^∨ plus Prop. 4.3(ii) gives (11); the general case by a snake-lemma comparison with an enlarged Σ′. This is the global duality input to Kolyvagin's argument. ES.4: 'Apply Poitou–Tate to strict/relaxed modifications and prove length bounds on the dual Selmer group'; ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4 (Poitou–Tate).

items.name: Dual Selmer quotient = dual of the singular cokernel
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 7.3(ii): S_{Σ_0}(K, W*_M)/S_Σ(K, W*_M) ≅ Hom_O(coker(loc^s_{Σ,Σ_0}), O/MO).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. I §7, Theorem 7.3(iii) (Poitou–Tate duality), p. 18
items.note: Restatement of (ii). Rubin's 'main tool' for bounding Selmer groups. ES.4 (Poitou–Tate length bounds).

items.name: Size of the dual Selmer group from localizations
items.statement: If Σ_0 is ∅ or the set of primes above p and Σ ⊃ Σ_0 is large enough that S_Σ(K, W*_M) = 0, then |S_{Σ_0}(K, W*_M)| = |coker(loc^s_{Σ,Σ_0})|. Hence enough classes in S^Σ(K, W_M) give a good bound on |S_{Σ_0}(K, W*_M)|; the purpose of an Euler system is to construct these classes.
items.note: This is the structure of Kolyvagin's argument: derivative classes (Ch. IV) are elements of S^Σ(K, W_M) whose singular localizations at auxiliary primes fill up the cokernel. ES.4: 'Apply Poitou–Tate to strict/relaxed modifications and prove length bounds on the dual Selmer group.'

items.name: S(K,W*)/S_{Σ_p}(K,W*) dual to the singular cokernel at p
items.statement: There is an isomorphism S(K, W*)/S_{Σ_p}(K, W*) ≅ Hom_O(coker(loc^s_{Σ_p}), D), where loc^s_{Σ_p} is the localization map S^{Σ_p}(K, T) → ∏_{v|p} H¹_s(K_v, T).
items.note: Theorem 7.3(iii) with Σ = Σ_p, Σ_0 = ∅, direct limit over M, Prop. 5.6, Cor. 3.10 and Prop. B.1.1 (finiteness from Prop. B.2.7(ii), Lemma 5.7). Used in Ch. II to pass between S(K,W*) and S_{Σ_p}(K,W*). ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4: 'Derive the lattice and rational-coefficient versions with all limit arguments recorded.'

items.name: Hom and Maps
items.statement: For topological groups G, T, Hom(G, T) is the group of continuous homomorphisms and Maps(G, T) the topological group of continuous functions G → T with the compact-open topology.
items.note: Mathlib: ContinuousMonoidHom and ContinuousMap (compact-open topology). Notation only.

items.name: Inverse limits of compact short exact sequences are exact
items.statement: If {A_n}, {B_n}, {C_n} are inverse systems of topological groups with compatible exact sequences 0 → A_n → B_n → C_n → 0 and the A_n are compact, then 0 → lim← A_n → lim← B_n → lim← C_n → 0 is exact.
items.note: Stated without proof (vanishing of lim¹ for compact groups). ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1: 'Prove the relevant Mittag–Leffler and lim¹ statements before interchanging cohomology and inverse limit.'

items.name: Dual of an inverse limit of finite modules
items.statement: If O is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field Φ and {A_n} is an inverse system of finite O-modules, the canonical map lim→_n Hom(A_n, Φ/O) → Hom(lim←_n A_n, Φ/O) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Stated without proof. ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7: 'with the inverse-limit and continuous-dual hypotheses used in passage between them.' Used in Cor. I.7.5.

items.name: Continuous cohomology (Tate)
items.statement: For a profinite group G and a topological G-module T, C^i(G, T) = Maps(G^i, T) with the usual coboundary d^i, and H^i(G, T) = ker(d^i)/image(d^{i−1}).
items.note: Mathlib's continuousCohomology (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Basic.lean:131) uses homogeneous invariant cochains in iterated C(G, …) rather than Maps(G^i,T); Tau Ceti's explicit inhomogeneous model in degrees ≤ 2 is TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1/H2 (LowDegree.lean:674, 730). Comparison of the two for profinite G in degrees 0–2 is planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-3-the-comparison-isomorphisms; all degrees in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees.

items.name: Long exact sequence with a continuous section
items.statement: If 0 → T′ → T → T″ → 0 is exact and there is a continuous (set-theoretic) section T″ → T, then 0 → C^i(G, T′) → C^i(G, T) → C^i(G, T″) → 0 is exact for every i and there is a long exact sequence ⋯ → H^i(G, T′) → H^i(G, T) → H^i(G, T″) → H^{i+1}(G, T′) → ⋯.
items.note: Tau Ceti proves the discrete-coefficient case through H²(G, B) (TauCeti.ContCohomology.DiscreteShortExact.explicitLongExact_H0A … _H2B, TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/LongExact.lean), not all degrees and not the continuous-section case. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees: 'The long exact sequence in every degree.' Note tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-5-exact-sequences deliberately restricts to discrete coefficients ('do not state this layer beyond discrete coefficients'); Rubin's continuous-section version for lattices/Q_p-spaces is ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1 ('Construct cohomology for lattices and their torsion quotients').

items.name: When continuous sections exist
items.statement: If T″ is discrete there is always a continuous section T″ → T; this holds whenever T′ is open in T. When T is a finitely generated Z_p-module or a finite-dimensional Q_p-vector space with the usual topology, there is also a continuous section.
items.note: Discrete case: Tau Ceti TauCeti.ContCohomology.exists_continuous_lift (ShortExact.lean) lifts continuous cochains into a discrete quotient. The lattice/vector-space cases: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1.

items.name: Cohomology commutes with inverse limits of finite modules (Tate)
items.statement: Suppose i > 0 and T = lim← T_n with each T_n a finite discrete G-module. If H^{i−1}(G, T_n) is finite for every n then H^i(G, T) = lim←_n H^i(G, T_n).
items.locator: Rubin, App. B §2, Proposition 2.3 ([T4] Cor. 2.2, [J] §2), p. 152
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7: 'Construct the derived-limit comparisons and retain lim¹ contributions until a proved Mittag–Leffler condition eliminates them'; R02.1. Used throughout (Example I.2.1, Cor. I.3.10, Prop. I.5.6, Lemma B.3.1).

items.name: H^i(G,T) ⊗ Q_p = H^i(G, T ⊗ Q_p) (Tate)
items.statement: If T is a finitely generated Z_p-module then for every i ≥ 0, H^i(G, T) has no divisible elements and the natural map H^i(G, T) ⊗ Q_p → H^i(G, T ⊗ Q_p) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Rubin, App. B §2, Proposition 2.4 ([T4] Prop. 2.3), p. 152
items.note: 'No divisible elements' must mean no nonzero divisible elements. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0 ('Integral and rational continuous cohomology'); ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1 ('Treat T, V=T[1/p], and V/T separately'). Used for Lemma I.2.2.

items.name: Inflation–restriction
items.statement: If H is a closed normal subgroup of G then there is an exact sequence 0 → H¹(G/H, T^H) → H¹(G, T) → H¹(H, T).
items.note: TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitInfl1_injective (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Inflation.lean:237) and explicitInfRes_exact (Inflation.lean:336: (explicitInfl1 G M N).range = (explicitRes1 G M N).ker), for any topological group G, normal N and topological G-module M with continuous action (plus continuity of the G/N-action on M^N). Rubin's statement is for arbitrary topological T, as here. Used in Lemma I.3.2(i), Lemma I.5.3.

items.name: Five-term Hochschild–Serre sequence
items.statement: Suppose further that p is prime and for every G-module (resp. H-module) S of finite p-power order, H¹(G, S) and H²(G, S) (resp. H¹(H, S)) are finite. If T is discrete, or a finitely generated Z_p-module, or a finite-dimensional Q_p-vector space, there is an exact sequence 0 → H¹(G/H, T^H) → H¹(G, T) → H¹(H, T)^{G/H} → H²(G/H, T^H) → H²(G, T).
items.note: Discrete case: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-5-exact-sequences ('exactness of 0 → H¹(G⧸N, M^N) → H¹(G, M) → H¹(N, M)^{G⧸N} → H²(G⧸N, M^N) → H²(G, M) at its four nodes'); not yet in the baseline (no fiveTerm_* declarations). Z_p/Q_p cases by limits (Prop. 2.3) and ⊗Q_p (Prop. 2.4): ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.2 ('Build the spectral sequence for a closed normal subgroup … Identify the low-degree sequence with the existing inflation–restriction maps').

items.name: Finiteness of Galois cohomology
items.statement: Suppose (i) K is a global field, K_S a (possibly infinite) Galois extension of K unramified outside a finite set of places, G = Gal(K_S/K); or (ii) K is a local field and G = G_K; or (iii) K is a local field of residue characteristic ≠ p and G is the inertia group in G_K. If T is a G-module which is finite (resp. finitely generated over Z_p, resp. co-finitely generated over Z_p) and i ≥ 0, then H^i(G, T) is finite (resp. finitely generated over Z_p, resp. co-finitely generated over Z_p).
items.note: Cited as well known ([Se2] II.14, III.8 for i = 1). Case (i) needs finite T of order prime to char K for global function fields; Rubin does not say so (only number fields are used). Planned: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.3 ('Prove finiteness of finite-coefficient cohomology'); local case tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-5-local-coefficients-the-brauer-group-the-local-invariant-and-duality ('Prove finiteness of H⁰, H¹, H² (finite_H)').

items.name: H¹ of Ẑ
items.statement: Suppose G ≅ Ẑ with topological generator γ, and T is a Z_p[G]-module which is a finitely generated Z_p-module, a finite-dimensional Q_p-vector space, or a discrete torsion Z_p-module. Then H¹(G, T) ≅ T/(γ − 1)T, induced by evaluating cocycles at γ.
items.note: Printed 'Z_p[G_K] module' (misprint (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E3). Finite case [Se3] §XIII.1, then limits/⊗Q_p. Not in the library (no procyclic H¹ declaration). tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees lists 'Worked example: Hⁱ(Ẑ, -) in every degree'. Used for Lemma I.3.2(i) and Lemma I.4.7(i).

items.name: lim← H¹(F,T) over a tower
items.statement: (K a field, T a Z_p[G_K]-module finitely generated over Z_p.) If K ⊂_f F_1 ⊂_f F_2 ⊂_f ⋯ and ∪ F_n = K_∞, then lim←_{K⊂_f F⊂K_∞} H¹(F, T) = lim←_n H¹(F_n, T/pⁿT).
items.note: From Prop. 2.3 (diagonal of a double limit). SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3: 'construct H^i_Iw(F,T) using corestriction'; ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1 (limit interchange).

items.name: Norm-compatible invariants vanish
items.statement: Let K be a field and T a Z_p[G_K]-module finitely generated over Z_p (the standing hypothesis of App. B §3). Suppose K_∞ is an infinite p-extension of K. Then lim←_{K⊂_f F⊂K_∞} T^{G_F} = 0, the inverse system taken with respect to the norm maps N_{F′/F} : T^{G_{F′}} → T^{G_F}.
items.note: Proof: T_0 = ∪ T^{G_F} = T^{G_{F_0}} by Noetherianity, and beyond F_0 the norms are multiplication by [F′:F], divisible by arbitrarily large powers of p. Not stated in the library. Planned as the H⁰ vanishing of the packet node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/iwasawa-cohomology (API TauCeti.Selmer.iwasawaCohomology_zero_eq_bot, 'Rubin B.3.2'); that node assumes a cofinal chain of open subgroups, which holds for the countable towers used here. Used in Prop. 3.3.

items.name: Universal norms are unramified at ℓ ≠ p
items.statement: Let T be a Z_p[G_K]-module finitely generated over Z_p. Suppose K is a finite extension of Q_ℓ, ℓ ≠ p, and K_∞ is the unique Z_p-extension of K. If {c_F} ∈ lim←_{K⊂_f F⊂K_∞} H¹(F, T) then c_F ∈ H¹_ur(F, T) for every F.
items.note: Proof: K_∞/K is unramified so I is the inertia group of every F; H¹(I,T) is finitely generated (Prop. 2.7(iii)); apply Lemma 3.2 to H¹(I,T). Planned as part (i) of the packet node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/universal-norms-unramified. Used in Ch. II/VII for Iwasawa-theoretic Euler systems.

items.name: Local unramifiedness of norm-compatible classes
items.statement: Let T be a Z_p[G_K]-module finitely generated over Z_p. Suppose K is a number field and K_∞/K is abelian with Gal(K_∞/K) ≅ Z_p^d, d ≥ 1. If {c_F} ∈ lim←_{K⊂_f F⊂K_∞} H¹(F, T), K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, λ is a prime of F not dividing p, and the decomposition group of λ in Gal(K_∞/K) is infinite, then (c_F)_λ ∈ H¹_ur(F_λ, T).
items.note: From Prop. 3.3 applied along a Z_p-subextension in which λ is undecomposed, then corestriction. Not in the library; planned as part (ii) of the packet node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/universal-norms-unramified.

items.name: Norm-compatible classes are unramified outside S
items.statement: With K, K_∞ and T (finitely generated over Z_p) as in Cor. 3.4, if S is a set of places of K containing all primes where T is ramified, all primes dividing p, all primes whose decomposition group in Gal(K_∞/K) is finite, and all infinite places, then lim←_{K⊂_f F⊂K_∞} H¹(F, T) = lim←_{K⊂_f F⊂K_∞} H¹(K_S/F, T), K_S the maximal extension of K unramified outside S.
items.note: Used with Prop. 2.7 to study lim← H¹(F,T). Planned as part (iii) of the packet node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/universal-norms-unramified.

items.name: Induced module Ind_H(T)
items.statement: For G profinite, H a closed subgroup, T a discrete H-module: Ind_H(T) = Ind_H^G(T) = {f ∈ Maps(G, T) : f(ηγ) = ηf(γ) for all γ ∈ G, η ∈ H}, with G acting by (gf)(γ) = f(γg); it is a discrete G-module. Ind_{1}(T) = Maps(G, T); Ind_H(T) ⊂ Ind_{H′}(T) for H′ ⊂ H closed; for a G-module T, evaluation at 1 gives Ind_G(T) ≅ T and t ↦ (γ ↦ γt) embeds T ↪ Ind_H(T).
items.note: TauCeti.DiscreteCoind (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Coinduced.lean:329): locally constant H-equivariant maps G → A with the right-translation action, a discrete G-module; this is the same object (Rubin's 'Ind' is the coinduced module; locally constant = continuous into discrete T). Evaluation at 1 for H = G is TauCeti.coindEvalTopEquiv (Coinduced.lean:490).

items.name: Cohomology of an induced module restricted to an open subgroup
items.statement: Suppose Γ is an open subgroup of G. For every i ≥ 0 there is a canonical isomorphism H^i(Γ, Ind_H(T)) ≅ ⊕_{g∈H\G/Γ} H^i(gΓg^{-1} ∩ H, T).
items.note: i = 0 by double-coset representatives; i ≥ 1 by exactness of Ind and a Leray spectral sequence ([Sh] pp. 50–51). Only the case Γ = G, i ≤ 1 is in the library (see rB-rem-4.3). tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-7-coinduced-modules-and-shapiros-lemma plans Shapiro 'compatible with restriction and, for open intermediate subgroups, corestriction'; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees plans the all-degree 'shapiroIso' and 'the Mackey double-coset formula in every degree'.

items.name: Shapiro's lemma
items.statement: When Γ = G, Proposition 4.2 is Shapiro's lemma: H^i(G, Ind_H(T)) ≅ H^i(H, T) for all i ≥ 0.
items.note: Degrees 0 and 1 are in Tau Ceti: TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitShapiro0 (Shapiro.lean:120) and explicitShapiro1 (Shapiro.lean:372), for profinite G and closed H. All degrees are planned: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-7-coinduced-modules-and-shapiros-lemma (degree 2, 'explicitShapiro2') and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees ('Construct a chain isomorphism shapiroCochainIso … define shapiroIso').

items.name: H¹ of an induced module as a cokernel
items.statement: With T, G, H as above, for every open subgroup Γ of G there is an exact sequence 0 → Ind_H(T)^Γ → Ind_{1}(T)^Γ → (Ind_{1}(T)/Ind_H(T))^Γ → H¹(Γ, Ind_H(T)) → 0.
items.note: From Prop. 4.2 with H = {1} (H¹(Γ, Ind_{1}(T)) = 0) and the long exact sequence. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-7-coinduced-modules-and-shapiros-lemma: 'Acyclicity and dimension shifting. Coind_1^G A … has vanishing Hⁱ for i = 1, 2'. Used for Prop. 4.5 and Kolyvagin's derivative construction (Ch. IV).

items.name: Restriction/corestriction via induced modules
items.statement: Suppose K is a field, F a finite extension of K, T a discrete G_K-module, and 𝒯 = Ind^{G_K}_{1}(T). There is a commutative diagram with exact rows 0 → T^{G_K} → 𝒯^{G_K} → (𝒯/T)^{G_K} → H¹(K, T) → 0, the same over G_F, with vertical maps the inclusions and Res_F (downwards to F) and N_{F/K} and Cor_{F/K} (back to K).
items.note: Cor. 4.4 with H = G_K and Γ = G_K or G_F; commutativity of the corestriction square is 'essentially the definition'. This concrete description of H¹ is what Rubin uses to build Kolyvagin's derivative classes in Ch. IV. Corestriction in degree 1 exists in Tau Ceti (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Corestriction.lean) but not this diagram; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees plans 'compatibility with the connecting maps'.

items.name: Semilocal Shapiro lemma
items.statement: K a number field, 𝔮 a prime of K, F/K finite, S the primes of F above 𝔮; for Q ∈ S fix 𝔔 | Q in K̄ with inertia/decomposition groups I_Q ⊂ D_Q ⊂ G_K; fix Q_0, D = D_{Q_0}, g_Q ∈ G_K with 𝔔 = g_Q^{-1}𝔔_0. For T a discrete G_K-module and T′ ⊂ T a D-submodule, T′_Q = g_Q^{-1}T′. Then for i ≥ 0, H^i(F, Ind^{G_K}_D(T′)) ≅ ⊕_{Q∈S} H^i(F_Q, T′_Q).
items.note: Prop. 4.2 with G = G_K, H = D, Γ = G_F and D\G_K/G_F ≅ S. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees (all-degree Shapiro and Mackey); ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7 'finite/infinite Shapiro'.

items.name: Semilocal cohomology as induced cohomology
items.statement: With notation as above, H^i(G_F, Ind_D^{G_K}(T)) ≅ ⊕_{Q∈S} H^i(F_Q, T) and H^i(G_F, Ind_D^{G_K}(T^{I})) ≅ ⊕_{Q∈S} H^i(F_Q, T^{I_Q}).
items.note: Prop. 5.1 with T′ = T and T′ = T^I. Printed with Ind^𝒢_𝒟 (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E4). tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees.

items.name: Restriction to a prime-to-p extension, semilocally
items.statement: Suppose F/K is finite Galois, T a finitely generated Z_p-module with continuous G_K-action, V = T ⊗ Q_p. (i) If [F:K] is prime to p, restriction induces H¹(K_𝔮, T) ≅ (⊕_{Q|𝔮} H¹(F_Q, T))^{Gal(F/K)}. (ii) Restriction induces H¹(K_𝔮, V) ≅ (⊕_{Q|𝔮} H¹(F_Q, V))^{Gal(F/K)}.
items.note: Proof: Cor. 5.2 for T/pⁿT, kernel and cokernel of restriction annihilated by [F:K] (inflation–restriction), then limits (Prop. 2.3) and ⊗Q_p (Prop. 2.4). Used for (5), (7) in §I.6. ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.2: 'Prove restriction/corestriction identities and the precise descent consequences for finite extensions of number fields.'

items.name: Ray-class p-extension K(q), Frobenius Fr_q and Euler polynomial P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*;x)
items.statement: Fix a number field K, a prime p and a p-adic representation T of G_K with coefficients in the ring of integers 𝒪 of a finite extension Φ of ℚ_p, unramified outside a finite set of primes. For every prime 𝔮 of K not dividing p where T is unramified, K(𝔮) is the maximal p-extension of K inside the ray class field of K modulo 𝔮, Fr_𝔮 is a Frobenius of 𝔮 in G_K, and P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*; x) = det(1 − Fr_𝔮^{-1} x | T*) ∈ 𝒪[x] (well defined because T* is unramified at 𝔮). K ⊂_f F means F is a finite extension of K.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §1, text before Definition 1.1, p. 21
items.note: ES.1 plans 'Construct the ray-class extensions K(q), their selected local cyclic quotients'; ES.2 plans 'the normalization dictionary between arithmetic/geometric Frobenius and the Tate-dual convention'. No ray-class p-extension or Tate-dual Euler polynomial in Mathlib/TauCeti (TauCeti has ray class groups, TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/Basic.lean, but not K(𝔮) or P). Used in the norm relation of Definition 1.1.

items.name: Euler system for (T,𝒦,𝒩) (Definition 1.1)
items.statement: Suppose 𝒦 is an (infinite) abelian extension of K and 𝒩 is an ideal of K divisible by p and by all primes where T is ramified, such that (i) 𝒦 contains K(𝔮) for every prime 𝔮 of K not dividing 𝒩, (ii) 𝒦 contains an extension K_∞ of K such that Gal(K_∞/K) ≅ ℤ_p^d for some d ≥ 1 and no (finite) prime of K splits completely in K_∞/K. A collection of cohomology classes c = {c_F ∈ H¹(F,T) : K ⊂_f F ⊂ 𝒦} is an Euler system for (T,𝒦,𝒩) if, whenever K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F′ ⊂ 𝒦, Cor_{F′/F}(c_{F′}) = (∏_{𝔮∈Σ(F′/F)} P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*; Fr_𝔮^{-1})) c_F, where Σ(F′/F) is the set of (finite) primes of K, not dividing 𝒩, which ramify in F′ but not in F.
items.note: ES.2: 'Define systems over an explicit directed family of finite abelian extensions ... The ES norm relation uses corestriction; it is not ordinary restriction'. Not in Mathlib/TauCeti (no 'Euler system' declaration in the index). Central object of the whole book; Rubin's version requires the ℤ_p^d-direction (ii), which replaces Kolyvagin's congruence condition (Remark 1.5).

items.name: Euler system for T and for (T,K_∞)
items.statement: A collection c = {c_F ∈ H¹(F,T)} is an Euler system for T if c is an Euler system for (T,𝒦,𝒩) for some choice of 𝒩 and 𝒦 as in Definition 1.1. If K_∞ is a ℤ_p^d-extension of K in which no finite prime splits completely, c is an Euler system for (T,K_∞) if c is an Euler system for (T,𝒦,𝒩) for some choice of 𝒩 and 𝒦 containing K_∞.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §1, after Definition 1.1, p. 22
items.note: ES.2 (same carrier: 'Prove its universal property, restriction of indexing family'). Hypothesis form used in Theorems 2.2–3.8.

items.name: No-splitting condition (Remark 1.2)
items.statement: The condition that no finite prime splits completely in K_∞/K is satisfied if K_∞ contains the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension of K. Since ℤ_p^d has no proper finite subgroups, a prime does not split completely in K_∞/K if and only if its decomposition group is infinite.
items.note: ES.8: 'Several-variable variants retain Rubin's no-completely-split-finite-prime hypothesis'; ESCMC L2: 'Prove its no-completely-split-finite-prime hypothesis for the chosen cyclotomic extension'. Not in library.

items.name: Euler system classes are universal norms in the K_∞ direction
items.statement: If c is an Euler system (Definition 1.1; 𝒩 divisible by p) and K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F′ ⊂ F K_∞, then Σ(F′/F) is empty, so Cor_{F′/F}(c_{F′}) = c_F.
items.note: ES.2: 'Separate the p-power tower relation from the auxiliary-prime relation.' Immediate from Definition 1.1 since F′/F ramifies only above p | 𝒩. Rubin prints 'F′ ⊂ F′K_∞', a misprint for F′ ⊂ FK_∞ (new issue recorded by the review); the statement uses the corrected condition. Used to define c_{K,∞} ∈ H¹_∞(K,T) in Definition 3.1.

items.name: Discarding Euler factors at an auxiliary modulus 𝒩′
items.statement: Given an Euler system for (T,𝒦,𝒩) and an ideal 𝒩′ prime to p, replacing 𝒦 by the maximal extension 𝒦′ of K in 𝒦 unramified at the primes dividing 𝒩′ and 𝒩 by 𝒩𝒩′ gives an Euler system for (T,𝒦′,𝒩𝒩′); the conclusions of the theorems of Chapter II are independent of 𝒦 and 𝒩.
items.note: ES.2: 'removal/addition of Euler factors ... restriction of indexing family'. Used for Kato's system (Remarks III.5.5).

items.name: Ray-class-field presentation of an Euler system (Remark 1.3)
items.statement: For a generalized ideal 𝔪 of K let K[𝔪] be the ray class field modulo 𝔪. Given 𝒦 and 𝒩 as in Definition 1.1, an Euler system for (T,𝒦,𝒩) is equivalent to a collection {c̃_𝔪 ∈ H¹(K[𝔪]∩𝒦, T) : every 𝔪} satisfying Cor_{K[𝔪𝔮]∩𝒦/K[𝔪]∩𝒦}(c̃_{𝔪𝔮}) = P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*; Fr_𝔮^{-1}) c̃_𝔪 if 𝔮 ∤ 𝔪𝒩, and = c̃_𝔪 if 𝔮 | 𝔪𝒩. Given such a collection set c_F = Cor_{K[𝔪]∩𝒦/F}(c̃_𝔪) with 𝔪 the conductor of F/K; conversely set c̃_𝔪 = ∏ P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*; Fr_𝔮^{-1}) c_{K[𝔪]∩𝒦}, the product over primes dividing 𝔪, not dividing 𝒩, which are unramified in (K[𝔪]∩𝒦)/K.
items.note: ES.2: 'Prove equivalence with the conductor-indexed presentation on a cofinal suitable family.' Rubin says 'one checks easily'. Used in III.2.1 to present the cyclotomic-unit system.

items.name: Presentation over 𝒦_min by squarefree r (Remark 1.4)
items.statement: For r = 𝔮_1⋯𝔮_k a product of distinct primes not dividing 𝒩 let K(r) = K(𝔮_1)⋯K(𝔮_k) and F(r) = F K(r) for K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞. Let 𝒦_min be the compositum of K_∞ and all K(𝔮), 𝔮 ∤ 𝒩 (the smallest field satisfying Definition 1.1 for 𝒩 and K_∞/K). An Euler system for (T,𝒦_min,𝒩) is determined by {c_{F(r)}}; conversely a collection {c_{F(r)}} such that, for K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F′ ⊂ K_∞, r squarefree prime to 𝒩 and 𝔮 ∤ r𝒩 with K(𝔮) ≠ K, Cor_{F(r𝔮)/F(r)}(c_{F(r𝔮)}) = P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*; Fr_𝔮^{-1}) c_{F(r)} and Cor_{F′(r)/F(r)}(c_{F′(r)}) = c_{F(r)}, determines an Euler system via c_L = Cor_{F(r)/L}(c_{F(r)}) with r and F minimal such that L ⊂ F(r).
items.note: ES.2 (conductor-indexed presentation); ES.1 ('squarefree-conductor category'). This is the form in which the Kolyvagin derivative construction of Chapter IV is carried out.

items.name: Kolyvagin's congruence condition is automatic (Remark 1.5)
items.statement: Kolyvagin's original method required the Euler system to satisfy an additional congruence condition. Using that 𝒦 contains K_∞ (classes extend in the p-direction) this condition is not needed; in fact it follows from the techniques of Chapter IV (Corollary IV.8.1). Conversely, if the classes satisfy appropriate congruence conditions one can drop from Definition 1.1(ii) the assumption that 𝒦 contains K_∞.
items.note: Credits Kolyvagin [Ko2] with the congruence-condition version; proof deferred to Chapter IV §8 (outside this range). ES.3 mentions 'The raw derivative classes initially satisfy a weak system relation' but no stage names the congruence condition. Recorded as the point where Rubin departs from Kolyvagin.

items.name: Hypotheses Hyp(K,T)
items.statement: Let 𝔭 be the maximal ideal of 𝒪, 𝕜 = 𝒪/𝔭, and K(1) the maximal p-extension of K inside the Hilbert class field. Hyp(K,T): (i) there is τ ∈ G_K such that τ acts trivially on μ_{p^∞}, on (𝒪_K^×)^{1/p^∞} and on K(1), and T/(τ−1)T is free of rank one over 𝒪; (ii) T ⊗ 𝕜 is an irreducible 𝕜[G_K]-module.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §2, Hypotheses Hyp(K,T), p. 24
items.note: ESCMC L1: 'Rubin II.2.2 ... p>2, residual irreducibility, and a tau fixing the designated roots of unity, unit roots and K(1), with rank-one coinvariants'; ES.4: 'In Rubin II.2.2 retain ... every auxiliary-field hypothesis'. Used (Remark 2.6) to produce primes 𝔮 with H¹_f(K_𝔮,W_M), H¹_s(K_𝔮,W*_M) free of rank one over 𝒪/M.

items.name: Hypotheses Hyp(K,V)
items.statement: Hyp(K,V): (i) there is τ ∈ G_K such that τ acts trivially on μ_{p^∞}, on (𝒪_K^×)^{1/p^∞} and on K(1), and dim_Φ(V/(τ−1)V) = 1; (ii) V is an irreducible Φ[G_K]-module. Hyp(K,T) is stronger than Hyp(K,V).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §2, Hypotheses Hyp(K,V), p. 24
items.note: ES.4 (Rubin/classical interface with its hypotheses, rational version). Hypothesis of Theorem 2.3 and 2.10(i).

items.name: Index of divisibility ind_𝒪(c) (Definition 2.1)
items.statement: If c is an Euler system, ind_𝒪(c) = sup{n : c_K ∈ 𝔭^n H¹(K,T) + H¹(K,T)_tors} ≤ ∞, i.e. 𝔭^{ind_𝒪(c)} is the largest power of the maximal ideal by which c_K can be divided in H¹(K,T)/H¹(K,T)_tors.
items.note: ES.4: 'its upper bound is the divisibility index of the initial class, with infinity allowed when the class is zero'; ES.5: 'Define ... the index of a system'. Right-hand side of Theorem 2.2.

items.name: Length ℓ_𝒪, field Ω, set Σ_p
items.statement: ℓ_𝒪(B) is the length of an 𝒪-module B, so that |B| = |𝕜|^{ℓ_𝒪(B)}; ℓ_𝒪(B) = ∞ allowed. Ω = K(1)K(W)K(μ_{p^∞},(𝒪_K^×)^{1/p^∞}) where K(W) is the smallest extension of K such that G_{K(W)} acts trivially on W. Σ_p is the set of primes of K above p.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §2, after Definition 2.1, p. 24
items.note: ES.4 'retain both n_W and n_W*' (these are defined via Ω). Mathlib has Module.length but not this field Ω.

items.name: Euler-system bound for the strict Selmer group (Theorem 2.2)
items.statement: Suppose that p > 2 and that T satisfies Hyp(K,T). If c is an Euler system for T then ℓ_𝒪(𝒮_{Σ_p}(K,W*)) ≤ ind_𝒪(c) + 𝔫_W + 𝔫*_W, where 𝔫_W = ℓ_𝒪(H¹(Ω/K,W) ∩ 𝒮^{Σ_p}(K,W)) and 𝔫*_W = ℓ_𝒪(H¹(Ω/K,W*) ∩ 𝒮_{Σ_p}(K,W*)).
items.note: ES.4: 'In Rubin II.2.2 retain both n_W and n_W* and every auxiliary-field hypothesis; only applications that prove their vanishing may specialize to an error-free formula.' Proof in Chapter V (outside range), via Kolyvagin derivative classes (Ch. IV §4) and global duality Theorem I.7.3. This is the finite-level form of Kolyvagin's argument; applied in III.2.3 and via 2.10 in III.5.11.

items.name: Finiteness of the strict Selmer group (Theorem 2.3)
items.statement: Suppose that V satisfies Hyp(K,V) and T is not the one-dimensional trivial representation. If c is an Euler system for T and c_K ∉ H¹(K,T)_tors, then 𝒮_{Σ_p}(K,W*) is finite. (This holds even if p = 2.)
items.note: ES.4 (Rubin/classical error-tolerant interface: 'exports inequalities in terms of proved finite error constants'). Proof in Chapter V. Remark 2.7: for T = 𝒪 finiteness is equivalent to Leopoldt's conjecture.

items.name: Rank-one T satisfies Hyp(K,T) (Remark 2.4)
items.statement: If rank_𝒪(T) = 1, then Hyp(K,T)(i) holds with τ = 1, and (ii) holds as well.
items.note: ES.0 plans admissibility predicates 'with proved implication lemmas'. Used in III.2.3 and III.2.7 (T* = 𝒪_{χ^{-1}}(1)).

items.name: Finiteness of H¹(Ω/K,W) (Remark 2.5, citing Corollary C.2.2)
items.statement: If V is an irreducible Φ[G_K]-module, then H¹(Ω/K,W) is finite (resp. H¹(Ω/K,W*) is finite) unless T = 𝒪 with trivial action (resp. T = 𝒪(1)).
items.note: Proved in Appendix C (outside range). No atlas stage plans this specific finiteness statement; ES.4 only says the constants are 'proved finite error constants'. Guarantees the error terms 𝔫_W, 𝔫*_W of Theorem 2.2 are finite.

items.name: Exceptional case T = 𝒪 (Remark 2.7)
items.statement: In the exceptional case T = 𝒪 of Theorem 2.3, 𝒮_{Σ_p}(K,W*) is finite if and only if Leopoldt's conjecture holds for K (Corollary I.6.4).
items.note: Cited from Chapter I. IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4 plans abelian Leopoldt only. Explains the exclusion of the trivial representation in 2.3 and Hyp(K_∞/K).

items.name: c_K lies in the relaxed-at-p Selmer group
items.statement: If c is an Euler system then c_K ∈ 𝒮^{Σ_p}(K,T) (by Corollary B.3.4, see also Proposition IV.6.1, and Lemma I.3.5(ii)).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §2, before Theorem 2.10, p. 25
items.note: ES.2/ES.4 local-condition bookkeeping; the universal-norm property forces the local classes away from p to be unramified. Needed to define loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_K).

items.name: Local conditions at p and singular localization
items.statement: For every prime v | p choose subspaces H¹_f(K_v,V) ⊂ H¹(K_v,V) and H¹_f(K_v,V*) ⊂ H¹(K_v,V*) which are orthogonal complements under ⟨ , ⟩_{K_v}. Write H¹(K_p,·) = ⊕_{v|p} H¹(K_v,·), similarly H¹_f and H¹_s = H¹/H¹_f, and loc^s_{Σ_p} : 𝒮^{Σ_p}(K,T) → H¹_s(K_p,T) the localization map (Corollary I.7.5).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §2, before Theorem 2.10, p. 25
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2: 'Define local conditions as submodules ... strict, relaxed'; L1: 'identifying the actual annihilator of each chosen local condition'.

items.name: Finiteness of the true Selmer group (Theorem 2.10(i))
items.statement: Suppose c is an Euler system for T and loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_K) ≠ 0. If T is not the one-dimensional trivial representation, V satisfies Hyp(K,V), and [H¹_s(K_p,T) : 𝒪 loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_K)] is finite, then 𝒮(K,W*) is finite.
items.note: ES.4: 'Apply Poitou–Tate to strict/relaxed modifications'. Proof: H¹_s(K_v,T) torsion-free so c_K ∉ H¹(K,T)_tors; Theorem 2.3 plus Corollary I.7.5: [𝒮(K,W*):𝒮_{Σ_p}(K,W*)] = [H¹_s(K_p,T) : 𝒪 loc^s_{Σ_p}(𝒮^{Σ_p}(K,T))] ≤ [H¹_s(K_p,T):𝒪 loc^s(c_K)]. Applied in III.5.11(i) (Kato's rank-zero theorem).

items.name: Bound for the true Selmer group (Theorem 2.10(ii))
items.statement: Suppose c is an Euler system for T with loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_K) ≠ 0, p > 2 and T satisfies Hyp(K,T). With 𝔫_W, 𝔫*_W as in Theorem 2.2, ℓ_𝒪(𝒮(K,W*)) ≤ ℓ_𝒪(H¹_s(K_p,T)/𝒪 loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_K)) + 𝔫_W + 𝔫*_W.
items.note: ES.4. Proof (p. 26): H¹(K,T)/𝒮^{Σ_p}(K,T) ↪ ⊕_{v∤p} H¹_s(K_v,T) is torsion-free, so ind_𝒪(c) ≤ ℓ_𝒪(loc^s(𝒮^{Σ_p}(K,T))/𝒪 loc^s(c_K)); combine with Theorem 2.2 and equality (1) of Corollary I.7.5. Applied in III.5.11(ii).

items.name: Index of divisibility bounded by the localized index
items.statement: If loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_K) ≠ 0 then ind_𝒪(c) ≤ ℓ_𝒪(loc^s_{Σ_p}(𝒮^{Σ_p}(K,T))/𝒪 loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_K)); indeed c_K ∈ 𝔭^n H¹(K,T) + H¹(K,T)_tors ⇒ c_K ∈ 𝔭^n 𝒮^{Σ_p}(K,T) + H¹(K,T)_tors ⇒ loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_K) ∈ 𝔭^n loc^s_{Σ_p}(𝒮^{Σ_p}(K,T)).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §2, proof of Theorem 2.10, p. 26
items.note: ES.4/ES.5 index bookkeeping. Key step converting the Euler-system bound into an L-value bound via localization at p.

items.name: Iwasawa algebra, pseudo-null modules, characteristic ideal
items.statement: For K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, Λ_F = 𝒪[Gal(F/K)]; Γ = Gal(K_∞/K) and Λ = 𝒪[[Γ]] = lim_← Λ_F (noncanonically a power series ring over 𝒪 in d variables). A Λ-module B is pseudo-null if annihilated by an ideal of height at least two; a pseudo-isomorphism has pseudo-null kernel and cokernel. For a finitely generated torsion Λ-module B there is an injective pseudo-isomorphism ⊕_i Λ/f_iΛ ↪ B and char(B) = ∏_i f_iΛ (well defined; the f_iΛ are unique if f_{i+1} | f_i). If B is finitely generated but not torsion, char(B) = 0.
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4: 'Define characteristic ideals intrinsically from lengths at height-one primes ... For O[[Z_p^d]] use height-one divisors; pseudo-null means codimension at least two'. Not in Mathlib/TauCeti (no characteristic-ideal declaration).

items.name: Multiplicativity of characteristic ideals
items.statement: If 0 → B′ → B → B″ → 0 is an exact sequence of finitely generated Λ-modules, then char(B) = char(B′)char(B″).
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4: 'Prove multiplicativity in short exact sequences, invariance under pseudo-isomorphism'. Used in proofs of 3.8, III.2.7, III.2.10.

items.name: Hypothesis Hyp(K_∞/K)
items.statement: If rank_{ℤ_p}(Γ) = 1 and G_{K_∞} acts either trivially or by the cyclotomic character on V, then either K is a totally real field and Leopoldt's conjecture holds for K (i.e. the p-adic completion of 𝒪_K^× injects into (𝒪_K ⊗ ℤ_p)^×), or K is an imaginary quadratic field. (Satisfied if K = ℚ.)
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §3, Hypothesis Hyp(K_∞/K), p. 27
items.note: ES.8 (Rubin's multivariable hypotheses retained); ESCMC L2 imports 'the inverse-limit and multivariable bounds of Rubin II.3'.

items.name: Hypotheses Hyp(K_∞,T) and Hyp(K_∞,V)
items.statement: Hyp(K_∞,T) (resp. Hyp(K_∞,V)) is Hyp(K,T) (resp. Hyp(K,V)) with G_K replaced by G_{K_∞}: (i) there is τ ∈ G_{K_∞} acting trivially on μ_{p^∞}, (𝒪_K^×)^{1/p^∞} and K(1) with T/(τ−1)T free of rank one over 𝒪 (resp. dim_Φ V/(τ−1)V = 1); (ii) T ⊗ 𝕜 irreducible as 𝕜[G_{K_∞}]-module (resp. V irreducible as Φ[G_{K_∞}]-module).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §3, Hypotheses Hyp(K_∞,T), Hyp(K_∞,V), p. 27
items.note: ES.8 (Iwasawa variation with Rubin's hypotheses). Verified for elliptic curves in III Proposition 5.8.

items.name: Implications between the hypotheses
items.statement: Hyp(K_∞,T) ⇒ Hyp(K_∞,V), Hyp(K,T) ⇒ Hyp(K,V), Hyp(K_∞,T) ⇒ Hyp(K,T), Hyp(K_∞,V) ⇒ Hyp(K,V).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §3, diagram after Hyp(K_∞,V), p. 27
items.note: ES.0: 'These are different records with proved implication lemmas'.

items.name: X_∞, H¹_∞(K,T), c_{K,∞} and ind_Λ(c) (Definition 3.1)
items.statement: With 𝐃 = Φ/𝒪 define Λ-modules 𝒮_{Σ_p}(K_∞,W*) = lim_→ 𝒮_{Σ_p}(F,W*), X_∞ = Hom_𝒪(𝒮_{Σ_p}(K_∞,W*),𝐃), H¹_∞(K,T) = lim_← H¹(F,T) (K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞; limits for restriction resp. corestriction).
