If c is an Euler system let c_{K,∞} = {c_F}_{K⊂_f F⊂K_∞} ∈ H¹_∞(K,T) and ind_Λ(c) = {φ(c_{K,∞}) : φ ∈ Hom_Λ(H¹_∞(K,T),Λ)} ⊂ Λ.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3: 'construct H^i_Iw(F,T) using corestriction'; ES.8: 'construct the Iwasawa system maps'. ind_Λ is the Λ-analogue of Definition 2.1.

items.name: Weak Leopoldt from an Euler system (Theorem 3.2)
items.statement: Suppose c is an Euler system for (T,K_∞), and V satisfies Hyp(K_∞,V). If c_{K,∞} does not belong to the Λ-torsion submodule of H¹_∞(K,T) then X_∞ is a torsion Λ-module.
items.note: ES.8; ESCMC L2 'Import the inverse-limit and multivariable bounds of Rubin II.3 from ES.8'. Remark 3.5: 'X_∞ torsion' is the weak Leopoldt conjecture for T. Proof in Chapter VII.

items.name: char(X_∞) divides ind_Λ(c) (Theorem 3.3)
items.statement: Suppose c is an Euler system for (T,K_∞), and T satisfies hypotheses Hyp(K_∞,T) and Hyp(K_∞/K). Then char(X_∞) divides ind_Λ(c).
items.note: ES.8/ESCMC L2 (as for 3.2). Used in III.2.7 (cyclotomic units; holds also for p = 2) and via 3.8 in III.5.16.

items.name: char(X_∞) divides p^t ind_Λ(c) (Theorem 3.4)
items.statement: Suppose c is an Euler system for (T,K_∞), and V satisfies hypotheses Hyp(K_∞,V) and Hyp(K_∞/K). Then there is a nonnegative integer t such that char(X_∞) divides p^t ind_Λ(c).
items.note: ES.8; ESCMC L2. Rational version of 3.3.

items.name: Weak Leopoldt conjecture for T (Remark 3.5)
items.statement: The assertion that X_∞ is a torsion Λ-module is called the weak Leopoldt conjecture for T.
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory I.2: 'Weak Leopoldt in the cyclotomic tower is a theorem to prove here' (for class-group modules); general-T version not planned separately.

items.name: Compatible local conditions in the tower; 𝒮(K_∞,W*) and H¹_{∞,s}(K_p,T)
items.statement: For every K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞ and w | p choose orthogonal-complement subspaces H¹_f(F_w,V), H¹_f(F_w,V*) with Cor_{F′_{w′}/F_w} H¹_f(F′_{w′},V) ⊂ H¹_f(F_w,V) and Res_{F′_{w′}/F_w} H¹_f(F_w,V*) ⊂ H¹_f(F′_{w′},V*) (the two are equivalent). Define 𝒮(K_∞,W*) = lim_→ 𝒮(F,W*) and H¹_{∞,s}(K_p,T) = lim_← H¹_s(F_p,T), with H¹(F_p,·) = ⊕_{w|p} H¹(F_w,·).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §3, Remark 3.6 and definitions, pp. 28–29
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3: 'Infinite-level local conditions are defined by the appropriate limits'.

items.name: Exact sequence relating true and strict Selmer duals (Proposition 3.7)
items.statement: There is an exact sequence 0 → H¹_{∞,s}(K_p,T)/loc^s_{Σ_p}(H¹_∞(K,T)) → Hom_𝒪(𝒮(K_∞,W*),𝐃) → X_∞ → 0, where loc^s_{Σ_p} : H¹_∞(K,T) → H¹_{∞,s}(K_p,T) is the localization map.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 (limits/control) with L1 duality. Proof: H¹_∞(K,T) = lim_← 𝒮^{Σ_p}(F,T) (Corollary B.3.4), then Corollary I.7.5 in the limit and Hom_𝒪(·,𝐃).

items.name: Main-conjecture divisibility for the true Selmer group (Theorem 3.8)
items.statement: Suppose c is an Euler system for (T,K_∞), and V satisfies Hyp(K_∞,V) and Hyp(K_∞/K). If loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_{K,∞}) ∉ H¹_{∞,s}(K_p,T)_{Λ-tors} and H¹_{∞,s}(K_p,T)/Λ loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_{K,∞}) is a torsion Λ-module, then Hom_𝒪(𝒮(K_∞,W*),𝐃) is a torsion Λ-module and (i) there is a nonnegative integer t such that char(Hom_𝒪(𝒮(K_∞,W*),𝐃)) divides p^t char(H¹_{∞,s}(K_p,T)/Λ loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_{K,∞})); (ii) if T satisfies Hyp(K_∞,T) then char(Hom_𝒪(𝒮(K_∞,W*),𝐃)) divides char(H¹_{∞,s}(K_p,T)/Λ loc^s_{Σ_p}(c_{K,∞})).
items.note: ES.8; KatoEulerSystems L4 'Deduce the standard cohomological divisibility and the ordinary Selmer divisibility'. Proof: 3.2 + 3.7 give char(Hom(𝒮,𝐃)) = char(X_∞)char(H¹_{∞,s}/loc^s(H¹_∞)); loc^s(H¹_∞) has rank one, so there is ψ into Λ with pseudo-null cokernel, and ind_Λ(c) divides ψ∘loc^s(c_{K,∞}); conclude with 3.3/3.4. Applied in III.5.16.

items.name: Twisted classes c^χ_F (Definition 4.1)
items.statement: Suppose c is an Euler system for (T,𝒦,𝒩) and χ : Gal(𝒦/K) → 𝒪^× is a character of finite order; 𝒪_χ is free of rank one with G_K acting by χ, with fixed generator ξ_χ, and T ⊗ χ = T ⊗_𝒪 𝒪_χ. Let L = 𝒦^{ker χ}. For K ⊂_f F ⊂ 𝒦, c^χ_F ∈ H¹(F,T⊗χ) is the image of c_{FL} under H¹(FL,T) →(⊗ξ_χ) H¹(FL,T)⊗𝒪_χ ≅ H¹(FL,T⊗χ) →(Cor) H¹(F,T⊗χ) (the middle isomorphism since G_{FL} ⊂ ker χ).
items.note: ES.2: 'Prove its universal property, restriction of indexing family, coefficient extension ..., twisting'.

items.name: Twisted Euler system (Proposition 4.2)
items.statement: Suppose c is an Euler system for (T,𝒦,𝒩) and χ : Gal(𝒦/K) → 𝒪^× is a character of finite order with conductor 𝔣. Then {c^χ_F : K ⊂_f F ⊂ 𝒦} is an Euler system for (T⊗χ, 𝒦, 𝔣𝒩).
items.note: ES.2 ('twisting'). Proof uses P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*; χ(Fr_𝔮)x) = P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|(T⊗χ)*; x) and Σ(F′L/FL) = {𝔮 ∤ 𝔣𝒩 ramified in F′ but not F}. Used in III.2.2 (c = c̃^{χ^{-1}}) and Remarks III.5.5.

items.name: Restriction of a twisted class (Lemma 4.3)
items.statement: With notation as in Definition 4.1, if K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, L ⊂ L′ ⊂ 𝒦, and the conductor of L′/K equals the conductor of L/K, then the image of c^χ_F under H¹(F,T⊗χ) →(Res) H¹(FL′,T⊗χ) →(⊗ξ_χ^{-1}) H¹(FL′,T) is ∑_{δ∈Gal(FL′/F)} χ(δ) δ c_{FL′}.
items.note: ES.2 (twisting). Proof: Cor_{FL′/FL}c_{FL′} = c_{FL} since no new primes ramify, then Res∘Cor = ∑δ. Used for formula (4) and Proposition III.2.6.

items.name: Rank-one setting T = 𝒪_χ
items.statement: For a character χ : G_K → 𝒪^× of finite prime-to-p order, T = 𝒪_χ, W = 𝐃_χ = 𝐃 ⊗_𝒪 𝒪_χ, T* = 𝒪(1) ⊗ 𝒪_{χ^{-1}} = 𝒪_{χ^{-1}ε_cyc}. L = K̄^{ker χ}, [L:K] prime to p, Δ = Gal(L/K); for a ℤ[Δ]-module B, B^χ is the χ-component of B ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} 𝒪, and a fixed generator of 𝒪_{χ^{-1}} gives B^χ ≅ (B ⊗̂ 𝒪_{χ^{-1}})^Δ.
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4: 'For Delta finite abelian of order prime to p, construct integral character idempotents'; SelmerIwasawaCohomology L4 (Tate twists).

items.name: Vanishing of H¹(L(μ_{p^∞})/K,W) (Lemma 1.1(i))
items.statement: In the setting of §1 (χ of finite prime-to-p order, T = 𝒪_χ): if χ ≠ 1 then H¹(L(μ_{p^∞})/K, W) = 0.
items.note: ESCMC L1: 'Retain the two cohomological error lengths n_W and n_W^*; prove their vanishing in every specialization'. Proof: with Ω = L(μ_{p^∞}), inflation–restriction gives H¹(Ω/K,𝕜_ρ) = Hom(Gal(Ω/L),𝕜_ρ^Δ), zero if ρ ≢ 1 mod 𝔭, then dévissage 0→𝕜_ρ→𝐃_ρ→𝐃_ρ→0. Makes the error terms of Theorem II.2.2 vanish in III.2.3.

items.name: Vanishing of H¹(L(μ_{p^∞})/K,W*) (Lemma 1.1(ii))
items.statement: In the setting of §1: if χ is not congruent to the cyclotomic character modulo the maximal ideal of 𝒪 then H¹(L(μ_{p^∞})/K, W*) = 0.
items.note: ESCMC L1 (as for (i)); apply the argument with ρ = χ^{-1}ε_cyc.

items.name: Kummer identification H¹(F,ℤ_p(1)) = (F^×)^
items.statement: For every extension F of ℚ, Kummer theory gives H¹(F,ℤ_p(1)) = lim_← H¹(F,μ_{p^n}) = lim_← F^×/(F^×)^{p^n} = (F^×)^, the p-adic completion of F^×.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0: 'prove the tower-compatible identification H^1(F,Z_p(1)) ≃ lim_m F^×/(F^×)^(p^m)'. TauCeti has Kummer coefficient modules (TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Coefficients.lean, KummerCoeff) but not this limit identification.

items.name: Distribution relation, case ℓ | m
items.statement: Fix ζ_m primitive m-th roots of unity with ζ_{mn}^n = ζ_m. For every m ≥ 1 and prime ℓ with ℓ | m: N_{ℚ(μ_{mℓ})/ℚ(μ_m)}(ζ_{mℓ} − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ−1}(ζ_m − 1), i.e. ζ_m − 1 for ℓ odd and 1 − ζ_m for ℓ = 2 (the print omits the sign; equivalently N(1 − ζ_{mℓ}) = 1 − ζ_m for every ℓ | m).
items.note: ESCMC L0: 'Prove both the p-power norm relation and the auxiliary-prime Euler-factor relation'; IntegralIwasawaTheory L0 'norm maps on units'. Mathlib has norms of ζ−1 down to ℚ only (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/PrimitiveRoots.lean), not relative norms. Cited from [Lan] Theorem 6.3.1. Planned with the corrected sign by packet nodes EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0/distribution-relation-of-dvd and /distribution-relation-rubin-convention.

items.name: Distribution relation, case ℓ ∤ m, m > 1
items.statement: For m > 1 and a prime ℓ ∤ m: N_{ℚ(μ_{mℓ})/ℚ(μ_m)}(ζ_{mℓ} − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ−1}(ζ_m − 1)^{1 − Fr_ℓ^{-1}} (the print omits the sign, which matters only for ℓ = 2; e.g. ζ_6 − 1 = −(ζ_3 − 1)^{1−Fr_2^{-1}}), where Fr_ℓ is the Frobenius of ℓ in Gal(ℚ(μ_m)/ℚ).
items.note: ESCMC L0 (auxiliary-prime Euler-factor relation). This is the Euler-system relation with P(Fr_ℓ^{-1}|ℤ_p(1)*; x) = 1 − x.

items.name: Distribution relation, case m = 1
items.statement: For a prime ℓ: N_{ℚ(μ_ℓ)/ℚ}(ζ_ℓ − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ−1} ℓ.
items.note: Mathlib IsPrimitiveRoot.norm_sub_one_of_prime_ne_two' (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/PrimitiveRoots.lean:465): for p odd prime, Irreducible (cyclotomic p K), norm K (ζ − 1) = p, which is (−1)^{ℓ−1}ℓ for ℓ odd; the case ℓ = 2 is IsPrimitiveRoot.norm_pow_sub_one_two (PrimitiveRoots.lean:475) at k = 0, giving (−2)^1 = −2. Also IsCyclotomicExtension.norm_zeta_sub_one_of_prime_ne_two (line 564).

items.name: Cyclotomic-unit Euler system for ℤ_p(1)
items.statement: For every m ≥ 1 define c̃_{m∞} = N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})/ℚ(μ_m)}(ζ_{mp} − 1) ∈ ℚ(μ_m)^× ⊂ H¹(ℚ(μ_m),ℤ_p(1)) and c̃_m = N_{ℚ(μ_m)/ℚ(μ_m)^+}(c̃_{m∞}). The distribution relation (2) shows that {c̃_{m∞}, c̃_m} is an Euler system for (ℤ_p(1), ℚ^{ab}, p) (Definition II.1.1 and Remark II.1.3), since for every prime ℓ ≠ p, det(1 − Fr_ℓ^{-1}x | ℤ_p(1)*) = det(1 − Fr_ℓ^{-1}x | ℤ_p) = 1 − x.
items.note: ESCMC L0: 'Construct the cyclotomic example from actual norm-compatible cyclotomic p-units ... and apply the Kummer map. Prove both the p-power norm relation and the auxiliary-prime Euler-factor relation.' (The roadmap plans smoothed units; Rubin uses the unsmoothed p-units ζ_{mp}−1 normed down.) This is Kolyvagin's original Euler system ([Ko2], [Ru3]).

items.name: c̃_{m∞} when p | m (Remark 2.1)
items.statement: If p | m then c̃_{m∞} = (−1)^{p−1}(ζ_m − 1) (= ζ_m − 1 for p odd, 1 − ζ_m for p = 2; the print omits the sign). If p ∤ m, the requirement N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})/ℚ(μ_m)} c̃_{mp} = c̃_m loses information, which leads to the hypothesis χ(p) ≠ 1 in Theorem 2.3.
items.note: ESCMC L0 (p-power norm relation). Immediate from (2) with ℓ = p | m. Explains the χ(p)=1 exception handled via Theorem 2.10 (Remark 2.5).

items.name: Setting for cyclotomic units: χ even, ℚ_n, L_n
items.statement: K = ℚ, K_∞ = ℚ_∞ the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension; χ : G_ℚ → 𝒪^× of finite prime-to-p order, even and nontrivial, conductor 𝔣, viewed as a Dirichlet character mod 𝔣 (χ(q) = 0 if q | 𝔣, else χ(Fr_q)). ℚ_n ⊂ ℚ(μ_{p^{n+1}}) is the degree-p^n subextension, L_n = Lℚ_n, L_∞ = Lℚ_∞; Δ = Gal(L/ℚ) is identified with Gal(L_n/ℚ_n). T = 𝒪_χ, T* = ℤ_p(1) ⊗ χ^{-1}.
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory I.1: 'Construct the cyclotomic Z_p-extension of a number field, its finite layers'; ESCMC L0.

items.name: Restriction isomorphism (3)
items.statement: Restriction gives an isomorphism H¹(ℚ_n,T*) ≅ H¹(L_n,T*)^Δ ≅ (L_n^× ⊗̂ 𝒪_{χ^{-1}})^Δ ≅ (L_n^×)^χ ⊂ L_n^× ⊗̂ 𝒪, where ⊗̂ is the p-adically completed tensor product.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0 (Kummer) with prime-to-p descent; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4 (character idempotents).

items.name: Image of c_ℚ for the twisted cyclotomic system (4)
items.statement: The Euler system c̃ for ℤ_p(1) gives, by Proposition II.4.2, an Euler system c = c̃^{χ^{-1}} for (T*, ℚ^{ab}, p𝔣). By Lemma II.4.3 the image of c_ℚ in L^× ⊗̂ 𝒪 under (3) is ∏_{δ∈Gal(ℚ(μ_𝔣)^+/ℚ)} (δc̃_𝔣)^{χ^{-1}(δ)} = ∏_{δ∈Gal(ℚ(μ_{𝔣p})/ℚ)} (ζ_{𝔣p}^δ − 1)^{χ^{-1}(δ)}.
items.note: ESCMC L1: 'compute the resulting derivative classes' / L0 twisting via ES.2.

items.name: Selmer groups as class-group duals (5)
items.statement: With W = 𝐃_χ and H¹_f(ℚ_{n,p},V) = H¹_ur(ℚ_{n,p},V), and A_n the ideal class group of L_n (A_L = A_0): 𝒮(ℚ,W) ≅ Hom(A_L, 𝐃_χ)^Δ and 𝒮(ℚ_∞,W) ≅ Hom(lim_← A_n, 𝐃_χ)^Δ (Proposition I.6.1).
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L4: 'Recover R06's class-group and p-ramified modules from the Selmer groups of Tate twists'.

items.name: χ-cyclotomic units C_{n,χ} (Definition 2.2)
items.statement: If n ≥ 0 let E_n be the group of global units of L_n. The group of χ-cyclotomic units C_{n,χ} is the subgroup of E_n^χ generated over 𝒪[Gal(L_n/ℚ)] by ξ_{n,χ} = ∏_{δ∈Gal(ℚ(μ_𝔣)/ℚ)} (ζ_𝔣^δ − 1)^{χ^{-1}(δ)} if n = 0, and ξ_{n,χ} = ∏_{δ∈Gal(ℚ_n(μ_{𝔣p^{n+1}})/ℚ_n)} (ζ_{𝔣p^{n+1}}^δ − 1)^{χ^{-1}(δ)} if n > 0. Also E_L = E_0, C_{L,χ} = C_{0,χ}, ξ_{L,χ} = ξ_{0,χ}.
items.note: ESCMC L4: 'semilocal units over an abelian field ...; character functors ...; circular units'; IntegralIwasawaTheory L0 'Define cyclotomic units as a subgroup of actual units' (prime-power conductor). Mathlib has cyclotomic-unit lemmas (Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/CyclotomicUnits.lean) but not this group.

items.name: c_ℚ = ξ_{L,χ}^{1−χ^{-1}(p)} (6)
items.statement: Identifying ξ_{L,χ} with its image in H¹(ℚ,T*) via E_L^χ ↪ (L^×)^χ ≅ H¹(ℚ,T*), it follows from (2) and (4) that c_ℚ = ξ_{L,χ}^{1−χ^{-1}(p)}, where χ(p) = 0 if p | 𝔣. If χ(p) ≠ 1 then, as χ has order prime to p, 1 − χ^{-1}(p) ∈ 𝒪^× and c_ℚ generates C_{L,χ}.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §2.4, proof of Theorem 2.3, equation (6), p. 36
items.note: ESCMC L1 (explicit cyclotomic class computation). Remark 2.5: if χ(p) = 1 then c_ℚ = 0.

items.name: E_L^χ is free of rank one
items.statement: Since p > 2, χ is even and χ ≠ 1, the Dirichlet unit theorem shows that E_L^χ is free of rank one over 𝒪.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §2.4, proof of Theorem 2.3, p. 36
items.note: ESCMC L1 (packet node L1/chi-units-rank-one-and-index, which requests the Galois-module unit theorem from IntegralIwasawaTheory L0); Mathlib has the Dirichlet unit theorem (NumberField.Units.dirichletUnitTheorem, Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/DirichletTheorem.lean) but not the Galois-module χ-component statement.

items.name: ind_𝒪(c) = ℓ_𝒪(E_L^χ/C_{L,χ})
items.statement: Since L^×/E_L is torsion-free, ind_𝒪(c) is the largest power of 𝔭 by which a generator of C_{L,χ} can be divided in E_L^χ; hence (p > 2, χ even nontrivial, χ(p) ≠ 1) ind_𝒪(c) = ℓ_𝒪(E_L^χ/C_{L,χ}).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §2.4, proof of Theorem 2.3, p. 36
items.note: ESCMC L1: 'Use the explicit cyclotomic class index'.

items.name: Class group bounded by cyclotomic units (Theorem 2.3)
items.statement: Suppose that p > 2 and χ(p) ≠ 1 (χ even, nontrivial, of finite prime-to-p order). Then |A_L^χ| divides [E_L^χ : C_{L,χ}].
items.note: ESCMC L1: 'Apply ES.4's Poitou–Tate descent bound to the actual class-group/Selmer comparison ... Verify these hypotheses for the present cyclotomic twist.' Proof (credited to Kolyvagin [Ko2]; first proved by Mazur–Wiles): Theorem II.2.2 for T* with τ = 1, error terms zero by Lemma 1.1, ind_𝒪(c) = ℓ_𝒪(E^χ/C); H¹_ur(ℚ_p,V) = V^I/(χ(p)−1)V^I = 0 so 𝒮_{Σ_p}(ℚ,W) = 𝒮(ℚ,W) = Hom_𝒪(A_L^χ,𝐃). This is Kolyvagin's original application to ideal class groups.

items.name: Mazur–Wiles equality (Corollary 2.4)
items.statement: With hypotheses as in Theorem 2.3, |A_L^χ| = [E_L^χ : C_{L,χ}].
items.note: ESCMC L4: 'the Euler-system inequality; Kummer duality; and the analytic class-number equality' (Greither §§2–3). Proof by reference to [Ru3] Theorem 4.2: Theorem 2.3 for all such χ plus the analytic class number formula. Cited as Mazur–Wiles [MW] Theorem 1.10.1.

items.name: Case χ(p) = 1 gives c_ℚ = 0 (Remarks 2.5)
items.statement: When χ(p) = 1, (6) shows that c_ℚ = 0, so Theorem II.2.2 gives nothing; Greenberg ([Gr1] §5) deduces the equality of Corollary 2.4 from Theorem 2.10 (the main conjecture). When p divides the order of χ, Theorem II.2.2 still bounds 𝒮(ℚ,W), but this is no longer exactly the class group. Theorem II.3.3 also applies when p = 2.
items.note: ESCMC L2: 'When a character is trivial on decomposition at p, carry the augmentation corrections ...; the argument is not the finite-level theorem assuming chi(p)≠1.'

items.name: Inverse-limit modules A_∞, E_∞, C_{∞,χ}, U_∞, Y_∞, E′_∞
items.statement: Let Λ = 𝒪[[Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ)]], L_{n,p} = L_n ⊗ ℚ_p, U_n the local units of L_{n,p}. A_∞ = lim_←(A_n)^, E_∞ = lim_←(E_n)^, C_{∞,χ} = lim_←(C_{n,χ})^, U_∞ = lim_←(U_n)^, Y_∞ = lim_←(L_{n,p}^×)^, inverse limits for norm maps, ( )^ p-adic completion; E′_n the p-units of L_n and E′_∞ = lim_←(E′_n)^.
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory I.2: 'Define inverse limits of p-primary class groups, S-class groups, units, S-units'.

items.name: Units ↔ Iwasawa cohomology diagram (Proposition 2.6(i))
items.statement: With the natural horizontal inclusions and surjections, there are vertical isomorphisms making the diagram commute: Λ{c_{ℚ_n}} ↪ H¹_∞(ℚ,T*) ↪ H¹_∞(ℚ_p,T*) ↠ H¹_{∞,s}(ℚ_p,T*) over C_{∞,χ} ↪ (E′_∞)^χ ↪ Y_∞^χ ↠ Y_∞^χ/U_∞^χ.
items.note: ESCMC L2 ('verify the control maps'); SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0/L3. Proof: image of c_{ℚ_n} is ξ_{n,χ} (Lemma II.4.3); 𝒮^{{p}}(ℚ_n,T*) ≅ (E′_n)^χ; H¹_∞ = lim 𝒮^{{p}} (Corollary B.3.4); local Kummer H¹_f ↔ U_n^χ; injectivity of the middle map uses Leopoldt (known here).

items.name: Y_∞^χ/U_∞^χ (Proposition 2.6(ii))
items.statement: There is a Λ-module isomorphism Y_∞^χ/U_∞^χ ≅ 0 if χ(p) ≠ 1, and ≅ 𝒪 if χ(p) = 1.
items.note: ESCMC L2 (augmentation corrections at χ trivial on decomposition at p). Proof: L_{m,p}^×/U_m ≅ ⊕_{w|p} ℤ ≅ ℤ[Δ/Δ_p] compatibly with norms, so Y_∞^χ/U_∞^χ ≅ ℤ_p[Δ/Δ_p]^χ, nonzero iff χ(p) = 1.

items.name: (E′_∞)^χ/E_∞^χ ↪ 𝒪 (Proposition 2.6(iii))
items.statement: There is a Λ-module injection (E′_∞)^χ/E_∞^χ ↪ 𝒪.
items.note: ESCMC L2. Follows from (ii) since E_∞^χ is the kernel of (E′_∞)^χ → Y_∞^χ/U_∞^χ.

items.name: Iwasawa divisibility for class groups (Theorem 2.7)
items.statement: char(A_∞^χ) divides char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}).
items.note: ESCMC L2: 'For cyclotomic units prove Rubin III.2.7: char(Y_infty^chi) divides char(E_infty^chi/C_infty,chi)' (roadmap's Y_∞ = Rubin's A_∞, unramified module). Proof: Theorem II.3.3 + Prop II.3.7 give char(Hom(𝒮(ℚ_∞,W),𝐃)) | ind_Λ(c) char(H¹_{∞,s}); Y_∞^χ torsion-free rank one ([Iw3] Thm 25) so ind_Λ(c) = char((E′_∞)^χ/C_{∞,χ}) | J char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}); char(A_∞^χ) | J² char(E^χ/C), and J ∤ char(A_∞^χ) (sketch).

items.name: char(A_∞^χ) is prime to the augmentation ideal
items.statement: For χ even (L real abelian), with J = char(𝒪) the augmentation ideal of Λ: J does not divide char(A_∞^χ). Sketch: A_∞^χ/JA_∞^χ is finitely generated over ℤ_p, J | char(A_∞^χ) ⇔ A_∞^χ/JA_∞^χ is infinite, and A_∞^χ/JA_∞^χ = Gal(M_∞/L_∞) with M_∞/L abelian; Leopoldt holds for L so L has no ℤ_p²-extensions, Gal(M_∞/L) has ℤ_p-rank one and [M_∞:L_∞] is finite.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §2.5, proof of Theorem 2.7, p. 38
items.note: ESCMC L2: 'Use the abelian Leopoldt theorem from R06, not a new assumption'; IntegralIwasawaTheory L4 (abelian Leopoldt). Rubin says 'We only sketch the proof'.

items.name: Equality char(A_∞^χ) = char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}) (Corollary 2.8)
items.statement: char(A_∞^χ) = char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}).
items.note: ESCMC L3: 'Prove equality in the preceding divisibility by the cyclotomic-unit index/class-number argument of Rubin III.2.8'. Proof by reference ([MW] §1.6, [Ru3] p. 414).

items.name: Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-function L_χ (Theorem 2.9(i))
items.statement: Let ω be the Teichmüller character (action on μ_p, or μ_4 if p = 2); ω^{-1}ε_cyc is a character of Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ). There is L_χ ∈ Λ such that for every k ≥ 1 and every character ρ of finite order of Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ), (ω^{-1}ε_cyc)^k ρ(L_χ) = (1 − ω^{-k}ρχ(p) p^{k−1}) L(1−k, ω^{-k}ρχ).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions L2: 'For primitive eta of conductor D>1 coprime to p, construct the integral measure zeta_eta ... = (1−(chi eta)(p)p^(k−1)) L(chi eta,1−k)'; IntegralIwasawaTheory I.3. Cited ([Iw2] §6, [Wa] Thm 7.10).

items.name: Iwasawa's theorem on local units (Theorem 2.9(ii))
items.statement: char(U_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}) = L_χΛ.
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries L4: 'Conclude Theorem 12.23, including U_infty,1^+ / C_infty,1^+ ≃ Z_p[[G^+]] / (I(G^+) zeta_p)' (prime-power conductor; the general-χ case, [Gi] Théorème 1, is only in ESCMC L4's Greither route: 'the local-unit characteristic computation'). Cited, main computation in Appendix D §2.

items.name: Class-field-theory exact sequence
items.statement: With M_∞ the maximal abelian p-extension of L_∞ unramified outside primes above p and Z_∞ = Gal(M_∞/L_∞), there is an exact sequence 0 → E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ} → U_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ} → Z_∞^χ → A_∞^χ → 0.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §2.6, proof of Theorem 2.10, p. 39
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory L1: 'Prove the exact sequence 0 → E_infty^+/C_infty^+ → U_infty^+/C_infty^+ → X_infty^+ → Y_infty^+ → 0'. Cited from [dS] §III.1.7.

items.name: Iwasawa main conjecture over ℚ (Theorem 2.10)
items.statement: Let M_∞ be the maximal abelian p-extension of L_∞ unramified outside primes above p, and Z_∞ = Gal(M_∞/L_∞). Then Z_∞ is a Gal(L/ℚ)-module and a finitely generated Λ-module, and char(Z_∞^χ) = L_χΛ, where L_χ is the p-adic L-function of Theorem 2.9.
items.note: ESCMC L3: 'Deduce finite generation and torsion of X^+ and char_(Z_p[[G^+]])(X_infty^+) = I(G^+) zeta_p for every odd prime p'. Proof: exact sequence + Corollary 2.8 + Theorem 2.9(ii).

items.name: Setting T = T_p(E), Weil pairing self-duality
items.statement: For E an elliptic curve over ℚ take K = ℚ, K_∞ = ℚ_∞, 𝒪 = ℤ_p, T = T_p(E), V = V_p(E) = T_p(E) ⊗ ℚ_p, W = E_{p^∞}. The Weil pairing gives isomorphisms V ≅ V*, T ≅ T*, W ≅ W*. ℚ_n is the degree-p^n layer of ℚ_∞ and ℚ_{n,p} its completion at the unique prime above p.
items.note: TauCeti EllipticCurves Layer 2 plans 'T_ℓ E = lim E[ℓⁿ] ... the ℓ-adic Weil pairing, and the continuous Galois representation'; ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6 'Construct the inverse-limit Tate module ... Weil-pairing determinant'. Not in Mathlib/TauCeti index (no Tate module or Weil pairing declarations).

items.name: Finite local condition H¹_f(ℚ_{n,p},V)
items.statement: H¹_f(ℚ_{n,p},V) = image(E(ℚ_{n,p}) ⊗ ℚ_p ↪ H¹(ℚ_{n,p},V)); since V = V*, this also fixes H¹_f(ℚ_{n,p},V*), and these subgroups are orthogonal complements.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L4: 'define and compare finite Bloch–Kato and ordinary local conditions'; EllipticCurves Layer 7 (Kummer local conditions). Orthogonality cited from Example I.6.4.

items.name: Exponential map and formal-group diagram
items.statement: exp_E : tan(E/ℚ_{n,p}) ⥲ E(ℚ_{n,p}) ⊗ ℚ_p. With ω_E the Néron differential of a minimal Weierstrass model, cotan(E/ℚ_{n,p}) = ℚ_{n,p}ω_E and ω_E* the dual basis; there is a commutative diagram of isomorphisms tan(E/ℚ_{n,p}) ← ℚ_{n,p} (·ω_E*), ℚ_{n,p} ←(λ_E) Ê(𝔭_n) ⊗ ℚ_p ⥲ E_1(ℚ_{n,p}) ⊗ ℚ_p → E(ℚ_{n,p}) ⊗ ℚ_p, with λ_E the formal-group logarithm and Ê(𝔭_n) ≅ E_1(ℚ_{n,p}) ([T3] Theorem 4.2); λ_E is also viewed as a homomorphism E(ℚ_{n,p}) → ℚ_{n,p}.
items.note: TauCeti EllipticCurves Layer 1: '(ii) The formal logarithm and exponential ... (iv) The identification Ê(𝔪) ≅ E₁(K)'; Layer 4 'the identification Ê(𝔪) ≅ E₁(K)'. TauCeti has the formal group law (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/...) but not λ_E on points.

items.name: Dual exponential exp*_E and exp*_{ω_E}
items.statement: Since V ≅ V*, local Tate duality gives Hom(E(ℚ_{n,p}),ℚ_p) ≅ Hom(H¹_f(ℚ_{n,p},V),ℚ_p) ≅ H¹_s(ℚ_{n,p},V), and hence the dual exponential exp*_E : H¹_s(ℚ_{n,p},V) ⥲ cotan(E/ℚ_{n,p}) = ℚ_{n,p}ω_E; exp*_{ω_E} = ω_E* ∘ exp*_E : H¹_s(ℚ_{n,p},V) ⥲ ℚ_{n,p}, injective on H¹_s(ℚ_{n,p},T).
items.note: PadicHodgeRegulators L1: 'Construct the exponential and dual exponential from the fundamental exact sequences'. Cited [Ka1] §II.1.2.

items.name: Explicit identification (14)–(15)
items.statement: The local pairing identifies H¹_s(ℚ_{n,p},V) ≅ Hom(E(ℚ_{n,p}),ℚ_p) and H¹_s(ℚ_{n,p},T) ≅ Hom(E(ℚ_{n,p}),ℤ_p) compatibly; explicitly z ∈ H¹_s(ℚ_{n,p},V) corresponds to x ↦ Tr_{ℚ_{n,p}/ℚ_p} λ_E(x) exp*_{ω_E}(z).
items.note: PadicHodgeRegulators L1: 'Prove their domains, kernels, local duality relation'. Cited [Ka1] Theorem II.1.4.1(iv).

items.name: Image of the integral singular quotient under exp* (Proposition 5.1)
items.statement: For p odd (the print omits this hypothesis, PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E11): exp*_{ω_E}(H¹_s(ℚ_p,T)) = [E(ℚ_p) : E_1(ℚ_p) + E(ℚ_p)_tors] p^{-1} ℤ_p.
items.note: No atlas stage plans this integral computation (PadicHodgeRegulators L1 only constructs exp*). Proof: by (14),(15) exp*(H¹_s(ℚ_p,T)) = p^a ℤ_p where λ_E(E(ℚ_p)) = p^{-a}ℤ_p; λ_E(E_1(ℚ_p)) = pℤ_p and rank E(ℚ_p) = 1 give the index. The step λ_E(E_1(ℚ_p)) = pℤ_p needs p odd (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E11). Used in 5.11 to make H¹_s(ℚ_p,T) = p^{-1}ℤ_p when p ∤ |Ẽ(𝔽_p)|.

items.name: Hasse–Weil L-function L(E,s) (Definition 5.2)
items.statement: L(E,s) = ∑_{n≥1} a_n n^{-s} = ∏_q ℓ_q(q^{-s})^{-1}, the Hasse–Weil L-function of E, with ℓ_q(q^{-s}) the usual Euler factor at q.
items.note: Mathlib WeierstrassCurve.LFunction (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/LFunction.lean:79) is the Euler product over primes of 1/f_p(‖p‖^{-s}) with f_p = 1 − a_pT + ‖p‖T² (good), 1 − T (split), 1 + T (nonsplit), 1 (additive), as a formal Dirichlet series; WeierstrassCurve.LSeries (line 84) is the complex series. Analytic continuation (needed for s = 1) is not in the library (RankZeroOneBSD BSD.0).

items.name: Imprimitive and twisted L-functions L_m(E,s), L_m(E,χ,s) and relation (16)
items.statement: For m ∈ ℤ^+, L_m(E,s) = ∑_{(n,m)=1} a_n n^{-s} = ∏_{q∤m} ℓ_q(q^{-s})^{-1} = (∏_{q|m} ℓ_q(q^{-s})) L(E,s). For a character χ of G_ℚ of conductor f_χ, L_m(E,χ,s) = ∑_{(n,f_χ m)=1} χ(n)a_n n^{-s} = ∏_{q∤f_χ m} ℓ_q(q^{-s}χ(q))^{-1}; L(E,χ,s) is the case m = 1, and L_m(E,χ,s) = (∏_{q|m} ℓ_q(q^{-s}χ(q))) L(E,χ,s) (16). If E is modular these have analytic continuation to ℂ.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §5.3, Definition 5.2 and (16), p. 48
items.note: RankZeroOneBSD BSD.0: 'Build the interface from the Euler product/Dirichlet series of E to its modular entire continuation' (twists planned there only for quadratic characters; Dirichlet-character twists are needed for Kato's reciprocity, KatoEulerSystems L3 'corresponding complex L-values').

items.name: Conductor N and real period Ω_E
items.statement: N is the conductor of E and Ω_E the fundamental real period of E (corresponding to the choice of ω_E).
items.note: RankZeroOneBSD BSD.1: 'Use the existing Mordell–Weil lattice modulo torsion, regulator, period'; TauCeti EllipticCurves Layer 7 (BSD quotient uses Ω(E)).

items.name: Kato's Euler system and reciprocity at n = 0 (Theorem 5.3)
items.statement: (Kato) Suppose E is modular. There is a positive integer r_E, independent of p, and an Euler system c for T_p(E) such that exp*_{ω_E}(loc^s_{{p}}(c_ℚ)) = r_E L_{Np}(E,1)/Ω_E.
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L2 ('Global zeta classes ... Prove ... the p-direction norm relation and the away-from-p Euler relation') and L3 ('Explicit reciprocity'). Cited from [Ka3], [Scho] §5 (good reduction at p), [Ru9] Cor. 7.2. This replaces Kolyvagin's Heegner-point input + Gross–Zagier + BFH + Murty–Murty.

items.name: Kato's twisted reciprocity law (Theorem 5.3)
items.statement: For every n ≥ 0 and every character χ of Gal(ℚ_n/ℚ), ∑_{γ∈Gal(ℚ_n/ℚ)} χ(γ) exp*_{ω_E}(loc^s_{{p}}(c^γ_{ℚ_n})) = r_E L_{Np}(E,χ,1)/Ω_E.
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L3: 'prove the interpolation at every finite-order character'. Used in 5.11 and 5.15.

items.name: Kato: L(E,1) ≠ 0 ⇒ E(ℚ), Ш(E) finite (Theorem 5.4(i))
items.statement: Suppose E is modular and E does not have complex multiplication. If L(E,1) ≠ 0 then E(ℚ) and Ш(E) are finite.
items.note: RankZeroOneBSD BSD.4: 'Given L(E,1)≠0 ... prove rank E(ℚ)=0 ... Give a second explicitly scoped route via the actual Beilinson–Kato Euler system'. Remarks 5.5: first proved by Kolyvagin [Ko2] with Heegner points plus [GZ], [BFH], [MM]. Proof (p. 54, the end of §5.9) from 5.11 and 5.18 with Serre's theorem (Remark 5.9).

items.name: Kato: twisted finiteness (Theorem 5.4(ii))
items.statement: Suppose E is modular and does not have complex multiplication. If L is a finite abelian extension of ℚ, χ is a character of Gal(L/ℚ), and L(E,χ,1) ≠ 0, then E(L)^χ and Ш(E/L)^χ are finite.
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L4 ('Prove the analytic twist-nonvanishing ... Apply the generic bounds'). Rubin does not prove (ii) here beyond L ⊂ ℚ_∞ (needs the twisted systems of Proposition II.4.2).

items.name: Kato's system lives over ℚ^{ab,DD′} (Remarks 5.5)
items.statement: Kato's is an Euler system for (T_p(E), ℚ^{ab,DD′}, NpDD′) for appropriate auxiliary integers D, D′; hence (for suitable D, D′ depending on χ) Proposition II.4.2 gives an Euler system for T_p(E) ⊗ χ for every finite-order character χ of G_ℚ, with properties analogous to Theorem 5.3.
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L2: 'descent in the auxiliary conductor'; ES.2 twisting. The printed description of ℚ^{ab,DD′} is wrong (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E9).

items.name: E(ℚ_∞) is finitely generated (Corollary 5.6)
items.statement: Suppose E is modular and E does not have complex multiplication. Then E(ℚ_∞) is finitely generated.
items.note: No atlas stage plans this corollary. Its analytic input, Rohrlich's nonvanishing for cyclotomic twists, is planned in KatoEulerSystems L4 ('Prove the analytic twist-nonvanishing theorem required to show the localized/global class is nonzero, including the cyclotomic-family theorem used in Kato's argument'; the packet node KatoEulerSystems:L4/nonvanishing-of-the-zeta-submodule-at-height-zero states Rohrlich's theorem), and Serre's open-image input in HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.7. Proof: Rohrlich [Ro] (L(E,χ,1) ≠ 0 for almost all χ of Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ)), Serre [Se4] Théorème 3 (E(ℚ_∞)_tors finite), Theorem 5.4(ii); see [RW] pp. 242–243.

items.name: CM curves excluded from Kato's route (Remark 5.7)
items.statement: When E has complex multiplication, T_p(E) does not satisfy Hyp(ℚ,V)(i), so the results of §2 and §3 cannot be applied with Kato's Euler system; Theorem 5.4 and Corollary 5.6 are nevertheless known for CM curves via the Euler system of elliptic units ([CW], [Ru5] §11, [RW]).
items.note: HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.7s: 'The selected additional CM source is Karl Rubin, Tate-Shafarevich groups and L-functions of elliptic curves with complex multiplication ... Its elliptic-unit route is not supplied by the cyclotomic unit roadmap.' The failure of Hyp(ℚ,V)(i) for CM curves is the packet node KatoEulerSystems:L4/cm-exclusion-and-the-separate-treatment.

items.name: Hypotheses for non-CM curves (Proposition 5.8(i))
items.statement: Fix a ℤ_p-basis of T and let ρ_{E,p} : G_ℚ → Aut(T) ≅ GL_2(ℤ_p). If E has no complex multiplication, then T_p(E) satisfies Hyp(ℚ_∞,V) and H¹(ℚ(E_{p^∞})/ℚ, E_{p^∞}) is finite.
items.note: Rests on Serre's open-image theorem [Se4] Théorème 3, which HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.7 plans ('For non-CM curves prove the required open-image/cohomological bounds and their uniformity'; FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.6 avoids it); not in Mathlib/TauCeti. The verification of the hypotheses for Kato's classes is KatoEulerSystems L4 ('after verifying the representation-theoretic and local hypotheses for these actual classes'). Proof: G_{ℚ(μ_{p^∞})} = ρ^{-1}(SL_2(ℤ_p)) (Weil pairing); open image gives V irreducible over G_{ℚ_∞} and τ with ρ(τ) = (1 x; 0 1), x ≠ 0.

items.name: Hypotheses for surjective ρ_{E,p} (Proposition 5.8(ii))
items.statement: If p is odd and the p-adic representation ρ_{E,p} is surjective (the print omits 'p odd'; for p = 2 the vanishing fails, PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E10), then T_p(E) satisfies Hyp(ℚ_∞,T) and H¹(ℚ(E_{p^∞})/ℚ, E_{p^∞}) = 0.
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L4 plans this verification for Kato's classes ('after verifying the representation-theoretic and local hypotheses for these actual classes ... possible powers of p in the latter when the large-image hypothesis is unavailable'). Proof: take x = 1; H¹(GL_2(ℤ_p),(ℚ_p/ℤ_p)²) = 0. The vanishing claim fails for p = 2 (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E10); all uses in this range have p odd or do not use it.

items.name: Surjectivity for almost all p (Remark 5.9)
items.statement: If E has no complex multiplication then ρ_{E,p} is surjective for all but finitely many p (Serre [Se4], Corollaire 1 of Théorème 3).
items.note: Serre's theorem, also item PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/g-serre-open-image, planned in HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.7 ('For non-CM curves prove the required open-image/cohomological bounds'). Needed in the proof of Theorem 5.4(i) to make Ш(E)_{p^∞} = 0 for almost all p.

items.name: τ is nontrivial unipotent; CM has no such τ (Remark 5.10)
items.statement: The conditions on τ in Hyp(ℚ,V)(i) force ρ_{E,p}(τ) to be nontrivial and unipotent. Thus if E has complex multiplication there is no τ satisfying Hyp(ℚ,V)(i).
items.note: Elementary linear algebra: det ρ(τ) = ε_cyc(τ) = 1 and dim V/(τ−1)V = 1; for CM the image is (virtually) abelian torus normalizer with no nontrivial unipotents. Planned by the packet node KatoEulerSystems:L4/cm-exclusion-and-the-separate-treatment.

items.name: Finiteness from L(E,1) ≠ 0 (Theorem 5.11(i))
items.statement: Suppose E is modular, E does not have complex multiplication, and L(E,1) ≠ 0. Then E(ℚ) and Ш(E)_{p^∞} are finite.
items.note: RankZeroOneBSD BSD.4 (Kato route); ES.4 ('Finiteness at one prime ... is not full finiteness of Sha'). Proof: ℓ_q(q^{-1}) ≠ 0, so Theorem 5.3 gives loc^s_{{p}}(c_ℚ) ≠ 0; Propositions 5.8(i), 5.1 and Theorem II.2.10(i) give 𝒮(ℚ,E_{p^∞}) finite, which equals Ш(E)_{p^∞} (Proposition I.6.7).

items.name: p-part bound for Ш (Theorem 5.11(ii))
items.statement: Suppose E is modular, without complex multiplication, L(E,1) ≠ 0, E has good reduction at p, p ∤ 2r_E|Ẽ(𝔽_p)| (Ẽ the reduction of E mod p, r_E as in Theorem 5.3), and ρ_{E,p} is surjective. Then |Ш(E)_{p^∞}| divides L_N(E,1)/Ω_E.
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L4 ('Keep rational and integral statements separate ... exact integral auxiliary factors'); BSD.6 ('the upper bound from the arithmetic Euler-system argument'). Proof: exp*(H¹_s(ℚ_p,T)) = p^{-1}ℤ_p ⊃ exp*(ℤ_p loc^s(c_ℚ)) = p^{-1}(L_N(E,1)/Ω_E)ℤ_p, then Theorem II.2.10(ii) with 𝔫_W = 𝔫*_W = 0.

items.name: p·ℓ_p(p^{-1}) = |Ẽ(𝔽_p)| and the index divides it
items.statement: If E has good reduction at p then p ℓ_p(p^{-1}) = |Ẽ(𝔽_p)| and [E(ℚ_p) : E_1(ℚ_p) + E(ℚ_p)_tors] divides |Ẽ(𝔽_p)|.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §5.7, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 51
items.note: First identity: ℓ_p(X) = 1 − a_pX + pX² with a_p = p + 1 − |Ẽ(𝔽_p)| — matches Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.localPolynomial definition (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/LFunction.lean:43) but no lemma evaluates it. Second: E(ℚ_p)/E_1(ℚ_p) ≅ Ẽ(𝔽_p), TauCeti EllipticCurves Layer 4 'the exact sequence 0 → E₁(K) → E₀(K) → Ẽ_ns(k) → 0'.

items.name: Prime-to-p point counts when E(ℚ)_tors ≠ 0 (Remarks 5.12)
items.statement: |Ẽ(𝔽_p)| < 2p for all primes p > 5; hence if E(ℚ)_tors ≠ 0 then |Ẽ(𝔽_p)| is prime to p for almost all p, and Theorem 5.4(i) for such a curve follows directly from Theorem 5.11.
items.note: TauCeti EllipticCurves Layer 3 ('the Hasse bound'); first claim is Hasse |Ẽ(𝔽_p)| ≤ p + 1 + 2√p < 2p for p ≥ 7. Also remarks that Euler systems give only upper bounds; no analogue of the class number formula here.

items.name: Frobenius roots α, β and Gauss sums
items.statement: Assume E has good ordinary or multiplicative reduction at p. α ∈ ℤ_p^× and β = p/α ∈ pℤ_p are the Frobenius eigenvalues over 𝔽_p (good ordinary); (α,β) = (1,p) (split multiplicative) or (−1,−p) (nonsplit). Fix a generator {ζ_{p^n}} of lim_← μ_{p^n}; G_n = Gal(ℚ_n/ℚ) = Gal(ℚ_{n,p}/ℚ_p); for χ of conductor p^n, τ(χ) = ∑_{γ∈Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^n})/ℚ)} χ(γ)ζ_{p^n}^γ; fix ℚ̄_p ↪ ℂ.
items.note: ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2: 'construct the p-stabilizations for a nonzero root alpha'; L1 Gauss sums.

items.name: Mazur–Swinnerton-Dyer / MTT p-adic L-function (Theorem 5.13)
items.statement: Suppose E is modular and E has good ordinary reduction or multiplicative reduction at p. Then there is a nonzero integer c_E independent of p, and a p-adic L-function ℒ_E ∈ c_E^{-1}Λ such that for every character χ of Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ) of finite order, χ(ℒ_E) = (1 − α^{-1})² L(E,1)/Ω_E if χ = 1 and E has good reduction at p; = (1 − α^{-1}) L(E,1)/Ω_E if χ = 1 and E is multiplicative at p; = α^{-n} τ(χ) L(E,χ^{-1},1)/Ω_E if χ has conductor p^n > 1.
items.note: ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2 ('For h=0 prove boundedness'), L4 ('Construct weight-two examples ... and the ordinary case'). Cited [MSD], [MTT].

items.name: Imprimitive p-adic L-function ℒ_{E,m}
items.statement: For m ∈ ℤ^+, ℒ_{E,m} = (∏_{q|m, q≠p} ℓ_q(q^{-1}Fr_q^{-1})) ℒ_E ∈ c_E^{-1}Λ; by (16) and Theorem 5.13, χ(ℒ_{E,m}) is expressed through L_m(E,χ^{-1},1).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §5.8, after Theorem 5.13, p. 52
items.note: ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L4: 'primitive/imprimitive level changes and the matching of local Euler factors'.

items.name: Coleman map Col_∞ and its interpolation (Proposition 5.14)
items.statement: Suppose E has good ordinary or multiplicative reduction at p. There is a Λ-module map Col_∞ : H¹_{∞,s}(ℚ_p,T) ↪ Λ such that for every z = {z_n} ∈ H¹_{∞,s}(ℚ_p,T) and every nontrivial character χ of G_n, χ(Col_∞(z)) = α^{-k} τ(χ) ∑_{γ∈G_n} χ^{-1}(γ) exp*_{ω_E}(z_n^γ), where p^k is the conductor of χ; and for the trivial character χ_0, χ_0(Col_∞(z)) = (1 − α^{-1})(1 − β^{-1})^{-1} exp*_{ω_E}(z_0).
items.note: PadicHodgeRegulators L3: 'construct L_V : H^1_Iw(Q_p,V) → H(G) ⊗ D_cris(V) ... prove the interpolation at every finite-order character'. Proof by reference (Coleman [Co], [Ru9] appendix, Perrin-Riou [PR2]).

items.name: Split multiplicative case: image in augmentation ideal
items.statement: If E has split multiplicative reduction at p then the image of Col_∞ is contained in the augmentation ideal of Λ.
items.note: Exceptional-zero behaviour; PadicHodgeRegulators L3/L4 treat crystalline and 'noncrystalline extensions' but no stage states this. Consistent with χ_0 formula at α = 1.

items.name: Kato's reciprocity law via Col_∞ (Corollary 5.15)
items.statement: With hypotheses and notation as in Theorems 5.3 and 5.13, Col_∞(loc^s_{{p}}({c_{ℚ_n}})) = r_E ℒ_{E,N}.
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L3: 'The endpoint is the properly normalized version of L_p^an(f,alpha) = projection_alpha(L_(V_f)(loc_p z_Kato(f)))'. Proof: compare χ-values using (16), 5.3, 5.13, 5.14 and ℓ_p(p^{-1}) = (1 − α^{-1})(1 − β^{-1}) (good) resp. (1 − β^{-1}) (multiplicative).

items.name: Z_∞ = Hom(𝒮(ℚ_∞,E_{p^∞}),ℚ_p/ℤ_p)
items.statement: Z_∞ = Hom(𝒮(ℚ_∞,E_{p^∞}), ℚ_p/ℤ_p), the Pontryagin dual of the Selmer group over ℚ_∞.
items.note: ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L0: 'Define the ordinary Greenberg Selmer group ... Its dual X is compact'.

items.name: Kato's divisibility up to p^t (Theorem 5.16)
items.statement: Suppose E is modular, E does not have complex multiplication, and E has good ordinary reduction or nonsplit multiplicative reduction at p. Then Z_∞ is a finitely generated torsion Λ-module and there is an integer t such that char(Z_∞) divides p^t ℒ_{E,N}Λ.
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L4: 'Deduce the standard cohomological divisibility and the ordinary Selmer divisibility'. Proof: Rohrlich [Ro] (ℒ_E ≠ 0), Propositions 5.8, 5.14, Corollary 5.15, Theorem II.3.8.

items.name: Integral divisibility under large image (Theorem 5.16)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 5.16, if ρ_{E,p} is surjective and p ∤ r_E ∏_{q|N, q≠p} ℓ_q(q^{-1}), then char(Z_∞) divides ℒ_EΛ.
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L4 ('possible powers of p in the latter when the large-image hypothesis is unavailable').

items.name: Split multiplicative case (Theorem 5.16)
items.statement: If E is modular, non-CM, with split multiplicative reduction at p, the conclusions of Theorem 5.16 hold with char(Z_∞) replaced by J·char(Z_∞), J the augmentation ideal of Λ.
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L4; exceptional-zero corrections also SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 ('exceptional-zero situations retain the correction complexes').

items.name: No nonzero finite submodules in Z_∞ (Corollary 5.17, Greenberg)
items.statement: Let E be as in Theorem 5.16. If p is a prime where E has good ordinary reduction and p ∤ ∏_{q|N} |E(ℚ_q)_tors|, then Z_∞ has no nonzero finite submodules.
items.note: Due to Greenberg [Gr2], [Gr3]; only sketched. No atlas stage plans absence of finite submodules for elliptic Selmer duals (IntegralIwasawaTheory I.2 mentions 'finite submodules' for class-group modules only). Sketch: exact sequence (17) 0 → 𝒮(ℚ_∞,E_{p^∞}) → H¹(ℚ_Σ/ℚ_∞,E_{p^∞}) → ⊕ H¹_s; H¹(ℚ_{∞,v},E_{p^∞}) = 0 at q ≠ p; lim_← E(ℚ_{n,p}) ⊗ ℤ_p = lim_← Ê(𝔭_n) free of rank one over Λ; [Gr2] Props 3–5 and Lemma p. 123. The sketch does not treat the real places of Q_∞ when p = 2 (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E12).

items.name: p-part of BSD upper bound (Corollary 5.18)
items.statement: Suppose E is modular, E does not have complex multiplication, E has good reduction at p, p ∤ 2r_E ∏_{q|N} ℓ_q(q^{-1})|E(ℚ_q)_tors| (r_E as in Theorem 5.3), and ρ_{E,p} is surjective. Then |Ш(E)_{p^∞}| divides L(E,1)/Ω_E.
items.note: Proof on p. 54 (the end of §5.9): supersingular case from 5.11(ii); ordinary case from 5.16, 5.17 and descent/control ([PR1] §6, [Schn] §2). BSD.6 plans prime-part formulas only for named JSW/Skinner–Urban branches ('These are named branches, not a universal good-prime formula'); KatoEulerSystems L4 stops at the characteristic-ideal divisibility; the descent from Z_∞ to ℚ (the control step in the proof, recorded as its own item) is planned only generically in SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 ('Prove control statements with explicit kernels/cokernels'), and no stage states this corollary. With 5.11 and Remark 5.9 gives Theorem 5.4(i).

items.name: Auxiliary fields K(𝔮), K(1), Γ_𝔮
items.statement: For a prime 𝔮 of K not dividing p, K(𝔮) is the maximal p-extension of K inside the ray class field of K modulo 𝔮, and K(1) the maximal p-extension of K inside the Hilbert class field. K(𝔮)/K(1) is unramified outside 𝔮, totally ramified above 𝔮, and cyclic with Galois group equal to the maximal p-quotient of (𝒪_K/𝔮)^×/(𝒪_K^× (mod 𝔮)). Γ_𝔮 = Gal(K(𝔮)/K(1)).
items.note: ES.1 plans: "Construct the ray-class extensions K(q), their selected local cyclic quotients and the squarefree-conductor category." The class-field-theory facts (ramification, cyclicity, Galois group) are quoted from class field theory without proof. Tau Ceti has ideal-theoretic ray class groups (TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.RayClassGroup, TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/Basic.lean) but not the ray class fields, so the statement is not in the library.

items.name: Modulus set 𝓡(𝒩), fields K(𝔯), Γ_𝔯 ≅ ∏Γ_𝔮
items.statement: Fix an ideal 𝒩 of K divisible by p and by all primes where T is ramified. 𝓡 = 𝓡(𝒩) = {squarefree products of primes 𝔮 of K, 𝔮 ∤ 𝒩}. For 𝔯 = 𝔮_1⋯𝔮_k ∈ 𝓡, K(𝔯) = K(𝔮_1)⋯K(𝔮_k) (contained in, but not in general equal to, the maximal p-extension of K in the ray class field modulo 𝔯), Γ_𝔯 = Gal(K(𝔯)/K(1)). The fields K(𝔮) are linearly disjoint over K(1), so Γ_𝔯 ≅ ∏_{𝔮|𝔯} Γ_𝔮 with Γ_𝔮 identified with the inertia group of 𝔮 in Γ_𝔯; for 𝔰 | 𝔯, Γ_𝔰 is both a subgroup and a quotient of Γ_𝔯.
items.note: ES.1 plans: "Construct the ray-class extensions K(q), their selected local cyclic quotients and the squarefree-conductor category." Linear disjointness is justified only by 'ramification considerations'.

items.name: F(𝔯) and Γ_{F(𝔯)} ≅ Γ_{F(1)} × Γ_𝔯
items.statement: Fix a Z_p^d-extension K_∞/K in which no finite prime splits completely (Definition II.1.1). For K ⊂ F ⊂ K_∞ let F(𝔯) = FK(𝔯), and for K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞ let Γ_{F(𝔯)} = Gal(F(𝔯)/K(1)). Identifying Γ_𝔯 with the subgroup generated by the inertia groups of primes dividing 𝔯 and Γ_{F(1)} with that generated by inertia groups of primes above p (K_∞/K being unramified outside p), Γ_{F(𝔯)} ≅ Γ_{F(1)} × Γ_𝔯; for 𝔰 | 𝔯, Γ_{F(𝔰)} is identified with a subgroup of Γ_{F(𝔯)}.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. IV §1, unnumbered (with Figure 1), p. 56
items.note: Bookkeeping of the tower F(𝔯)/F(1)/K(1) used throughout Ch. IV; no atlas stage describes the Z_p^d-direction compositum F(𝔯).

items.name: Norm elements N_𝔯
items.statement: For 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, N_𝔯 = Σ_{σ∈Γ_𝔯} σ ∈ Z[Γ_𝔯] ⊂ Z[Gal(K(𝔯)/K)]. If 𝔰 | 𝔯 and K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, viewing N_𝔰 ∈ Z[Γ_𝔯] ⊂ Z[Gal(F(𝔯)/K)], one has N_𝔯 = N_𝔰 N_{𝔯/𝔰}.
items.note: ES.3 plans: "Construct the cyclic group-ring norm N_q and derivative D_q ... and prove the product/augmentation identities for squarefree conductors."

items.name: Euler factor P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;x)
items.statement: Fr_𝔮 denotes a Frobenius of 𝔮 in G_K and P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;x) = det(1 − Fr_𝔮^{-1}x | T*) ∈ 𝒪[x].
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. IV §1, unnumbered (recalled from Ch. II), p. 56
items.note: ES.2 plans: "Construct the normalization dictionary between arithmetic/geometric Frobenius and the Tate-dual convention."

items.name: Kolyvagin moduli 𝓡_{F,M}
items.statement: If K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞ and M ∈ 𝒪 is nonzero, 𝓡_{F,M} = {𝔯 ∈ 𝓡 : for every prime 𝔮 dividing 𝔯, M | [K(𝔮):K(1)], M | P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;1), and 𝔮 splits completely in F(1)/K}. M̄ ∈ Z^+ denotes the smallest power of p divisible by M (Definition I.4.6).
items.note: ES.1 plans: "Construct the ray-class extensions K(q), their selected local cyclic quotients and the squarefree-conductor category." 𝓡_{F,M} is Rubin's squarefree-conductor set at level M; its defining divisibilities are what make Lemma 4.2 work.

items.name: Lemma 1.2(i): M | [K(𝔮):K(1)] criterion
items.statement: Suppose 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡 is a prime of K. Then M | [K(𝔮):K(1)] if and only if 𝔮 splits completely in K(μ_M̄, (𝒪_K^×)^{1/M̄}).
items.note: Proof: class field theory identifies Gal(K(𝔮)/K(1)) with the p-part of (𝒪_K/𝔮)^×/(𝒪_K^× mod 𝔮) (cyclic), so the divisibility is equivalent to Fr_𝔮 fixing μ_M̄ and (𝒪_K^×)^{1/M̄}. Used in Lemma 1.3 and Definition 5.3 (via Lemma I.4.7).

items.name: Lemma 1.2(ii): P(Fr^{-1}|T*;N(𝔮)Fr^{-1}) kills T
items.statement: Suppose 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡 is a prime of K. Then P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*; N(𝔮)Fr_𝔮^{-1}) annihilates T.
items.note: Proof: P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;x) = det(1 − Fr_𝔮^{-1}x|T*) = det(1 − N(𝔮)^{-1}Fr_𝔮 x|T) and Cayley–Hamilton (Mathlib has Cayley–Hamilton, e.g. Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly, but not this statement). Used in Corollary 8.1.

items.name: Lemma 1.2(iii): P ≡ det(1 − Fr x|W_M) mod M
items.statement: Suppose 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡 is a prime of K. If M | [K(𝔮):K(1)] then P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;x) ≡ det(1 − Fr_𝔮 x|W_M) (mod M).
items.note: Uses N(𝔮) ≡ 1 mod M (since [K(𝔮):K(1)] | N(𝔮) − 1). Used in Lemma 1.3 and Corollary 5.5.

items.name: Lemma 1.2(iv): P(Fr^{-1}|T*;Fr^{-1}) kills W_M
items.statement: Suppose 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡 is a prime of K. If M | [K(𝔮):K(1)] then P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*; Fr_𝔮^{-1}) annihilates W_M.
items.note: Cayley–Hamilton modulo M. Used in Definition 5.3 (to define Q_𝔮(Fr_𝔮^{-1})), Lemma 7.3 and the proof of Theorem 5.4.

items.name: Lemma 1.3: Frobenius criterion for 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M}
items.statement: Suppose τ ∈ G_{K_∞(1)} acts trivially on μ_{p^∞} and on (𝒪_K^×)^{1/p^∞}, and T^{τ=1} ≠ 0. Suppose further that K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, M ∈ 𝒪 is nonzero, and 𝔮 is a prime of K not dividing 𝒩 such that the Frobenius Fr_𝔮 of 𝔮 is equal to (a conjugate of) τ on F(1)(μ_M̄, (𝒪_K^×)^{1/M̄}, W_M). Then 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M}.
items.note: ES.1 plans: "Use upstream Chebotarev on the finite extensions cut out jointly by T modulo powers and a finite collection of cohomology classes ... the supply of core vertices". Together with Chebotarev this gives the large supply of primes in 𝓡_{F,M} used in Ch. V; proof via Lemma 1.2(i),(iii).

items.name: Definition 2.1: the modules X_{F(𝔯)}
items.statement: For every 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡 and K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞ let x_{F(𝔯)} be an indeterminate. X_{F(𝔯)} = Y_{F(𝔯)}/Z_{F(𝔯)}, where Y_{F(𝔯)} is the free 𝒪[Gal(F(𝔯)/K)]-module on {x_{F(𝔰)} : 𝔰 | 𝔯} and Z_{F(𝔯)} is generated by σx_{F(𝔰)} − x_{F(𝔰)} (σ ∈ Gal(F(𝔯)/F(𝔰)) = Γ_{𝔯/𝔰}); N_𝔮 x_{F(𝔮𝔰)} − P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;Fr_𝔮^{-1}) x_{F(𝔰)} (𝔮 prime, 𝔮𝔰 | 𝔯, K(𝔮) ≠ K(1)); x_{F(𝔮𝔰)} − x_{F(𝔰)} (𝔮 prime, 𝔮𝔰 | 𝔯, K(𝔮) = K(1)). For 𝔰 | 𝔯 and K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F' ⊂ K_∞ there are natural maps (1) X_{F'(𝔯)} → X_{F(𝔯)}, x_{F'(𝔱)} ↦ x_{F(𝔱)} (surjective), and (2) X_{F(𝔰)} → X_{F'(𝔯)}, x_{F(𝔱)} ↦ N_{F'(𝔯)/F(𝔯)} x_{F'(𝔱)}.
items.note: The presentation of the "free" Euler system. ES.2 plans the module of compatible classes "as an equalizer/submodule" and a "conductor-indexed presentation", which is a different object (the target, not the universal source), so not counted as planned. Note that 𝔮 ramifies in F(𝔯)/K iff p divides the ramification degree of 𝔮 in the ray class field mod 𝔮.

items.name: Definition 2.2: universal Euler system
items.statement: The universal Euler system for (T, 𝒩, K_∞/K) is 𝐗 = 𝐗(T,𝒩,K_∞/K) = lim→_{F,𝔯} X_{F(𝔯)}. Also X_{∞,𝔯} = lim←_{K⊂_f F⊂K_∞} X_{F(𝔯)} (via maps (1)) and X_{∞,𝓡} = lim→_{𝔯∈𝓡} X_{∞,𝔯}; and H^1_∞(K(𝔯),T) = lim←_{K⊂_f F⊂K_∞} H^1(F(𝔯),T).
items.note: Rubin's device for making the derivative construction canonical when W^{G_{F(𝔯)}} ≠ 0 (Remark 4.3). H^1_∞ is Iwasawa cohomology along K_∞/K (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 plans H^i_Iw generally, not this object).

items.name: Lemma 2.3: Euler systems are images of the universal one
items.statement: If 𝐜 is an Euler system for (T, 𝒦, 𝒩) with K_∞ ⊂ 𝒦, then sending x_{F(𝔯)} to 𝐜_{F(𝔯)} induces G_K-equivariant maps X_{F(𝔯)} → H^1(F(𝔯),T), X_{∞,𝔯} → H^1_∞(K(𝔯),T), 𝐗 → lim→_{F,𝔯} H^1(F(𝔯),T), X_{∞,𝓡} → lim→_{𝔯∈𝓡} H^1_∞(K(𝔯),T) (direct limits with respect to restriction maps).
items.note: Immediate from Definition II.1.1: the classes satisfy the defining relations. Used to define the map 𝐜 : X_{F(𝔯)} → H^1(F(𝔯),W_M) lifted in Proposition 4.8.

items.name: Remark 2.4: converse
items.statement: Conversely, a map X_{∞,𝓡} → lim→_{𝔯∈𝓡} H^1_∞(K(𝔯),T) induces an Euler system for (T, 𝒦_min, 𝒩), where 𝒦_min is as in Remark II.1.4.
items.note: Stated without proof as following from Lemma 2.5; not used later.

items.name: Lemma 2.5(i): invariants do not grow in F(𝔯)/F(1)
items.statement: If K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞ and 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, then T^{G_{F(𝔯)}} = T^{G_{F(1)}} and W^{G_{F(𝔯)}} = W^{G_{F(1)}}.
items.note: Gal(F(𝔯)/F(1)) = Γ_𝔯 is generated by inertia groups at primes dividing 𝔯, where T is unramified.

items.name: Lemma 2.5(ii): H^1_∞(K(𝔯),T) ≅ H^1_∞(K(𝔯𝔰),T)^{Γ_𝔰}
items.statement: If 𝔯𝔰 ∈ 𝓡 then the restriction map induces an isomorphism H^1_∞(K(𝔯),T) ≅ H^1_∞(K(𝔯𝔰),T)^{Γ_𝔰}.
items.note: Proof by inflation–restriction over K_S (Propositions B.2.5(ii), B.2.7(i)), Corollary B.3.5, the hypothesis that every finite prime has infinite decomposition group in K_∞/K, and Lemma B.3.2 to kill lim← of the H^2 terms. (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E14).

items.name: Proposition 3.1(i): X_{F(𝔯)} free over 𝒪
items.statement: Suppose 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, 𝔰 | 𝔯, and K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F' ⊂ K_∞. X_{F(𝔯)} is a finitely generated, free 𝒪-module.
items.note: Proof constructs the explicit 𝒪-basis B_{F(𝔯)} = ∪_{𝔰|𝔯} A_{F,𝔰} x_{F(𝔰)} with A_{F,𝔰} = Gal(F(𝔯)/K(𝔯)) A_1 ∏_{𝔮|𝔰}(Γ_𝔮 − {1}), and the map φ: X_{F(𝔯)}⊗Φ → Φ[Gal(F(𝔯)/K)], x_{F(𝔰)} ↦ ∏_{𝔮|(𝔯/𝔰)} N_𝔮 ∏_{𝔮|𝔰}(|Γ_𝔮| + (P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;Fr_𝔮^{-1}) − |Γ_𝔮|)N_𝔮/|Γ_𝔮|), shown to be an isomorphism by evaluating characters.

items.name: Proposition 3.1(ii): X_{F(𝔯)}⊗Φ free of rank one
items.statement: Suppose 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡 and K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞. X_{F(𝔯)} ⊗ Φ is a free, rank-one module over Φ[Gal(F(𝔯)/K)], where Φ is the field of fractions of 𝒪.
items.note: Via the isomorphism φ in the proof of (i).

items.name: Proposition 3.1(iii): free over 𝒪[Gal(F(𝔯)/K(𝔯))]
items.statement: Suppose 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡 and K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞. X_{F(𝔯)} is a free 𝒪[Gal(F(𝔯)/K(𝔯))]-module of rank [K(𝔯):K].
items.note: Gal(F(𝔯)/K(𝔯)) permutes the basis B_{F(𝔯)} freely. Feeds Corollary 3.2 and Proposition 3.4.

items.name: Proposition 3.1(iv): base change along (1)
items.statement: Suppose 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡 and K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F' ⊂ K_∞. The map (1) induces an isomorphism X_{F'(𝔯)} ⊗_{𝒪[Gal(F'(𝔯)/K)]} 𝒪[Gal(F(𝔯)/K)] ≅ X_{F(𝔯)}.
items.note: Surjective by construction, injective by rank count from (iii).

items.name: Proposition 3.1(v): invariants along (2)
items.statement: Suppose 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, 𝔰 | 𝔯 and K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F' ⊂ K_∞. The map (2) induces an isomorphism X_{F(𝔰)} ≅ X_{F'(𝔯)}^{Gal(F'(𝔯)/F(𝔰))}.
items.note: Uses B_{F(𝔰)} ⊂ B_{F(𝔯)} (torsion-free cokernel) and finiteness from (ii).

items.name: Corollary 3.2: X_{∞,𝔯} free over 𝒪[[Γ]]
items.statement: If Γ = Gal(K_∞(𝔯)/K(𝔯)) then X_{∞,𝔯} is a free 𝒪[[Γ]]-module of rank [K(𝔯):K] and for every K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, X_{∞,𝔯} ⊗_{𝒪[[Gal(K_∞(𝔯)/K)]]} 𝒪[Gal(F(𝔯)/K)] ≅ X_{F(𝔯)}.
items.note: From Proposition 3.1(iii),(iv); here 𝒪[[G]] = lim←_U 𝒪[G/U]. Used in Propositions 3.4(ii), 4.8, 6.8.

items.name: Lemma 3.3(i): Hom into R[[G]] vs R[[H]]
items.statement: Suppose R is a ring, G is a profinite abelian group, and H is a subgroup of finite index in G. Suppose B is an R[[G]]-module. Then Hom_{R[[G]]}(B, R[[G]]) ≅ Hom_{R[[H]]}(B, R[[H]]) as R[[H]]-modules.
items.note: Composition with the coefficient-of-1 projection π: R[[G]] → R[[H]] relative to a coset basis C ∋ 1. Tau Ceti/Mathlib have finite-group coinduction (Rep.indCoindIso) but not this completed-group-ring statement.

items.name: Lemma 3.3(ii): Ext^1 vanishing
items.statement: With R, G, H, B as in Lemma 3.3: if B is free as an R[[H]]-module then Ext^1_{R[[G]]}(B, R[[G]]) = 0.
items.note: Deduced from (i) as Ext^1_{R[[G]]}(B,R[[G]]) = Ext^1_{R[[H]]}(B,R[[H]]).

items.name: Proposition 3.4(i): Ext^1 vanishing at finite level
items.statement: Suppose 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, k ≥ 0, and M ∈ 𝒪 is nonzero. If K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞ and G = Gal(F(𝔯)/K), then Ext^1_{(𝒪/M𝒪)[G]}(X_{F(𝔯)}/MX_{F(𝔯)}, (𝒪/M𝒪)[G]^k) = 0.
items.note: Lemma 3.3(ii) with H = {1}. Remark 3.5: alternatively because (𝒪/M𝒪)[G] is self-injective for finite G. Tau Ceti's TauCeti/Algebra/Module/Injective/SelfInjective.lean proves self-injectivity only for algebras over a field with an associative perfect form (Function.Bijective.moduleInjective_self), not over 𝒪/M𝒪. PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L6 plans, for a Gorenstein commutative O-order R, that 'for a nonzero element of O ... the appropriate Artinian quotient is self-injective'; O[G] for finite abelian G is such an order, so the Remark 3.5 route could be imported from L6 once O[G] is shown Gorenstein there. L6 does not name group rings, so the status stays missing.

items.name: Proposition 3.4(ii): Ext^1 vanishing in the limit
items.statement: Suppose 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, k ≥ 0, and M ∈ 𝒪 is nonzero. If G = Gal(K_∞(𝔯)/K), then Ext^1_{(𝒪/M𝒪)[[G]]}(X_{∞,𝔯}/MX_{∞,𝔯}, (𝒪/M𝒪)[[G]]^k) = 0.
items.note: Lemma 3.3(ii) with H = Gal(K_∞(𝔯)/K(𝔯)) and Corollary 3.2. This is the input that makes the lift d_∞ in Proposition 4.8 exist when W_M^{G_{F(1)}} ≠ 0.

items.name: Remark 3.5: self-injectivity only at finite level
items.statement: (𝒪/M𝒪)[G] is injective as a module over itself when G is finite (giving Proposition 3.4(i) directly); this is not true for (𝒪/M𝒪)[[Gal(K_∞(𝔯)/K)]].
items.note: Explains why the universal Euler system and Lemma 3.3 are needed for the limit version.

items.name: Definition 4.1: generator σ_𝔮 of Γ_𝔮
items.statement: Fix a generator ξ of lim← μ_{p^n}, and for every prime 𝔮 of K not dividing p fix a prime 𝔔 of K̄ above 𝔮. Let I_𝔔 be the inertia group of 𝔔 in G_K and M = |Γ_𝔮| = [K(𝔮):K(1)]. Since M is a power of p prime to 𝔮, I_𝔔 has a unique cyclic quotient of order M, canonically ≅ μ_M (Lemma I.4.5); Γ_𝔮 is a cyclic quotient of I_𝔔, so Γ_𝔮 ≅ μ_M, and σ_𝔮 ∈ Γ_𝔮 is the generator corresponding to the generator ζ of μ_M given by ξ.
items.note: ES.1 plans: "Construct the finite–singular comparison including its cyclic-group tensor factor; prove independence of a chosen generator after that factor is retained." Rubin fixes the generator via ξ and suppresses the dependence on 𝔔 and ξ.

items.name: Definition 4.1: Kolyvagin derivative operators D_𝔮, D_𝔯
items.statement: For every prime 𝔮 not dividing p, D_𝔮 = Σ_{i=0}^{|Γ_𝔮|−1} iσ_𝔮^i ∈ Z[Γ_𝔮]. If 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, viewing D_𝔮 ∈ Z[Γ_𝔯] for 𝔮 | 𝔯, D_𝔯 = ∏_{primes 𝔮|𝔯} D_𝔮 ∈ Z[Γ_𝔯].
items.note: ES.3 plans: "Construct the cyclic group-ring norm N_q and derivative D_q".

items.name: Identity (4): (σ_𝔮 − 1)D_𝔮 = |Γ_𝔮| − N_𝔮
items.statement: In Z[Γ_𝔮], (σ_𝔮 − 1)D_𝔮 = |Γ_𝔮| − N_𝔮.
items.note: ES.3 plans: "prove (sigma_q−1)D_q=|G_q|−N_q". The key step of Lemma 4.2.

items.name: Lemma 4.2: D_𝔯 x_{F(𝔯)} is invariant mod M
items.statement: Suppose K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, M ∈ 𝒪 is nonzero, and 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M}. If N_{F(1)/F} ∈ Z[Gal(F(𝔯)/F)] is an element whose restriction to Z[Gal(F(1)/F)] is Σ_{γ∈Gal(F(1)/F)} γ, then N_{F(1)/F} D_𝔯 x_{F(𝔯)} ∈ (X_{F(𝔯)}/MX_{F(𝔯)})^{Gal(F(𝔯)/F)}. Further, N_{F(1)/F} D_𝔯 x_{F(𝔯)} is independent of the choice of N_{F(1)/F}.
items.note: ES.3 plans: "Establish invariance of the derivative class". Proof: (σ − 1)D_𝔯 x_{F(𝔯)} ∈ MX_{F(𝔯)} for σ ∈ Gal(F(𝔯)/F(1)), by induction on the number of primes using (4), the relation N_𝔮 x_{F(𝔯)} = P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;Fr_𝔮^{-1})x_{F(𝔰)} and the divisibilities in 𝓡_{F,M}.

items.name: Remark 4.3: descent when W^{G_{F(𝔯)}} = 0
items.statement: By Lemma 4.2 (and Lemma 2.3) the image of N_{F(1)/F} D_𝔯 𝐜_{F(𝔯)} in H^1(F(𝔯),W_M) is fixed by Gal(F(𝔯)/F). If W^{G_{F(𝔯)}} = 0 then the restriction map H^1(F,W_M) → H^1(F(𝔯),W_M)^{Gal(F(𝔯)/F)} (5) is an isomorphism, and κ_{F,𝔯,M} is the inverse image of N_{F(1)/F} D_𝔯 𝐜_{F(𝔯)}; when W^{G_{F(𝔯)}} ≠ 0 the map (5) need not be an isomorphism.
items.note: ES.3 plans: "the exact restriction/descent statement, including kernel or cokernel errors when invariants do not vanish". Rubin avoids error terms by the universal Euler system (Definition 4.10).

items.name: Definition 4.4: induced module 𝕎_M
items.statement: 𝕎_M = Ind(W_M) = Maps(G_K, W_M), the continuous maps (not necessarily homomorphisms) from G_K to W_M, with G_K acting by (γf)(g) = f(gγ) for all γ, g ∈ G_K. W_M ↪ 𝕎_M via t ↦ (g ↦ gt), and W_M is identified with a submodule of 𝕎_M.
items.note: TauCeti.coind G U A (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Coinduced.lean:82) is the locally constant maps f : G → A with f(u*g) = u•f(g), with right-translation action (g•f)(x) = f(x*g) (instSMulCoind, line 128; coind_smul_apply, line 132); for U = ⊥ it is all locally constant maps (mem_coind_bot_iff, line 467). For discrete W_M, continuous = locally constant, so coind G_K ⊥ W_M is Rubin's 𝕎_M. The embedding t ↦ (g ↦ gt) was not found as a named declaration. Planned in the ProfiniteCohomology roadmap Layer 7: "Coind_H^G A is the locally constant H-equivariant maps G → A ... with the right-translation action".

items.name: Proposition 4.5(i): δ_L exact sequence
items.statement: For every 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡 and every L with K ⊂_f L ⊂ K_∞(𝔯) there is a canonical map δ_L : (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_L} → H^1(L,W_M) such that there is an exact sequence 0 → W_M^{G_L} → 𝕎_M^{G_L} → (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_L} →δ_L H^1(L,W_M) → 0.
items.note: G_L-cohomology of 0 → W_M → 𝕎_M → 𝕎_M/W_M → 0 with H^1(L,𝕎_M) = 0 (Proposition B.4.5). Tau Ceti has Shapiro in degree 1 for coinduced modules (TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitShapiro1, ContCohomology/Shapiro.lean:372, H^1(G, Coind_U^G A) ≃ H^1(U,A)), which gives the vanishing for G = G_K, but not for the restriction of Coind_1^{G_K} to an open G_L, so the statement itself is not in the library. The rest of the sequence is library: exactness at the three H⁰ terms and at H¹(A) is TauCeti.ContCohomology.DiscreteShortExact.explicitLongExact_H0A/H0B/H0C/H1A (LongExact.lean:145–294); only H¹(G_L, 𝕎_M) = 0 for L ≠ K (𝕎_M restricted to G_L is a finite sum of Coind_1^{G_L}(W_M)) is missing.

items.name: Proposition 4.5(ii): cocycle for δ_L
items.statement: If f ∈ (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_L} and f̂ ∈ 𝕎_M lifts f, then δ_L(f) is represented by the cocycle γ ↦ (γ − 1)f̂ ∈ W_M for γ ∈ G_L.
items.note: Standard connecting-map computation; in Tau Ceti as the general theorem TauCeti.ContCohomology.DiscreteShortExact.explicitDelta0_apply (ContCohomology/ShortExact.lean:550) for any DiscreteShortExact sequence of discrete G-modules. The only glue is packaging 0 → W_M → 𝕎_M → 𝕎_M/W_M → 0 as a DiscreteShortExact over G_L (the embedding t ↦ (g ↦ gt) is not a named declaration). Used in Lemma 4.12, Lemma 7.1 and Corollary 8.1.

items.name: Proposition 4.5(iii): δ compatible with Res and Cor
items.statement: If K ⊂_f L ⊂_f L' ⊂ K_∞(𝔯) then the inclusion (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_L} → (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_{L'}} and the norm N_{L'/L} : (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_{L'}} → (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_L} are compatible via δ_L, δ_{L'} with Res_{L'} : H^1(L,W_M) → H^1(L',W_M) and Cor_{L'/L} : H^1(L',W_M) → H^1(L,W_M).
items.note: Proposition B.4.5. In Tau Ceti as general theorems: TauCeti.ContCohomology.DiscreteShortExact.explicitDelta0_res and explicitCor_delta0, with the degree-0 corestriction explicitCor0 the norm (coe_explicitCor0); only the packaging of 0 → W_M → 𝕎_M → 𝕎_M/W_M → 0 as a DiscreteShortExact is glue. Used to take inverse limits in Proposition 4.7 and in Definition 4.10.

items.name: Lemma 4.6(i): 𝕎_M^{G_{F(𝔯)}} free
items.statement: Let d = rank_𝒪(T), and suppose 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡. For every K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, 𝕎_M^{G_{F(𝔯)}} is a free (𝒪/M𝒪)[Gal(F(𝔯)/K)]-module of rank d.
items.note: 𝕎_M^{G_{F(𝔯)}} = Maps(Gal(F(𝔯)/K),W_M) = Hom_𝒪(𝒪[Gal(F(𝔯)/K)],𝒪/M𝒪) ⊗ W'_M.

items.name: Lemma 4.6(ii): lim← 𝕎_M^{G_{F(𝔯)}} free over Λ_𝔯/M
items.statement: Let d = rank_𝒪(T), 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡 and Λ_𝔯 = 𝒪[[Gal(K_∞(𝔯)/K)]]. Then lim←_F 𝕎_M^{G_{F(𝔯)}} (inverse limit with respect to the norm maps) is a free Λ_𝔯/MΛ_𝔯-module of rank d, and if K ⊂_f F' ⊂ K_∞, lim←_F 𝕎_M^{G_{F(𝔯)}} ⊗_{Λ_𝔯} 𝒪[Gal(F'(𝔯)/K)] ≅ 𝕎_M^{G_{F'(𝔯)}}.
items.note: Same computation as (i) in the limit.

items.name: Proposition 4.7: short exact sequence in the limit
items.statement: Suppose 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡. Then the maps δ_{F(𝔯)} of Proposition 4.5 induce an exact sequence 0 → lim←_F 𝕎_M^{G_{F(𝔯)}} → lim←_F (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_{F(𝔯)}} →δ_𝔯 H^1_∞(K(𝔯),W_M) → 0, where H^1_∞(K(𝔯),W_M) = lim←_{K⊂_f F⊂K_∞} H^1(F(𝔯),W_M).
items.note: Inverse limit of Proposition 4.5(i) (finite terms, Proposition B.1.1(i)); the term lim← W_M^{G_{F(𝔯)}} vanishes by Lemma B.3.2. This removes the obstruction W_M^{G_{F(1)}} ≠ 0 in the limit.

items.name: Proposition 4.8: lifting the Euler system to 𝕎_M/W_M
items.statement: Suppose 𝐜 is an Euler system and 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡. There is a family of 𝒪[G_K]-module maps {𝐝_F : X_{F(𝔯)} → (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_{F(𝔯)}} : K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞} lifting 𝐜, i.e. δ_{F(𝔯)} ∘ 𝐝_F = 𝐜 : X_{F(𝔯)} → H^1(F(𝔯),W_M) (x_{F(𝔰)} ↦ 𝐜_{F(𝔰)} for 𝔰 | 𝔯, Lemma 2.3), and N_{F'(𝔯)/F(𝔯)} ∘ 𝐝_{F'} = 𝐝_F ∘ π_{F'/F} for K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F' ⊂ K_∞, where N_{F'(𝔯)/F(𝔯)} : (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_{F'(𝔯)}} → (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_{F(𝔯)}} is the norm and π_{F'/F} : X_{F'(𝔯)} → X_{F(𝔯)} is the map (1) of Definition 2.1, x_{F'(𝔰)} ↦ x_{F(𝔰)} (the printed diagram labels this left vertical map N_{F'(𝔯)/F(𝔯)} as well). These conditions determine each 𝐝_F uniquely up to an element of Hom_{𝒪[G_K]}(X_{F(𝔯)}, 𝕎_M).
items.note: ES.3 plans: "Prove lift and generator independence in the intrinsic target" and "Over K use Rubin". Proof: apply Hom_{Λ_𝔯/M}(X_{∞,𝔯}/M, −) to Proposition 4.7; Ext^1 vanishes by Lemma 4.6(ii) and Proposition 3.4(ii), giving d_∞; descend via Corollary 3.2. Remark 4.9: only existence for individual F is used; compatibility in F gives the uniqueness.

items.name: Definition 4.10: Kolyvagin derivative class κ_{F,𝔯,M}
items.statement: Suppose 𝐜 is an Euler system, K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, M ∈ 𝒪 is nonzero, and 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M}. Fix a map 𝐝 = 𝐝_F : X_{F(𝔯)} → 𝕎_M/W_M lifting 𝐜 as in Proposition 4.8. Fix N_{F(1)/F} ∈ Z[Gal(F(𝔯)/F)] whose restriction to Gal(F(1)/F) is Σ_{γ∈Gal(F(1)/F)} γ and write D_{𝔯,F} = N_{F(1)/F} D_𝔯. Lemma 4.2 shows 𝐝(D_{𝔯,F} x_{F(𝔯)}) ∈ (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_F}, and κ_{F,𝔯,M} = δ_F(𝐝(D_{𝔯,F} x_{F(𝔯)})) ∈ H^1(F,W_M).
items.note: ES.3 ("Derivative operators and corrected Kolyvagin classes") plans the derivative classes and says "Over K use Rubin". This is the construction the paper credits to Kolyvagin [Ko2] ("Following Kolyvagin [Ko2]", p. 62); Rubin's universal-Euler-system lift is his own device for the case W^{G_{F(𝔯)}} ≠ 0.

items.name: Remark 4.11: κ_{F,𝔯,M} is well defined
items.statement: The definition of κ_{F,𝔯,M} is independent of the choice of N_{F(1)/F} (Lemma 4.2) and of the choice of 𝐝 in Proposition 4.8: if 𝐝' is another choice then 𝐝 − 𝐝' ∈ Hom_{G_K}(X_{F(𝔯)},𝕎_M), so 𝐝(D_{𝔯,F}x_{F(𝔯)}) − 𝐝'(D_{𝔯,F}x_{F(𝔯)}) ∈ image(𝕎_M^{G_F}) = ker(δ_F). Also κ_{F,𝔯,M} depends only on the images of {𝐜_{F(𝔰)} : 𝔰 | 𝔯} in H^1(F(𝔯),W_M).
items.note: ES.3 plans: "Prove lift and generator independence in the intrinsic target."

items.name: Lemma 4.12: explicit cocycle for κ_{F,𝔯,M}
items.statement: Suppose 𝐜 is an Euler system, K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, M ∈ 𝒪 is nonzero, 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M}, and 𝐝 : X_{F(𝔯)} → 𝕎_M/W_M is a lifting of 𝐜 as in Proposition 4.8. Let f ∈ 𝕎_M be any lifting of 𝐝(D_{𝔯,F}x_{F(𝔯)}). Then κ_{F,𝔯,M} is represented by the cocycle γ ↦ (γ − 1)f ∈ W_M.
items.note: Definition 4.10 plus Proposition 4.5(ii). Used in the proof of Theorem 5.4.

items.name: Lemma 4.13(i): κ_{F,1,M} is the image of 𝐜_F
items.statement: With 𝐜, F, M as in Definition 4.10: the class κ_{F,1,M} is the image of 𝐜_F in H^1(F,W_M).
items.note: ES.3 acceptance: "the conductor-one component is the initial class in the theorem's precise target". Proof uses D_{1,F} = N_{F(1)/F}, Proposition 4.5(iii) and Cor_{F(1)/F} 𝐜_{F(1)} = 𝐜_F.

items.name: Lemma 4.13(ii): restriction of κ to F(𝔯)
items.statement: With 𝐜, F, M, 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M} as in Definition 4.10: the restriction of κ_{F,𝔯,M} to F(𝔯) is the image of D_{𝔯,F}𝐜_{F(𝔯)} in H^1(F(𝔯),W_M).
items.note: ES.3 plans: "the exact restriction/descent statement". Used in Corollary 6.2 and Lemma 6.3.

items.name: Lemma 4.13(iii): change of modulus
items.statement: With 𝐜, F as in Definition 4.10: if M | M' and 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M'} then under the natural map H^1(F,W_{M'}) → H^1(F,W_M), κ_{F,𝔯,M'} ↦ κ_{F,𝔯,M}, and under the natural map H^1(F,W_M) → H^1(F,W_{M'}), κ_{F,𝔯,M} ↦ (M'/M)κ_{F,𝔯,M'}.
items.note: ES.3 acceptance: "quotient/scalar/twist compatibility is proved". Used in Corollary 6.5.

items.name: Theorem 5.1: κ_{F,𝔯,M} is finite away from p𝔯
items.statement: Suppose K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, M ∈ 𝒪 is nonzero, and 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M}. If w is a place of F not dividing p𝔯 then (κ_{F,𝔯,M})_w ∈ H^1_f(F_w,W_M). Equivalently, κ_{F,𝔯,M} ∈ 𝒮^{Σ_{p𝔯}}(F,W_M), where Σ_{p𝔯} is the set of primes of K dividing p𝔯.
items.note: Main local result (proved in §6: Corollary 6.2(ii), Lemma 6.3, Propositions 6.1, 6.8). ES.3 plans the derivative classes and says the corrected classes are only then exported as "a Kolyvagin system", which includes this local condition; the stage text does not single out primes away from p𝔯, so the planning is implicit.

items.name: Lemma 5.2: the polynomial Q_𝔮
items.statement: Suppose M ∈ 𝒪 is nonzero and 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡_{K,M}. Then there is a unique Q_𝔮(x) ∈ (𝒪/M𝒪)[x] such that P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;x) ≡ (x − 1)Q_𝔮(x) (mod M).
items.note: Take Q_𝔮(x) = (P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;x) − P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;1))/(x − 1); uniqueness since x − 1 is not a zero divisor. Ingredient of the finite–singular map; ES.1 plans: "Construct the finite–singular comparison".

items.name: Definition 5.3: α_𝔮, β_𝔮
items.statement: Suppose M ∈ 𝒪 is nonzero and 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡_{K,M}; use the same prime 𝔔 of K̄ above 𝔮 to choose σ_𝔮 and Fr_𝔮, and fix σ̄_𝔮 in the inertia group of 𝔔 extending σ_𝔮. By Lemma I.4.7(i) (applicable by Lemma 1.2(i)) there are isomorphisms α_𝔮 : H^1_s(K_𝔮,W_M) ≅ W_M^{Fr_𝔮=1} and β_𝔮 : H^1_f(K_𝔮,W_M) ≅ W_M/(Fr_𝔮 − 1)W_M given on cocycles by α_𝔮(c) = c(σ̄_𝔮), β_𝔮(c) = c(Fr_𝔮).
items.note: ES.1 plans: "Prove unramified, finite, singular and transverse local descriptions at an auxiliary q, using the actual Frobenius quotient and inertia maps." The isomorphisms themselves are Lemma I.4.7 (Ch. I).

items.name: Definition 5.3: finite–singular comparison φ^{fs}_𝔮
items.statement: Since P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;Fr_𝔮^{-1}) annihilates W_M (Lemma 1.2(iv)), Q_𝔮 induces Q_𝔮(Fr_𝔮^{-1}) : W_M/(Fr_𝔮 − 1)W_M → W_M^{Fr_𝔮=1}. The finite–singular comparison map φ^{fs}_𝔮 : H^1_f(K_𝔮,W_M) → H^1_s(K_𝔮,W_M) is the composition α_𝔮^{-1} ∘ Q_𝔮(Fr_𝔮^{-1}) ∘ β_𝔮. If K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞ and 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M} then F_𝔔 = K_𝔮 and φ^{fs}_𝔮 is viewed as a map H^1_f(F_𝔔,W_M) → H^1_s(F_𝔔,W_M).
items.note: ES.1 plans: "Construct the finite–singular comparison including its cyclic-group tensor factor".

items.name: Theorem 5.4: singular part of κ_{F,𝔯𝔮,M} at 𝔮
items.statement: Suppose K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, M ∈ 𝒪 is nonzero, and 𝔯𝔮 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M}. If φ^{fs}_𝔮 is the map of Definition 5.3 and (κ_{F,𝔯𝔮,M})^s_𝔮 denotes the image of κ_{F,𝔯𝔮,M} in H^1_s(F_𝔔,W_M), then (κ_{F,𝔯𝔮,M})^s_𝔮 = φ^{fs}_𝔮(κ_{F,𝔯,M}).
items.note: ES.3 plans: "verify all finite–singular edge relations". Proved in §7 via Lemmas 4.12, 7.1, 7.3 and identity (9); equivalently Q_𝔮(Fr_𝔮^{-1})κ_{F,𝔯,M}(Fr_𝔮) = κ_{F,𝔯𝔮,M}(σ_𝔮) in W_M. This is the key input to the Selmer bounds of Ch. V.

items.name: φ^{fs}_𝔮 is an isomorphism when W_M/(Fr_𝔮−1)W_M is free of rank one
items.statement: Suppose 0 ≠ M ∈ 𝒪, 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡_{K,M}, and W_M/(Fr_𝔮 − 1)W_M is free of rank one over 𝒪/M𝒪. Then Q_𝔮(Fr_𝔮^{-1}) : W_M/(Fr_𝔮 − 1)W_M → W_M^{Fr_𝔮=1} and hence φ^{fs}_𝔮 are isomorphisms.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. IV §5, proof of Corollary 5.5, p. 68
items.note: Unnumbered fact in the proof, from Lemma 1.2(iii) and Corollary A.2.7 (τ = Fr_𝔮^{-1}, Q = Q_𝔮). ES.1 acceptance: "finite–singular isomorphisms commute with quotient maps".

items.name: Corollary 5.5: equality of orders
items.statement: Suppose 0 ≠ M ∈ 𝒪, 𝔯𝔮 ∈ 𝓡_{K,M}, and W_M/(Fr_𝔮 − 1)W_M is free of rank one over 𝒪/M𝒪. Then the order of (κ_{K,𝔯𝔮,M})^s_𝔮 in H^1_s(K_𝔮,W_M) is equal to the order of (κ_{K,𝔯,M})_𝔮 in H^1_f(K_𝔮,W_M).
items.note: From Theorem 5.4 and the preceding item. ES.3 plans the "finite–singular edge relations"; this is their consequence.

items.name: Proposition 6.1: Euler system classes are unramified away from p
items.statement: If K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, and 𝒬 is a prime of F(𝔯) not dividing p, then for every γ ∈ G_K, (γ𝐜_{F(𝔯)})_𝒬 ∈ H^1_ur(F(𝔯)_𝒬,T) and (γ𝐜̄_{F(𝔯)})_𝒬 ∈ H^1_ur(F(𝔯)_𝒬,W_M), where 𝐜̄_{F(𝔯)} is the image of 𝐜_{F(𝔯)} in H^1(F(𝔯),W_M).
items.note: {γ𝐜_{F(𝔯)}}_F ∈ H^1_∞(K(𝔯),T) and universal norms along K_∞ are unramified away from p (Corollary B.3.4, planned as the SelmerIwasawaCohomology packet node L3/universal-norms-unramified (ii), applied over K(𝔯) along K_∞(𝔯)/K(𝔯)); holds even where T is ramified. Uses the Euler system extending in the K_∞-direction.

items.name: Corollary 6.2(i): κ unramified away from p𝔯
items.statement: Suppose K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M}, and 𝒬 is a prime of F not dividing p𝔯. Then (κ_{F,𝔯,M})_𝒬 ∈ H^1_ur(F_𝒬,W_M).
items.note: Inertia at 𝒬 lies in G_{F(𝔯)}; apply Lemma 4.13(ii) and Proposition 6.1.

items.name: Corollary 6.2(ii): finite where T is unramified
items.statement: Suppose K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M}, and 𝒬 is a prime of F not dividing p𝔯. If T is unramified at 𝒬 then (κ_{F,𝔯,M})_𝒬 ∈ H^1_f(F_𝒬,W_M).
items.note: Lemma I.3.8(ii): H^1_f = H^1_ur when T is unramified.

items.name: Lemma 6.3: archimedean places
items.statement: Suppose K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M}, and w is an infinite place of F. Then (κ_{F,𝔯,M})_w ∈ H^1_f(F_w,W_M).
items.note: w splits completely in F(𝔯)/F; Lemma 4.13(ii), Remark I.3.7 (H^1_f(F_w,T) = H^1(F_w,T)) and Lemma I.3.8(i).

items.name: Corollary 6.5: Theorem 5.1 with a bounded loss
items.statement: There is a positive integer m, independent of M, such that for every K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, every 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡_{F,Mm}, and every prime 𝒬 of F not dividing p𝔯, (κ_{F,𝔯,M})_𝒬 ∈ H^1_f(F_𝒬,W_M).
items.note: m = sup_{𝔮∤p} [W^{I_𝔮} : (W^{I_𝔮})_div]; Lemma I.3.5(iii), Corollary 6.2 and Lemma 4.13(iii). Rubin notes it suffices in place of Theorem 5.1 for the theorems of Ch. II.

items.name: Definition 6.6: semilocal cohomology and W^f_M
items.statement: Fix 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, a prime 𝔮 of K not dividing p𝔯, and inertia and decomposition groups 𝓘 ⊂ 𝒟 ⊂ G_K of 𝔮. For L/K finite unramified at 𝔮 let S_L be the primes of L above 𝔮, H^i(L_𝔮,W_M) = ⊕_{𝒬∈S_L} H^i(L_𝒬,W_M) and H^i(L_𝔮,T^𝓘/MT^𝓘) = ⊕_{𝒬∈S_L} H^i(L_𝒬,T^{𝓘_𝒬}/MT^{𝓘_𝒬}) (Gal(L/K)-modules), res_𝔮 the sum of restrictions. W^f_M = T^𝓘/MT^𝓘 ≅ ((W^𝓘)_div)_M ⊂ (W_M)^𝓘 ⊂ W_M, 𝕎^f_M = Ind(W^f_M) = Maps(G_K,W^f_M) ⊂ 𝕎_M, and Ind_𝒟(W_M) ⊂ 𝕎_M (resp. Ind_𝒟(W^f_M) ⊂ 𝕎^f_M) the maps with f(hg) = hf(g) for all h ∈ 𝒟.
items.note: Local mimic of the construction of κ, used to prove Theorem 5.1 at primes where T is ramified. Ind_𝒟(W_M) is TauCeti.coind G_K 𝒟 W_M (Coinduced.lean:82) but the rest of the definition is not in the library.

items.name: Lemma 6.7: global–local connecting-map diagram
items.statement: With 𝔯, 𝔮 ∤ p𝔯, 𝓘 ⊂ 𝒟 and W^f_M, 𝕎^f_M as in Definition 6.6: for every K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞ there is a natural commutative diagram with exact columns whose columns are 0 → W_M^{G_{F(𝔯)}} → 𝕎_M^{G_{F(𝔯)}} → (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_{F(𝔯)}} →δ_{F(𝔯)} H^1(F(𝔯),W_M) → 0, 0 → H^0(F(𝔯)_𝔮,W_M) → 𝕎_M^{G_{F(𝔯)}} → (𝕎_M/Ind_𝒟(W_M))^{G_{F(𝔯)}} →δ_{F(𝔯)_𝔮} H^1(F(𝔯)_𝔮,W_M) → 0, and 0 → H^0(F(𝔯)_𝔮,W^f_M) → (𝕎^f_M)^{G_{F(𝔯)}} → (𝕎^f_M/Ind_𝒟(W^f_M))^{G_{F(𝔯)}} →δ_{F(𝔯)_𝔮,W^f_M} H^1(F(𝔯)_𝔮,W^f_M) → 0, with the natural horizontal maps (the left-to-middle bottom map being res_𝔮).
items.note: G_{F(𝔯)}-cohomology of three short exact sequences; Corollary B.4.4 and Proposition B.5.2.

items.name: Proposition 6.8: local and unramified lifts of 𝐜
items.statement: Suppose 𝐜 is an Euler system and 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡; fix a prime 𝔮 of K not dividing p𝔯 and 𝓘 ⊂ 𝒟, W^f_M, 𝕎^f_M and the semilocal groups H^i(F(𝔯)_𝔮, ·) as in Definition 6.6 (the decomposition group of 𝔮 in K_∞/K being infinite). There are two families of 𝒪[G_K]-module maps {𝐝_{F,𝔮} : X_{F(𝔯)} → (𝕎_M/Ind_𝒟(W_M))^{G_{F(𝔯)}}} and {𝐝^f_{F,𝔮} : X_{F(𝔯)} → (𝕎^f_M/Ind_𝒟(W^f_M))^{G_{F(𝔯)}}} (K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞) lifting 𝐜, i.e. such that (i) they are compatible with the norm maps for K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F' ⊂ K_∞, and (ii) for every K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞ and every 𝔰 | 𝔯, δ_{F(𝔯)_𝔮} ∘ 𝐝_{F,𝔮} and δ_{F(𝔯)_𝔮,W^f_M} ∘ 𝐝^f_{F,𝔮} both send x_{F(𝔰)} to (𝐜_{F(𝔰)})_𝔮. Each 𝐝_{F,𝔮} is determined up to Hom_{𝒪[G_K]}(X_{F(𝔯)},𝕎_M), and each 𝐝^f_{F,𝔮} up to Hom_{𝒪[G_K]}(X_{F(𝔯)},𝕎^f_M), by these two conditions.
items.note: Local analogue of Proposition 4.8; uses Proposition 6.1 (classes land in H^1(F(𝔯)_𝒬,T^{𝓘_𝒬})), a Z_p-subextension K'_∞ with finitely many primes above 𝔮, Lemma B.3.2, Proposition B.2.7(ii), Proposition 3.4 and Corollary 3.2.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 at primes where T is ramified
items.statement: With K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡_{F,M} and 𝔮 ∤ p𝔯: for every prime 𝒬 of F above 𝔮, (κ_{F,𝔯,M})_𝒬 lies in the image of H^1(F_𝒬, T^{𝓘_𝒬}/MT^{𝓘_𝒬}) → H^1(F_𝒬,W_M), hence in the image of H^1(F_𝒬^ur/F_𝒬, T^{𝓘_𝒬}/MT^{𝓘_𝒬}), hence (since Gal(F_𝒬^ur/F_𝒬) has cohomological dimension one, H^1_ur(F_𝒬,T) surjects onto it) in the image of H^1_ur(F_𝒬,T), so (κ_{F,𝔯,M})_𝒬 ∈ H^1_f(F_𝒬,W_M).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. IV §6, proof of Theorem 5.1, pp. 73–74
items.note: Compares 𝐝 (Proposition 4.8) and 𝐝^f_𝔮 (Proposition 6.8) by the uniqueness in Proposition 6.8 (Remark 6.9), then Lemmas I.3.5(ii), I.3.8(i). Same planning as Theorem 5.1 (ES.3 "export a Kolyvagin system").

items.name: Identity (9): lifted telescoping in Z[𝓘]
items.statement: Fix a prime 𝔔 of K̄ above 𝔮 with inertia and decomposition groups 𝓘 ⊂ 𝒟; lift σ_𝔮 to 𝓘 and view N_𝔮 = Σ_{i=1}^{m} σ_𝔮^i, D_𝔮 = Σ_{i=0}^{m−1} iσ_𝔮^i ∈ Z[𝓘], where m = [K(𝔮):K(1)]. Then (σ_𝔮 − 1)D_𝔮 = mσ_𝔮^m − N_𝔮 in Z[𝓘].
items.note: Replacement for (4) when σ_𝔮^m ≠ 1 in 𝓘. ES.3 plans only the identity in the finite group ring.

items.name: Lemma 7.1: decomposition-group elements commute on lifts
items.statement: Fix an Euler system 𝐜, a nonzero M ∈ 𝒪, a prime 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡 (dividing 𝔯 or not), 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, and a prime 𝔔 of K̄ above 𝔮 with inertia and decomposition groups 𝓘 ⊂ 𝒟 ⊂ G_K (the setting of §7). Suppose 𝐝 : X_{F(𝔯)} → 𝕎_M/W_M is a lifting of 𝐜 as in Proposition 4.8, and 𝐝̂(x_{F(𝔯)}) ∈ 𝕎_M is a lift of 𝐝(x_{F(𝔯)}). For every γ ∈ G_K and σ, σ' ∈ 𝒟, σσ'γ𝐝̂(x_{F(𝔯)}) = σ'σγ𝐝̂(x_{F(𝔯)}).
items.note: Here 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡 (whether or not 𝔮 | 𝔯). By Proposition 6.1, cocycles for γ𝐜_{F(𝔯)} vanish on 𝓘 ∩ G_{F(𝔯)}, which contains the commutator subgroup of 𝒟. Remark 7.2: this fails in general for σ, σ' ∉ 𝒟.

items.name: Lemma 7.3: norm relation lifts to 𝕎_M
items.statement: Suppose 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡_{K,M} does not divide 𝔯, and K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞. Fix a lifting 𝐝 : X_{F(𝔯𝔮)} → 𝕎_M/W_M of 𝐜 as in Proposition 4.8, and fix liftings 𝐝̂(x_{F(𝔯𝔮)}), 𝐝̂(x_{F(𝔯)}) ∈ 𝕎_M of 𝐝(x_{F(𝔯𝔮)}) and 𝐝(x_{F(𝔯)}). Then for every γ ∈ G_K, N_𝔮γ𝐝̂(x_{F(𝔯𝔮)}) = P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;Fr_𝔮^{-1})γ𝐝̂(x_{F(𝔯)}).
items.note: 'Essentially equivalent to Theorem 5.4'. Proof: the difference lies in W_M and is independent of choices; then choose lifts via a finite extension F'/F in K_∞ whose decomposition group at 𝔮 in F'(𝔯𝔮)/F(𝔯𝔮) has order divisible by k_pM (uses that decomposition groups in K_∞/K are infinite) and Lemma 7.1. The proof only uses M | [K(𝔮):K(1)], not M | P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;1) (this is why Corollary 8.1 may apply it at 𝔮 ∉ R_{K,M}, PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E19; misprints in the proof: E17, E18).

items.name: Corollary 8.1: Kolyvagin's congruence condition
items.statement: Suppose 𝐜 is an Euler system for T, K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, 𝔮 ∈ 𝓡 is prime, and 𝔯𝔮 ∈ 𝓡. Then for every prime 𝒬 of F(𝔯𝔮) dividing 𝔮, (𝐜_{F(𝔯𝔮)})_𝒬 = ((P_𝔮(Fr_𝔮^{-1}) − P_𝔮(N(𝔮)Fr_𝔮^{-1}))/[K(𝔮):K(1)]) (𝐜_{F(𝔯)})_𝒬 ∈ H^1(F(𝔯𝔮)_𝒬,T), where P_𝔮(x) = P(Fr_𝔮^{-1}|T*;x).
items.note: The 'congruence condition' of Kolyvagin's original definition of Euler systems in [Ko2] (Remark II.1.5), which Rubin bypasses by requiring classes in the K_∞-direction and recovers here. R(x) = (P_𝔮(x) − P_𝔮(N(𝔮)x))/[K(𝔮):K(1)] ∈ 𝒪[x] since [K(𝔮):K(1)] | N(𝔮) − 1. Proof: H^1(F(𝔯𝔮)_𝒬,T) = lim← H^1(F(𝔯𝔮)_𝒬,W_M) (Proposition B.2.3), Lemma I.3.2(i), Proposition 4.5(ii), Lemmas 1.2(ii), 7.1, 7.3. HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.2 plans a Heegner-specific 'reduction-congruence relation', not this general statement.

items.name: Example 8.2: T = Z_p(1)
items.statement: Suppose T = Z_p(1). For 𝔯 ∈ 𝓡, H^1(F(𝔯),T) = (F(𝔯)^×)^ (p-adic completion) and P_𝔮(x) = 1 − x, so (P_𝔮(Fr_𝔮^{-1}) − P_𝔮(N(𝔮)Fr_𝔮^{-1}))/[K(𝔮):K(1)] = ((N(𝔮) − 1)/[K(𝔮):K(1)])Fr_𝔮^{-1}, and Corollary 8.1 says 𝐜_{F(𝔯𝔮)}/𝐜_{F(𝔯)}^{((N(𝔮)−1)/[K(𝔮):K(1)])Fr_𝔮^{-1}} is, for every prime 𝒬 of F(𝔯𝔮) above 𝔮, a unit at 𝒬 whose image in 𝕜_𝒬^× (𝕜_𝒬 the residue field) has order prime to p, the 'p-part' of the congruence 𝐜_{F(𝔯𝔮)} ≡ 𝐜_{F(𝔯)}^{((N(𝔮)−1)/[K(𝔮):K(1)])Fr_𝔮^{-1}} (mod 𝒬). For cyclotomic units this reflects 1 − ζ_{rq} ≡ 1 − ζ_r^{Fr_q^{-1}} modulo every prime above q.
items.note: Denominator written with [K(𝔮):K(1)] as in Corollary 8.1; the page prints [K(𝔮):K] (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E20, PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E21). Illustration only.

items.name: R_M = R_{K,M} and the classes κ_{r,M} (Ch. V notation)
items.statement: Fix an Euler system c for (T, 𝒦, 𝒩). For a power M of p, R_M = R_{K,M} (Definition IV.1.1) is the set of ideals in R divisible only by primes q such that q ∤ 𝒩, M | [K(q) : K(1)], M | P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; 1), and q splits completely in K(1). For r ∈ R_M, κ_{r,M} ∈ H¹(K, W_M) denotes the Kolyvagin derivative class κ_{K,r,M} of Chapter IV §4. For an O-module B and b ∈ B, order(b, B) = inf{n ≥ 0 : 𝔭ⁿ b = 0} ≤ ∞. ι_M : H¹(K, W_M) → H¹(K, W) is induced by W_M ⊂ W; (η)_L is restriction to an extension L.
items.note: Notation of the descent. ES.1 plans the auxiliary-prime set: 'Construct the ray-class extensions K(q), their selected local cyclic quotients and the squarefree-conductor category'; ES.3 plans the derivative classes ('Construct the cyclic group-ring norm N_q and derivative D_q ...'). Library audit (data/library-coverage.json) records Galois-cohomological Selmer groups as absent from both libraries; Tau Ceti has only RayClassGroup (TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.RayClassGroup), not ray class fields K(q).

items.name: Lemma 1.1: order of ι_M(κ_{1,M}) equals ord_𝔭 M − ind_O(c)
items.statement: Suppose M is a power of p and ord_𝔭 M ≥ ind_O(c). Then order(ι_M(κ_{1,M}), H¹(K, W)) = ord_𝔭 M − ind_O(c).
items.note: Proof: by Lemma IV.4.13(i) ι_M(κ_{1,M}) is the image of c_K under H¹(K,T) → H¹(K,W_M) → H¹(K,W), whose kernel is M H¹(K,T) + H¹(K,T)_tors (Lemma I.2.2(iii)); then use that H¹(K,T)/H¹(K,T)_tors is torsion-free and Definition II.2.1 of ind_O(c). This is the base case d_0 of both inductions in §2 and the input (16) of §3. ES.4: 'its upper bound is the divisibility index of the initial class, with infinity allowed when the class is zero'; ES.3 acceptance: 'the conductor-one component is the initial class in the theorem's precise target'.

items.name: Lemma 2.1: existence of γ ∈ G_L with large κ(γτ), η(γτ) (p > 2)
