items.statement: Assume p > 2 and Hyp(K, T); fix τ ∈ G_K as in Hyp(K, T)(i), i.e. τ acts trivially on μ_{p^∞}, on (O_K^×)^{1/p^∞} and on K(1), and T/(τ − 1)T is free of rank one over O (so W_M/(τ − 1)W_M ≅ O/MO ≅ W*_M/(τ − 1)W*_M). Fix a power M of p. Suppose L is a Galois extension of K such that G_L acts trivially on W_M and on W*_M. If κ ∈ H¹(K, W_M), η ∈ H¹(K, W*_M), then there is γ ∈ G_L satisfying (i) order(κ(γτ), W_M/(τ − 1)W_M) ≥ order((κ)_L, H¹(L, W_M)); (ii) order(η(γτ), W*_M/(τ − 1)W*_M) ≥ order((η)_L, H¹(L, W*_M)).
items.note: Proof: the bad sets B_κ, B_η are empty or cosets of subgroups of index ≥ p (uses irreducibility of T ⊗ k, Hyp(K,T)(ii), to get κ(G_L) = W_{𝔭^d}); a union of two such cosets is proper since p > 2. Remark 2.2: this is the only use of p > 2 in Theorem II.2.2. ES.1: 'Prove the simultaneous localization and independence lemmas needed for descent ... Record the small-prime restrictions in the argument.' The printed inclusion κ(J) ⊂ W_{𝔭^{d−1}} + (τ − 1)W_M ⊊ W_{𝔭^d} holds only after intersecting with W_{𝔭^d} (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E22).

items.name: The auxiliary field Ω
items.statement: Ω = K(W) K(1) K(μ_{p^∞}, (O_K^×)^{1/p^∞}), where K(W) is the smallest extension of K such that G_{K(W)} acts trivially on W. G_Ω acts trivially on W* as well.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. V §2, p. 81 (also Ch. II §2, p. 24)
items.note: The error terms n_W, n*_W are lengths of H¹(Ω/K, ·) ∩ Selmer. ES.4: 'In Rubin II.2.2 retain both n_W and n_W* and every auxiliary-field hypothesis'.

items.name: Lemma 2.3: inductive Chebotarev choice of Kolyvagin primes q_1,…,q_k
items.statement: Assume p > 2 and Hyp(K, T), τ as above. Fix a power M of p. Suppose C is a finite subset of H¹(K, W*_M) and let k = |C|. Then there is a finite set Σ = {q_1, …, q_k} of primes of K such that, writing r_i = ∏_{j=1}^{i} q_j (0 ≤ i ≤ k), for every i, 1 ≤ i ≤ k: (i) q_i ∈ R_M; (ii) Fr_{q_i} is in the conjugacy class of τ in Gal(K(W_M)/K); (iii) order((κ_{r_{i−1},M})_{q_i}, H¹_f(K_{q_i}, W_M)) ≥ order((κ_{r_{i−1},M})_Ω, H¹(Ω, W_M)); (iv) {η ∈ C : (η)_q = 0 for every q ∈ Σ} ⊂ H¹(Ω/K, W*_M).
items.note: Proof: induction; apply Lemma 2.1 with L = K(W_M)K(1)(μ_M, (O_K^×)^{1/M}), κ = κ_{r_{i−1},M}, η = η_i, then Chebotarev in the fixed field L′ of ker((κ_{r_{i−1},M})_L) ∩ ker((η_i)_L) to pick q_i ∤ 𝒩′r_{i−1} with Frobenius γτ; q_i ∈ R_M by Lemma IV.1.3; H¹_f(K_q, W_M) ≅ W_M/(Fr_q − 1)W_M by Lemma I.4.7(i). ES.1: 'Use upstream Chebotarev on the finite extensions cut out jointly by T modulo powers and a finite collection of cohomology classes'. The Chebotarev density theorem itself is not in the pinned libraries (Tau Ceti has only Frobenius prime sets, TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/FrobeniusPrimeSet.lean, and NumberField.exists_auxiliaryPrime for rational primes ≡ 1 mod n).

items.name: Definition 2.4: the singular localization map loc^s_{Σ,W_M} and exact sequence (4)
items.statement: Suppose Σ is a finite set of primes in R. For every M there is an exact sequence 0 → S^{Σ_p}(K, W_M) → S^{Σ∪Σ_p}(K, W_M) --loc^s_{Σ,W_M}--> ⊕_{q∈Σ} H¹_s(K_q, W_M), where H¹_s(K_q, W_M) = H¹(K_q, W_M)/H¹_f(K_q, W_M) and loc^s_{Σ,W_M} is the sum of the localization maps (denoted loc^s_{Σ∪Σ_p,Σ_p} in Theorem I.7.3); loc^s_{Σ,W} is defined in the same way with W in place of W_M. Also Σ_𝔞 = set of primes dividing an ideal 𝔞, and n_W = ℓ_O(H¹(Ω/K, W) ∩ S^{Σ_p}(K, W)).
items.note: Feeds the global duality Theorem I.7.3(iii), which bounds [S_{Σ_p}(K,W*_m) : S_{Σ∪Σ_p}(K,W*_m)] by ℓ_O(coker loc^s). ES.4: 'Apply Poitou–Tate to strict/relaxed modifications and prove length bounds on the dual Selmer group'.

items.name: Lemma 2.5: ℓ_O(coker loc^s_{Σ,W_𝔪}) ≤ ind_O(c) + n_W
items.statement: Assume p > 2 and Hyp(K, T). Suppose 𝔪 = 𝔭ⁿ is a nonzero ideal of O, k ∈ Z⁺, M is a power of p satisfying ord_𝔭 M ≥ n + (k + 1)n_W + ind_O(c), and Σ = {q_1, …, q_k} ⊂ R_M is a finite set of primes of K such that for 1 ≤ i ≤ k, (a) Fr_{q_i} is in the conjugacy class of τ in Gal(K(W_M)/K), (b) order((κ_{r_{i−1},M})_{q_i}, H¹_f(K_{q_i}, W_M)) ≥ order((κ_{r_{i−1},M})_Ω, H¹(Ω, W_M)), where r_i = ∏_{j=1}^{i} q_j. Then the map loc^s_{Σ,W_𝔪} of (4) satisfies ℓ_O(coker(loc^s_{Σ,W_𝔪})) ≤ ind_O(c) + n_W.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. V §2, Lemma 2.5, p. 82 (proofs pp. 83–86)
items.note: Two proofs: first under (∗) W^{G_K} = 0 and H¹(Ω/K, W) = 0 (Remark 2.6; bound ind_O(c)), then in general. Core step: by Corollary IV.5.5 (finite–singular relation, needs (a)), order((κ_{r_i,M})_{q_i}, H¹_s) = order((κ_{r_{i−1},M})_{q_i}, H¹_f); Theorem IV.5.1 puts κ_{r_i,M} in S^{Σ_p r_i}(K, W_M); the submodules A^{(i)} generated by 𝔭^{d_i−n}ι_M(κ_{r_i,M}) give a filtration of loc^s(A) with graded lengths ≥ n + d_{i−1} − d_i, and ℓ_O(⊕_{q∈Σ} H¹_s(K_q, W_𝔪)) = kn by Lemma I.4.7(i). ES.4: 'The error-tolerant Rubin/classical interface retains cohomological restriction errors, bounded local torsion and derivative denominators.'

items.name: Theorem II.2.2 (proved in V §2): ℓ_O(S_{Σ_p}(K, W*)) ≤ ind_O(c) + n_W + n*_W
items.statement: Suppose that p > 2 and that T satisfies Hyp(K, T). If c is an Euler system for T then ℓ_O(S_{Σ_p}(K, W*)) ≤ ind_O(c) + n_W + n*_W, where n_W = ℓ_O(H¹(Ω/K, W) ∩ S^{Σ_p}(K, W)) and n*_W = ℓ_O(H¹(Ω/K, W*) ∩ S_{Σ_p}(K, W*)).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. V §2, Proof of Theorem II.2.2, p. 86 (statement Ch. II §2, Theorem 2.2, p. 24)
items.note: Proof: for 𝔪 = 𝔭ⁿ let C be the image of S_{Σ_p}(K, W*_𝔪) (finite, Lemma I.5.7(i)) in H¹(K, W*_M) with ord_𝔭 M > n + (|S_{Σ_p}(K,W*_𝔪)| + 1)n_W + ind_O(c); Lemma 2.3 gives Σ, Lemma 2.5 plus Theorem I.7.3(iii) give ℓ_O(S_{Σ_p}(K,W*_𝔪)/S_{Σ∪Σ_p}(K,W*_𝔪)) ≤ n_W + ind_O(c), and Lemma 2.3(iv) puts ι_𝔪(S_{Σ∪Σ_p}(K,W*_𝔪)) inside H¹(Ω/K, W*) ∩ S_{Σ_p}(K, W*); pass to the direct limit over 𝔪. This is the Selmer-length half of Kolyvagin's method. ES.4 explicitly: 'In Rubin II.2.2 retain both n_W and n_W* and every auxiliary-field hypothesis'; also imported by EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L1.

items.name: The constant a (maximal G_K-stable subgroup of (τ−1)W)
items.statement: Assume Hyp(K, V) and fix τ as in Hyp(K, V)(i) (p = 2 allowed). a is the least positive integer such that 𝔭^a annihilates the maximal G_K-stable subgroup of (τ − 1)W and of (τ − 1)W*. Hyp(K, V)(ii) ensures a is finite, since a divisible G_K-stable subgroup of (τ − 1)W would be the image of a G_K-stable subgroup of (τ − 1)V, which must be zero.
items.note: One of the error constants in the exponent bound. ES.4: 'The general error-tolerant proof exports inequalities in terms of proved finite error constants.'

items.name: Lemma 3.1: variant of Lemma 2.1 with error a + 1 (any p)
items.statement: Assume Hyp(K, V), τ as in Hyp(K, V)(i). Fix a power M of p. Suppose L is a Galois extension of K such that G_L acts trivially on W_M and on W*_M. If κ ∈ H¹(K, W_M), η ∈ H¹(K, W*_M), then there is γ ∈ G_L satisfying (i) order(κ(γτ), W_M/(τ − 1)W_M) ≥ order((κ)_L, H¹(L, W_M)) − a − 1; (ii) order(η(γτ), W*_M/(τ − 1)W*_M) ≥ order((η)_L, H¹(L, W*_M)) − a − 1.
items.note: Proof as Lemma 2.1: a G_K-submodule of W_M projecting to zero in W_M/(τ − 1)W_M is killed by 𝔭^a; the extra 1 handles p = 2. ES.4 plans the error-tolerant version; ES.1: 'Record the small-prime restrictions in the argument.'

items.name: Lemma 3.2: H¹(Ω/K, W) and H¹(Ω/K, W*) are finite
items.statement: (Under Hyp(K, V).) If T ≠ O and T ≠ O(1) then H¹(Ω/K, W) and H¹(Ω/K, W*) are finite.
items.note: Proof: Corollary C.2.2 with F = K (Appendix C; also Remark II.2.5). No stage plans this finiteness; ES.4 says the general proof 'does not assert these constants are bounded for arbitrary T', and HE.7 plans the elliptic-curve-specific 'uniform bounds on restriction/corestriction kernels'.

items.name: Case T = O(1): S_{Σ_p}(K, W*) ⊂ Hom(A_K, D) is finite
items.statement: If T = O(1) then S_{Σ_p}(K, W*) ⊂ Hom(A_K, D), where A_K is the ideal class group of K; so S_{Σ_p}(K, W*) is finite.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. V §3, Proof of Theorem II.2.3, p. 87 (citing Ch. I §6.1)
items.note: First step of the proof of Theorem II.2.3. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4 plans 'Recover R06's class-group and p-ramified modules from the Selmer groups of Tate twists'. Mathlib has finiteness of the class group (NumberField.classNumber / ClassGroup.fintype), but not this Selmer identification.

items.name: Theorem II.2.3 proof, exponent step: 𝔪 S_{Σ_p}(K, W*) = 0 with 𝔪 = 𝔭^{2+2a+3b+2n+ind_O c}
items.statement: Suppose V satisfies Hyp(K, V), T ≠ O, T ≠ O(1), c is an Euler system for T (p = 2 allowed). Let n = max{ℓ_O(H¹(Ω/K, W)), ℓ_O(H¹(Ω/K, W*))} and b = ℓ_O(W^{τ=1}/(W^{τ=1})_div). Then for every power M of p and every η ∈ S_{Σ_p}(K, W*_M), order(η, H¹(K, W*_M)) ≤ 2 + 2a + 3b + 2n + ind_O c; hence if 𝔪 = 𝔭^{2+2a+3b+2n+ind_O c} then 𝔪 S_{Σ_p}(K, W*) = 0.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. V §3, Proof of Theorem II.2.3, pp. 87–88
items.note: Proof: Lemma 3.1 with L = K(W_M)K(1)(μ_M, (O_K^×)^{1/M}) and κ = κ_{1,M}; Chebotarev gives one prime q ∈ R_M (Lemma IV.1.3); Theorem IV.5.4 and Corollary A.2.6 give order((κ_{q,M})_q, H¹_s) ≥ order((κ_{1,M})_q, H¹_f) − 2b; ℓ_O(H¹_s(K_q, W_M)) ≤ ord_𝔭 M + b (Lemma I.4.7(i)); Theorem I.7.3(iii) with Σ = Σ_{pq}, Σ′ = Σ_p bounds order((η)_q, H¹_f(K_q, W*_M)) by ind_O(c) + a + 1 + n + 3b. Only one Kolyvagin prime at a time: this is Kolyvagin's bounded-exponent argument. ES.4: 'For a classical descent with nonzero bounded errors, prove a bound uniform in the torsion exponent before passing to p-primary Selmer groups.'

items.name: Theorem II.2.3 (proved in V §3): S_{Σ_p}(K, W*) is finite
items.statement: Suppose that V satisfies Hyp(K, V) and T is not the one-dimensional trivial representation. If c is an Euler system for T and c_K ∉ H¹(K, T)_tors, then S_{Σ_p}(K, W*) is finite (this holds even if p = 2).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. V §3, Proof of Theorem II.2.3, p. 88 (statement Ch. II §2, Theorem 2.3, p. 24)
items.note: From the exponent bound: S_{Σ_p}(K, W*) = S_{Σ_p}(K, W*)_𝔪 ⊂ S(K, W*)_𝔪 = ι_𝔪(S(K, W*_𝔪)) (Lemma I.5.4), finite by Lemma I.5.7(i). c_K ∉ H¹(K,T)_tors is exactly ind_O(c) < ∞. HE.7: 'Combine bounded exponent with finite finite-level Selmer groups to prove finiteness.' ES.4 owns the reusable argument ('ES.4 owns the reusable error-tolerant descent argument').

items.name: IX.1: without a Z_p-extension, c_K is unconstrained (rigidity fails)
items.statement: Suppose K has class number one, 𝒩 is an ideal of K divisible by p and all primes where T is ramified, P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; 1) = 0 for every q ∤ 𝒩 (e.g. T the symmetric square of the Tate module of an elliptic curve), 𝒦 is the maximal abelian extension of K unramified at the primes dividing 𝒩 (the print says 'unramified outside 𝒩', the slip of PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E9 and E23; the text adds 'so 𝒦 does not contain a Z_p-extension of K', which only the corrected reading satisfies since p | 𝒩), and c is an Euler system for (T, 𝒦, 𝒩). Then Cor_{F/K} c_F = ∏_{q∈Σ(F/K)} P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; 1) c_K = 0 for F ≠ K, so c_K can be replaced by any element of H¹(K, T); e.g. c_F = 0 for F ≠ K with c_K arbitrary is an Euler system. Since there are examples with these properties and nontrivial Selmer groups, no theorem like Theorem II.2.2 (or IV.5.4) whose conclusion depends essentially on c_K can hold in this situation.
items.note: Motivates the Z_p-extension (universal norm) hypothesis (ii) of Definition II.1.1. ES.2 notes only 'A system allowed by the definition may be zero'; no stage records this counterexample.

items.name: IX.1: alternative rigidity conditions (ii)′(a),(b),(c)
items.statement: In Definition II.1.1 replace condition (ii) by (ii)′: at least one of (a) 𝒦 contains a Z_p^d-extension of K in which no finite prime splits completely; (b) for every r, c_{K(r)} ∈ S^{Σ_p}(K(r), T), and there is γ ∈ G_K with γ = 1 on K(1)(μ_{p^∞}, (O_K^×)^{1/p^∞}) and γ − 1 injective on T; (c) for every r ∈ R, c_{K(r)} ∈ S^{Σ_p}(K(r), T); for every prime q ∤ 𝒩 and every power n of p, Fr_q^n − 1 is injective on T; and {c_{K(r)}} satisfies the congruence of Corollary IV.8.1. Condition (ii)′(a) is the original (ii).
items.note: These are the hypotheses under which Heegner points fit (via (b)/(c), Remark 4.2). ES.3 plans the Mazur–Rubin Q-route with 'injectivity of Fr_q^(p^k)−1', which is the MR analogue of (c), not Rubin's (ii)′; no stage defines Rubin's (ii)′.

items.name: IX.1: Theorems II.2.2, II.2.3, II.2.10 hold under (ii)′ if T^{G_{K(1)}} = 0
items.statement: Under the definition of Euler system with (ii)′ in place of (ii), Theorems II.2.2, II.2.3 and II.2.10 all hold, with conclusions exactly as stated, under the additional assumption T^{G_{K(1)}} = 0. (Idea: there is a power m of p, independent of M, such that the derivative classes κ_{K,r,M} can be constructed and the local properties of Ch. IV §5 proved for r ∈ R_{K,Mm}.)
items.note: Only sketched ('We indicate very briefly how to adapt the proofs'). Construction: T^{G_{K(r)}} = 0 (Lemma IV.2.5(i)) gives 0 → 𝕋^{G_{F(r)}} → (𝕋/T)^{G_{F(r)}} → H¹(F(r), T) → 0 with 𝕋 = Maps(G_K, T), lift c as in Proposition IV.4.8 and project to (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_{F(r)}}; Theorem IV.5.1 replaced by Corollary IV.6.5 (from Proposition IV.6.1, now an assumption); Theorem IV.5.4 via an analogue of Lemma IV.7.3 (next item). Not planned in any stage.

items.name: IX.1: analogue of Lemma IV.7.3 under (ii)′(b) via auxiliary primes l
items.statement: Assume (ii)′(b) with γ ∈ G_K. Fix rq ∈ R, a power M of p, a power M′ of p divisible by M·P(γ|T; 1) (≠ 0), and n = |μ_{p^∞} ∩ K|. Choose a prime l of K with (a) Fr_l = γ on K(1)(μ_{nM′}, (O_K^×)^{1/(nM′)}, W_{M′}), (b) Fr_l = 1 on K(rq), (c) Fr_l ≠ 1 on K(λ^{1/(np)}) where λO_K = q^h, h the order of q in the class group. Then nM′ | [K(l) : K], the decomposition group of q has order ≥ M′ in Gal(K(l)/K), P(Fr_l^{-1}|T*; Fr_l^{-1}) = P(Fr_l^{-1}|T*; 1) ≡ P(γ^{-1}|T*; 1) = P(γ|T; 1) (mod M) in O[Gal(K(rq)/K)], and, if rq ∈ R_{K,M′}, P(γ|T; 1)(N_q γ d̂(x_{F(rq)}) − P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; Fr_q^{-1}) γ d̂(x_{F(r)})) = 0 ∈ W_{M′}; this suffices for the equality of Theorem IV.5.4 for κ_{F,r,M}, κ_{F,rq,M}.
items.note: Sketch only; simultaneous satisfiability of (a)–(c) is left as an exercise. The key point: P(Fr_l^{-1}|T*; Fr_l^{-1})c_{K(r)} is a norm from K(rl) by the distribution relation, replacing universal norms from K_∞. Under (ii)′(c) one reverses §IV.8 to get Lemma IV.7.3. Not planned.

items.name: Example 1.1: the Euler system c̃_m = (ζ_m − 1)(ζ_m^{-1} − 1) twisted by χ^{-1}
items.statement: For every m > 1 prime to p define c̃_m = (ζ_m − 1)(ζ_m^{-1} − 1) ∈ (Q(μ_m)^+)^× ⊂ H¹(Q(μ_m)^+, Z_p(1)), and c̃_1 = 1. This collection is not an Euler system (c̃_{Q(μ_ℓ)} ∉ S^{Σ_p}(Q(μ_ℓ), Z_p(1)) for ℓ ≠ p). If χ : G_Q → O^× is a nontrivial character of finite order with conductor f prime to p, then the twist c = c̃^{χ^{-1}} (Definition II.4.1) is an Euler system for (Z_p(1) ⊗ χ^{-1}, Q^{ab,p}, fp), where Q^{ab,p} is the maximal abelian extension of Q unramified at p (the print says 'unramified outside p', PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E23), in the sense of (ii)′: (ii)′(a) fails but (ii)′(b) (with γ ∈ G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})}, γ ∉ ker χ) and (ii)′(c) (Example IV.8.2) hold.
items.note: EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0 plans the cyclotomic-unit system from 'norm-compatible cyclotomic p-units and their smoothed units', not this prime-to-p variant. The printed description of Q^{ab,p} ('unramified outside p') is corrected to 'unramified at p' (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E23).

items.name: Theorem 1.2: |A_L^χ| = [E_L^χ : C_{L,χ}] for even χ of conductor prime to p
items.statement: Suppose p > 2 and χ : G_Q → O^× is a nontrivial even character of finite order prime to p (the standing assumption of Ch. III §§1–2, whose notation the theorem uses) and of conductor prime to p. Then |A_L^χ| = [E_L^χ : C_{L,χ}] (notation of Ch. III §2; L the field cut out by χ).
items.note: Sketch: if χ(p) ≠ 1 this is Corollary III.2.4. Otherwise use Example 1.1: c_1 generates C_{L,χ}; Theorem II.2.2 gives |S_{Σ_p}(Q, (Q_p/Z_p) ⊗ χ)| divides [E_L^χ : C_{L,χ}]; since the derivative classes lie in S^{Σ_r}(Q, μ_M ⊗ χ^{-1}) (because c_{Q(μ_r)} ∈ S(Q(μ_r), Z_p(1) ⊗ χ^{-1}), [Ru3] Prop. 2.4), rerun the proof with Σ′ = ∅, Σ = Σ_r in Theorem I.7.3 to get |A_L^χ| = |S(Q, (Q_p/Z_p) ⊗ χ)| divides [E_L^χ : C_{L,χ}]; equality by the analytic class number formula. Planned by the EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture packet node L4/greither-gras-conjecture (Greither, Theorem 4.14 and Corollary 4.15: for F real abelian unramified at p with |Δ| prime to p and p odd, [E_p/C_p] = [A(F)] in K_0(ℤ_p[Δ])), which gives the equality for each even χ ≠ 1, including χ(p) = 1, after identifying the χ-part of Sinnott's circular units with C_{L,χ}. Rubin's route through Example 1.1 is not the one planned there. The ESCMC decomposition node L1/analytic-class-number-upgrade-at-finite-level covers only χ(p) ≠ 1.

items.name: IX.1: S(Q, (Q_p/Z_p)⊗χ) = Hom_O(A_L^χ, D) and S_{Σ_p}(Q, (Q_p/Z_p)⊗χ) = Hom(A_L^χ/P, D)
items.statement: With χ even, of conductor prime to p, and L cut out by χ: S(Q, (Q_p/Z_p) ⊗ χ) = Hom_O(A_L^χ, D) (Proposition I.6.1), while S_{Σ_p}(Q, (Q_p/Z_p) ⊗ χ) = Hom(A_L^χ/P, D), where P is the subgroup of A_L^χ generated by the classes of primes of L above p.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. IX §1, Proof of Theorem 1.2, p. 135
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4: 'Recover R06's class-group and p-ramified modules from the Selmer groups of Tate twists'.

items.name: IX.2: condition (*) replacing 'no finite prime splits completely in K_∞/K'
items.statement: (*) for every prime q of K which splits completely in K_∞/K, and for every finite extension F of K in 𝒦, (c_F)_q ∈ H¹_ur(F_q, T). Under (*) the hypothesis of Definition II.1.1 that no finite prime splits completely in K_∞/K can be removed: (*) replaces its use in Proposition IV.6.1 / Corollary B.3.4, and since the completely split primes have density zero they can be removed from R without affecting the Chebotarev arguments.
items.note: Relevant to Heegner points: all rational primes inert in the imaginary quadratic field split completely in the anticyclotomic Z_p-extension (Remark 4.2). ES.8 instead plans to 'retain Rubin's no-completely-split-finite-prime hypothesis'; (*) is not planned.

items.name: Definition 3.1: Euler system of depth M (for W_M)
items.statement: Fix a nonzero M ∈ O. An Euler system for W_M (an Euler system of depth M) is a collection of cohomology classes satisfying all the properties of Definition II.1.1 except that c_F ∈ H¹(F, W_M) instead of c_F ∈ H¹(F, T). (Remark 3.2: W_M may be replaced by any free O/MO-module of finite rank with G_K-action.) The derivative classes κ_{F,r,M} and Theorem IV.5.4 go through unchanged; Theorem IV.5.1 only in a weaker form.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. IX §3, Definition 3.1 and Remark 3.2, p. 136
items.note: Kolyvagin's original Heegner argument works with classes modulo M (Kummer images of Heegner points in H¹(K, E[M])). ES.0 plans quotient propagation of Selmer data 'under T→T/varpi^m' but not Euler systems valued in H¹(F, W_M).

items.name: Theorem 3.3: annihilation of S_{Σ_p}(K, W*_M) by a finite-depth Euler system
items.statement: Suppose M ∈ O is nonzero and c is an Euler system for W_M. Suppose Hyp(K, T) holds, the error terms n_W and n*_W of Theorem II.2.2 are both zero, and W_M^{G_K} = 0. Let 𝔞₁ = ⋂_{primes q of K, q∤p} Ann_O(W^{I_q}/(W^{I_q})_div) and let 𝔞₂ ⊂ O be the annihilator of 𝔞₁c_K in H¹(K, W_M). Then (M/𝔞₂)𝔞₁ S_{Σ_p}(K, W*_M) = 0. This is the author's final version, Theorem 9.3.3. The 1999 draft prints 'let n be the order of mc_K in H¹(K,W_M). Then nS_{Σ_p}(K,W*_M) = 0', which fails for the zero Euler system (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E25).
items.note: Stated as following from the proofs of Chapters IV and V; m is finite (Remark 3.4: [W^I : (W^I)_div] is finite, = 1 if T is unramified at q; proof of Corollary IV.6.5). (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E25). The final version continues: 'In particular if 𝔞₁c_K ≠ 0 then S_{Σ_p}(K, W*) is finite'. From the displayed annihilation this follows directly when 𝔞₁²c_K ≠ 0, for example when T is unramified at every q ∤ p, where 𝔞₁ = O. Not planned.

items.name: IX.4: K′ = K̄^{ker χ}, K′(q)_χ, K′(1)_χ and the ambient field 𝒦′
items.statement: Fix K and T as in Ch. II §1, d a positive integer dividing p − 1 and χ : G_K → Z_p^× a character of order d; K′ = K̄^{ker(χ)} is the cyclic degree-d extension cut out by χ. For every prime q of K not dividing p, K′(q)_χ is the maximal p-extension of K′ inside the ray class field of K′ modulo q such that Gal(K′/K) acts on Gal(K′(q)_χ/K′) via χ; K′(1)_χ is the χ-part of the maximal unramified p-extension of K′. 𝒦′ is an (infinite) abelian p-extension of K′ and 𝒩 an ideal of K divisible by p, the conductor of χ and all primes where T is ramified, such that 𝒦′ ⊃ K′(q)_χ for every prime q ∤ 𝒩.
items.note: For K = Q, d = 2, χ odd quadratic, K′ is imaginary quadratic and K′(q)_χ lies in the ring class field of conductor q (anticyclotomic). HE.0 plans ring class fields: 'Derive ring class fields and Artin maps from existing class field theory, including fields of definition, ramification, splitting, complex conjugation and the generalized-dihedral action' — the d = 2 case only; the general χ-part construction is not planned. Tau Ceti has ray class groups (TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.RayClassGroup) but not ray class fields.

items.name: Definition 4.1: χ-anticyclotomic Euler system for (T, 𝒦′, 𝒩)
items.statement: A collection c = {c_F ∈ H¹(F, T) : K′ ⊂_f F ⊂ 𝒦′} is a χ-anticyclotomic Euler system for (T, 𝒦′, 𝒩) if (i) whenever K′ ⊂_f F ⊂_f F′ ⊂ 𝒦′, Cor_{F′/F}(c_{F′}) = (∏_{q∈Σ(F′/F)} P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; Fr_q^{-1})) c_F, where Σ(F′/F) is the set of primes of K not dividing 𝒩 which ramify in F′ but not in F, Fr_q is a Frobenius of q in G_K, and P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; x) = det(1 − Fr_q^{-1}x|T*) ∈ O[x]; and (ii) at least one of: (a) 𝒦′ contains a Z_p^e-extension K′_∞ of K′ for some e ≥ 1 (the print writes Z_p^d, reusing the letter d of the order of χ, PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E28) in which no finite prime splits completely, with Gal(K′/K) acting on Gal(K′_∞/K′) via χ; (b) for every r, c_{K′(r)_χ} ∈ S^{Σ_p}(K′(r)_χ, T), and there is γ ∈ G_K with ε_cyc(γ) = χ(γ), γ^d the identity on K′(1)_χ(μ_{p^∞}, (O_{K′}^×)^{1/p^∞}), and γ − 1 injective on T; (c) for every r ∈ R, c_{K′(r)_χ} ∈ S^{Σ_p}(K′(r)_χ, T) (the print has c_{K(r)} ∈ S^{Σ_p}(K(r), T), PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E27); for every q ∤ 𝒩 and every power n of p, Fr_q^n − 1 is injective on T; and the classes {c_F} satisfy the appropriate analogue of the congruence of Corollary IV.8.1.
items.note: The definition designed to contain Kolyvagin's Heegner-point system. The atlas does not plan Rubin's abstract χ-anticyclotomic definition: HeegnerPointEulerSystems routes the Heegner classes through ES.2/ES.3 and 'Howard's Heegner version of Kolyvagin systems' (HE.5). Source slips: K(r) for K′(r)_χ in (ii)(c) (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E27), and the letter d for the Z_p-rank in (ii)(a), where d is already the order of χ (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E28).

items.name: Remark 4.2: for d = 1 a χ-anticyclotomic Euler system is an Euler system
items.statement: If d = 1, then χ is trivial, K′ = K, and a χ-anticyclotomic Euler system for T is the same as an Euler system for T in the sense of Definition II.1.1 (or §1).
items.note: Immediate from the definitions. Not planned since Definition 4.1 is not planned.

items.name: Remark 4.2: Heegner points give a χ-anticyclotomic Euler system satisfying (ii)(b),(c) but not (ii)(a)
items.statement: If K = Q, d = 2 and χ is an odd quadratic character, then K′ is imaginary quadratic and 𝒦′ an anticyclotomic p-extension of K′. If T is the Tate module of a modular elliptic curve and χ(q) = 1 for every q dividing the conductor [of E; printed 'of χ'], then the Heegner points in anticyclotomic extensions of K′ (modified as in §6 to get the correct distribution relation) give a χ-anticyclotomic Euler system for T. 𝒦′ can be taken to contain the anticyclotomic Z_p-extension K′_∞ of K′, but all rational primes inert in K′ split completely in K′_∞/K′, so (ii)(a) fails; both (ii)(b) and (ii)(c) hold.
items.note: Asserted without proof (Heegner points are not discussed; references [Ko2], [Ru2], [Gro2]). The norm relations are HE.2: 'For inert ℓ prime to cN prove the trace relation with a_ℓP_c'; the Kummer classes and their local conditions are HE.3; the modification of Euler factors is IX.6 (ES.2 'removal/addition of Euler factors'); the splitting of inert primes is in HE.0's 'ramification, splitting, complex conjugation and the generalized-dihedral action'. (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E26).

items.name: IX.4: R_{K′,M} and the derivative classes κ_{K′,r,M} ∈ H¹(K′, W_M)
items.statement: Given a χ-anticyclotomic Euler system and a power M of p, define as in Ch. IV §4 derivative classes κ_{K′,r,M} ∈ H¹(K′, W_M) for every r ∈ R_{K′,M}, where R_{K′,M} is the set of squarefree ideals of K divisible only by primes q with q ∤ 𝒩, M | [K′(q)_χ : K′(1)_χ], and M | P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; 1). These classes satisfy analogues of Theorems IV.5.1 and IV.5.4 and, with global duality (Theorem I.7.3), bound the appropriate Selmer group.
items.note: Only asserted ('one can proceed exactly as in Chapter IV §4'). For Heegner points (K = Q, d = 2, q inert in K′ with M | ℓ + 1 and M | a_ℓ) this is Kolyvagin's derivative class: HE.4 'For squarefree products n of Kolyvagin primes inert in K, construct the finite quotient coefficient ideal from a_ℓ and ℓ+1 and invoke ES.3's derivative operator'. The general χ version is not planned; the d = 2 Heegner case is HE.4, and ES.3 supplies the derivative operator it invokes. Route it with the other IX §4 items as a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.3.

items.name: IX.4: Ω′ and ind_O(c, χ^i)
items.statement: Ω′ = K′(1)_χ(μ_{p^∞}, (O_{K′}^×)^{1/p^∞}, W), and for every i, ind_O(c, χ^i) = sup{n : c_{K′}^{χ^i} ∈ 𝔭ⁿ H¹(K′, T) + H¹(K′, T)_tors} ≤ ∞, where c_{K′}^{χ^i} is the projection of c_{K′} into the subgroup H¹(K′, T)^{χ^i} on which Gal(K′/K) acts via χ^i.
items.note: χ-component analogue of Definition II.2.1. For Heegner points (d = 2) these are the ± eigenspaces under complex conjugation. Not planned in this form.

items.name: Theorem 4.3: 𝔭^{ind_O(c,χ^i)} S_{Σ_p}(K′, W*)^{χ^{1−i}} = 0
items.statement: Suppose c is a χ-anticyclotomic Euler system for T. Suppose further that H¹(Ω′/K′, W) = H¹(Ω′/K′, W*) = 0, T ⊗ k is an irreducible k[G_{K′}]-module, and there is τ ∈ G_K such that ε_cyc(τ) = χ(τ), τ^d is the identity on K′(1)_χ(μ_{p^∞}, (O_{K′}^×)^{1/p^∞}), and T/(τ − 1)T is free of rank one over O. Then for every i, 𝔭^{ind_O(c,χ^i)} S_{Σ_p}(K′, W*)^{χ^{1−i}} = 0.
items.note: Only the method is indicated (Remark 4.4): single-prime classes κ_{K′,q,M} as in Ch. V §3. This is the anticyclotomic form of Kolyvagin's annihilation of the opposite eigenspace of the Selmer group by the Heegner class. The atlas plans the Heegner endpoint through Howard/MR instead (HE.6 'a nonzero bottom class yields a rank-one compact Selmer lattice'; HE.7 for all primes), not this theorem.

items.name: Remark 4.4: φ^{fs}_q shifts χ-components: φ^{fs}_q(H¹_f(K′_q, W_M)^{χ^i}) ⊂ H¹_s(K′_q, W_M)^{χ^{i−1}}
items.statement: For rq ∈ R_{K′,M}, loc^s_q(κ_{K′,rq,M}) = φ^{fs}_q(κ_{K′,r,M}) where φ^{fs}_q : H¹_f(K′_q, W_M) → H¹_s(K′_q, W_M), with H¹_{f}(K′_q, W_M) = ⊕_{v|q} H¹_f(K′_v, W_M) and similarly for H¹_s, both Gal(K′/K)-modules. φ^{fs}_q is not Gal(K′/K)-equivariant; for q ∈ R_{K′,M}, φ^{fs}_q(H¹_f(K′_q, W_M)^{χ^i}) ⊂ H¹_s(K′_q, W_M)^{χ^{i−1}}. Hence taking r = 1 gives many classes in H¹(K′, W_M)^{χ^{i−1}} ramified at one prime of K not dividing p, with ramification expressed by c_{K′}^{χ^i}; these annihilate S_{Σ_p}(K′, W*)^{χ^{1−i}}.
items.note: 'One can show' — no proof given. For Heegner points (d = 2) this is Kolyvagin's sign rule that the derivative class for n lies in the ε·(−1)^{ω(n)} eigenspace: HE.4 'Prove ... the complex-conjugation parity'. Generic χ not planned; route it with the other IX §4 items as a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.3.

items.name: Remark 4.4: full Selmer-length bound by induction works for Heegner points using T* ≅ T
items.statement: To bound the order (not just exponent) of the components of S_{Σ_p}(K′, W*) one must induct as in Chapter V, but each step moves to a different χ-component. For the Euler system of Heegner points the induction succeeds using T* ≅ T; for d > 2 there is no obvious substitute for this self-duality.
items.note: Rubin does not formulate or prove the statement. This is Kolyvagin's structure theorem for Sha via Heegner points. HE.6: 'Give the exact direction of divisibility and the factor two from self-duality'; ES.5: 'Heegner descent can yield a square-index Sha bound through self-dual arithmetic structure'.

items.name: IX.5: S^Σ_{Σ′}(K, A) (relaxed at Σ, strict at Σ′)
items.statement: Suppose Σ and Σ′ are disjoint finite sets of places of K. If A is T, W, W_M, T*, W* or W*_M, S^Σ_{Σ′}(K, A) = ker(S^Σ(K, A) → ⊕_{v∈Σ′} H¹(K_v, A)), and similarly over finite extensions. E.g. S^Σ_{Σ′}(K, T) consists of c ∈ H¹(K, T) with c_v ∈ H¹_f(K_v, T) for v ∉ Σ ∪ Σ′, c_v = 0 for v ∈ Σ′, and no restriction for v ∈ Σ.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2: 'Define unramified, strict, relaxed and Greenberg conditions separately' and 'Prove changes of local conditions'. Library audit: Galois-cohomological Selmer groups absent. (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E29: the print lists W twice and writes H¹_f(K_v, W) in the example; both are corrected in the final version, p. 183).

items.name: Definition 5.1: Euler system trivial at Σ
items.statement: Suppose c is an Euler system for (T, 𝒦, 𝒩), and Σ is a finite set of primes of K not dividing p. c is trivial at Σ if c_F ∈ S^{Σ_p}_Σ(F, T) for every F.
items.note: Not planned (ES.2 plans smoothing and Euler-factor changes, not local triviality).

items.name: Theorem 5.2: derivative classes of an Euler system trivial at Σ lie in S^{Σ_p r}_Σ(F, W_M)
items.statement: Let Σ be a finite set of primes of K not dividing p. If c is an Euler system for T, trivial at Σ, then the derivative classes κ_{F,r,M} of Chapter IV §4 satisfy κ_{F,r,M} ∈ S^{Σ_p r}_Σ(F, W_M).
items.note: Proof: by Theorem IV.5.1 only (κ_{F,r,M})_q = 0 for q ∈ Σ is needed; the image d_q of the lift d is a lift of c in the sense of Proposition IV.6.8, as is 0 since (c_{F(r)})_q = 0, so by uniqueness d_q ∈ image(Hom(X_{F(r)}, 𝕎_M^{G_{F(r)}})), giving (κ_{F,r,M})_q = 0. Not planned.

items.name: Theorem 5.3: ℓ_O(S^Σ_{Σ_p}(K, W*)) ≤ ind_O(c) + n_W + n*_W for c trivial at Σ
items.statement: Suppose that p > 2 and that T satisfies Hyp(K, T). Let Σ be a finite set of primes of K not dividing p. If c is an Euler system for T, trivial at Σ, then ℓ_O(S^Σ_{Σ_p}(K, W*)) ≤ ind_O(c) + n_W + n*_W where n_W = ℓ_O(H¹(Ω/K, W) ∩ S^{Σ_p}_Σ(K, W)) and n*_W = ℓ_O(H¹(Ω/K, W*) ∩ S^Σ_{Σ_p}(K, W*)) (the print has S_{Σ_p}, PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E30).
items.note: Proof: identical to Theorem II.2.2 (Ch. V §2) with Theorem 5.2 in place of Theorem IV.5.1. Remarks 5.4: similar analogues for the other Ch. II theorems (S^Σ_{Σ_p}(K_∞, W*)); taking Σ large makes n_W small; corresponds to modified Euler factors in p-adic L-functions ([Gro1] §1). (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E30). Not planned.

items.name: Lemma 6.1(i),(ii): changing Euler factors f_q → g_q with f_q ≡ g_q mod N(q) − 1
items.statement: (Setting of Ch. II §1; 𝒦 abelian over K, 𝒩 divisible by p and all primes where T ramifies; Σ(F′/F) = primes of K not dividing 𝒩 which ramify in F′/K but not in F/K.) Suppose {f_q ∈ O[x] : q ∤ 𝒩} and {g_q ∈ O[x] : q ∤ 𝒩} satisfy f_q(x) ≡ g_q(x) (mod N(q) − 1) for every q, and {c̃_F ∈ H¹(F, T) : K ⊂_f F ⊂ 𝒦} satisfies Cor_{F′/F}(c̃_{F′}) = (∏_{q∈Σ(F′/F)} f_q(Fr_q^{-1})) c̃_F whenever K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F′ ⊂ 𝒦. Then there is {c_F ∈ H¹(F, T) : K ⊂_f F ⊂ 𝒦} with (i) Cor_{F′/F}(c_{F′}) = (∏_{q∈Σ(F′/F)} g_q(Fr_q^{-1})) c_F for all such F, F′; (ii) c_F = c̃_F for every finite abelian extension F of K unramified outside 𝒩.
items.note: Proof: with d_q = g_q(Fr_q^{-1}) − f_q(Fr_q^{-1}) and F_S the largest subextension of F unramified outside S and 𝒩, c_F = Σ_{S⊂Σ(F)} (∏_{q∈Σ(F)−S} d_q / [F : F_S]) (∏_{q∈S−Σ(F_S)} f_q(Fr_q^{-1})) c̃_{F_S}; the fractions lie in O[Gal(F/K)] because [F : F_S] divides ∏(N(q) − 1); (i) follows from F′_S ∩ F = F_S and ∏(d_q + f_q(Fr_q^{-1})) = ∏ g_q(Fr_q^{-1}). ES.2: 'twisting, smoothing and removal/addition of Euler factors' and 'Changes of local Euler factors induce explicit modification maps'.

items.name: Lemma 6.1(iii): χ-twisted sums of c_F and c̃_F agree
items.statement: In Lemma 6.1, if F is a finite abelian extension of K, χ is a character of Gal(F/K) of conductor 𝔣, and every prime which ramifies in F/K divides 𝒩𝔣, then Σ_{γ∈Gal(F/K)} χ(γ)γc_F = Σ_{γ∈Gal(F/K)} χ(γ)γc̃_F.
items.note: Proof: for S a proper subset of Σ(F) the conductor hypothesis gives Σ_γ χ(γ)γc̃_{F_S} = 0; (ii) is the special case. Needed so that twisted/χ-parts (used for Theorem II.2.2 applications via Definition II.4.1) are unchanged. ES.2 as for Lemma 6.1(i).

items.name: Example 6.2: f_q(x) = 1 − x, g_q(x) = 1 − q^{-1}x applied to {c̃′_F ∈ H¹(F, Z_p)}
items.statement: Suppose K = Q, f_q(x) = 1 − x and g_q(x) = 1 − q^{-1}x. Then f_q(x) ≡ g_q(x) (mod (q − 1)Z_p) for every q ≠ p. Applying Lemma 6.1 with these data to the collection {c̃′_F ∈ H¹(F, Z_p)} of Chapter III §4.1 gives an Euler system for Z_p (the print says Z_p(1), PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E31).
items.note: Used in Ch. III §4.1 (Stickelberger/Kummer classes) to build the Euler system for (Z_p, Q^{ab,b}, bp). Not planned (EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0 plans cyclotomic units, not the Z_p system).

items.name: Lemma 6.3: replacing f_q(Fr_q) by g_q(Fr_q^{-1}) with g_q(x) = u_q x^d f_q(x^{-1})
items.statement: Suppose {f_q(x) ∈ O[x, x^{-1}] : q ∤ 𝒩}, units {u_q ∈ O^× : q ∤ 𝒩}, d ∈ Z, and {c̃_F ∈ H¹(F, T) : K ⊂_f F ⊂ 𝒦} with Cor_{F′/F}(c̃_{F′}) = (∏_{q∈Σ(F′/F)} f_q(Fr_q)) c̃_F whenever K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F′ ⊂ 𝒦. Put g_q(x) = u_q x^d f_q(x^{-1}) ∈ O[x, x^{-1}]. Then there is {c_F ∈ H¹(F, T) : K ⊂_f F ⊂ 𝒦} with (i) Cor_{F′/F}(c_{F′}) = (∏_{q∈Σ(F′/F)} g_q(Fr_q^{-1})) c_F, and (ii) c_F = c̃_F for every finite extension F of K unramified outside 𝒩.
items.note: Proof: c_F = (∏_{q∈Σ(F/K)} u_q Fr_q^{-d}) c̃_F with a fixed Frobenius Fr_q ∈ Gal(K^ab/K). ES.2: 'Construct the normalization dictionary between arithmetic/geometric Frobenius and the Tate-dual convention.'

items.name: IX.6: P(Fr_q^{-1}|T; x^{-1}) = (−N(q))^{-d} det(Fr_q|T*) x^{-d} P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; N(q)x)
items.statement: With P(Fr_q^{-1}|T; x) = det(1 − Fr_q^{-1}x|T) and d = rank_O T, for every q: P(Fr_q^{-1}|T; x^{-1}) = det(1 − Fr_q^{-1}x^{-1}|T) = det(1 − N(q)^{-1}Fr_q x^{-1}|T*) = (−N(q))^{-d} det(Fr_q|T*) x^{-d} det(1 − N(q)Fr_q^{-1}x|T*).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. IX §6, Proof of Corollary 6.4, p. 144
items.note: Checked: the eigenvalues of Fr_q on T* = Hom(T, O(1)) are N(q)/α for α the eigenvalues of Fr_q on T. ES.2: 'normalization dictionary between arithmetic/geometric Frobenius and the Tate-dual convention'.

items.name: Corollary 6.4: classes with Euler factors P(Fr_q^{-1}|T; Fr_q) give an Euler system
items.statement: Suppose {c̃_F ∈ H¹(F, T) : K ⊂_f F ⊂ 𝒦} satisfies Cor_{F′/F}(c̃_{F′}) = (∏_{q∈Σ(F′/F)} P(Fr_q^{-1}|T; Fr_q)) c̃_F whenever K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F′ ⊂ 𝒦. Then there is an Euler system {c_F} for (T, 𝒦, 𝒩) such that c_F = c̃_F for every finite extension F of K unramified outside 𝒩.
items.note: Proof: Lemma 6.3 with f_q = P(Fr_q^{-1}|T; x), u_q = (−N(q))^d det(Fr_q|T*)^{-1}, then Lemma 6.1 with f_q = P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; N(q)x), g_q = P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; x). This is the step Remark 4.2 refers to ('modify the Heegner points slightly, as in §6'): the Heegner trace relation Tr P_{cℓ} = a_ℓ P_c is of this geometric-Frobenius shape. ES.2: 'removal/addition of Euler factors'; HE.2/HE.4 then consume it.

items.name: Heegner point x₁ on X₀(N)
items.statement: Let X₀(N) be the modular curve over ℚ classifying elliptic curves with a cyclic N-isogeny. Let K = ℚ(√−D) be an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant −D in which all prime factors of N are split; assume D ≠ 3, 4 so that 𝒪^× = ⟨±1⟩. Choose an ideal 𝒩 of 𝒪 with 𝒪/𝒩 ≃ ℤ/Nℤ. Viewing K ⊂ ℂ, the complex tori ℂ/𝒪 and ℂ/𝒩⁻¹ are related by a cyclic N-isogeny and so define a complex point x₁ of X₀(N); by the theory of complex multiplication x₁ is rational over K₁, the Hilbert class field of K.
items.note: HE.1 plans exactly this: "Construct CM elliptic curves and cyclic-isogeny pairs over ℂ, identify them with the existing X₀(N) moduli objects, and prove descent to ring class fields by the main theorem of complex multiplication". Rationality over K₁ is the conductor-1 case of the ring-class construction of §3. Starting datum of the whole argument.

items.name: Modular parametrization φ and Manin-type constant c
items.statement: Let E be a modular elliptic curve of conductor N over ℚ and fix a parametrization φ : X₀(N) → E mapping the cusp ∞ to the origin. There is a unique invariant differential ω on E over ℚ such that φ*(ω) is the differential Σ aₙqⁿ dq/q of the normalized (a₁ = 1) newform on X₀(N). Write ω₀ = cω with ω₀ a Néron differential on E. It is known that c is an integer, and one may assume c ≥ 1.
items.note: Parametrization: EllipticCurveModularity R29.5 "Compose the rational-cusp-normalised Abel–Jacobi map, the quotient map and this isogeny ... and that the chosen cusp maps to the identity". Integrality of c is quoted as known without reference (it is the Manin-constant integrality, Edixhoven / Mazur). c enters only Conjecture 1.2(2). The differential ω and the constant c are GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.3 ('Construct differential pullbacks and Manin constants as comparison quantities'); the integrality of c is planned by no stage.

items.name: Heegner point y_K = Tr_{K₁/K} φ(x₁)
items.statement: Let y₁ = φ(x₁) ∈ E(K₁) and define y_K = Tr_{K₁/K}(y₁) ∈ E(K), the sum of y₁ and its conjugates under the group law of E.
items.note: HE.1: "Map CM points to degree-zero Jacobian classes using a cusp ... then to A or E through the existing modular quotient ... Preserve the distinction between a trace to K and a point over its ring class field." y_K = P₁ is the bottom class of the Euler system (§4).

items.name: Dependence of y_K on 𝒩
items.statement: If 𝒩′ is another ideal with 𝒪/𝒩′ ≃ ℤ/Nℤ and y′_K is the corresponding point in E(K), then y′_K = ±y_K + (torsion). Hence the canonical height ĥ(y_K) is well defined, independent of the choice of 𝒩.
items.note: Stated without proof. HE.1: "Construct a compatible family of points P_c and show its dependence on choices is given by the specified Galois/Hecke actions and torsion translation." (The sign comes from the Fricke/Atkin–Lehner action, cf. Prop. 5.3.)

items.name: Gross–Zagier limit formula (1.1)
items.note: Cited from [GZ; Ch. I, (6.5)], not proved here. GZ.8: "Specialize to X₀(N), a rational elliptic modular quotient ... Compare trace-normalized and averaged Heegner points and the existing elliptic height." Used only to translate the analytic hypothesis into 'y_K has infinite order'.

items.name: y_K has infinite order iff L′(E/K,1) ≠ 0
items.statement: The point y_K has infinite order if and only if L′(E/K,1) ≠ 0.
items.note: Immediate from (1.1) and ĥ(P) = 0 ⇔ P torsion. GZ.8: "for a suitable nonzero test vector obtain non-torsion from a nonzero derivative using GZ.1". The height half is in the library, see g-height-zero-iff-torsion.

items.name: ĥ(y_K) ≠ 0 iff y_K of infinite order
items.statement: ĥ(y_K) ≠ 0 if and only if the point y_K has infinite order in E(K) (the equivalence used in the hypothesis of Conjecture 1.2).
items.note: TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/CanonicalHeight.lean:338 `Point.canonicalHeight_eq_zero_iff_isOfFinAddOrder [W.toAffine.IsElliptic] [Northcott (Point.canonicalHeight (W := W))] (P : W.Point) : P.canonicalHeight = 0 ↔ IsOfFinAddOrder P`; the Northcott hypothesis is discharged for number fields by the instance chain CanonicalHeight.lean:308 ← MordellWeil/NaiveHeight.lean:173 ← Mathlib NumberTheory/Height/Northcott.lean:35 and Height/NumberField.lean:426. Normalization (TauCeti's ĥ is twice some authors') does not affect vanishing.

items.name: Conjecture 1.2(1) (Gross–Zagier): rank one
items.statement: Conjecture. Assume ĥ(y_K) ≠ 0, or equivalently that y_K has infinite order in E(K). Then the group E(K) has rank 1, so the index I_K = [E(K) : ℤy_K] is finite.
items.note: From [GZ; Ch. V, 2.2]. Part (1) is exactly Kolyvagin's Theorem 1.3(1) (so no longer conjectural); HE.7 plans it: "a non-torsion Heegner point in the stated modular setting yields rank one".

items.name: Conjecture 1.2(2): exact order of Ш(E/K)
items.statement: Conjecture. Under the hypothesis of 1.2, the Tate–Shafarevich group Ш(E/K) is finite and #Ш(E/K) = (I_K / c·∏_{p|N} m_p)², where m_p = (E(ℚ_p) : E⁰(ℚ_p)).
items.note: A conjecture (BSD for E/K rewritten via (1.1)); not proved in the text. Remarks after it: I_K and c depend on φ but I_K/c does not; since c and the m_p are integers, #Ш(E/K) should divide I_K², so by the Cassels pairing Ш(E/K) should be annihilated by I_K. No stage plans this exact formula; RankZeroOneBSD BSD.5 plans only the ingredients ("Relate the height of a non-torsion Heegner point to the squared index of its class in the rank-one lattice") and BSD.6 proves p-parts under extra hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 1.3(1) (Kolyvagin): rank one
items.statement: Theorem (Kolyvagin). Assume that the point y_K has infinite order in E(K). Then the group E(K) has rank 1.
items.note: Quoted from [K1, Thm. A]; Gross proves only the weaker Prop. 2.1 (for the odd primes with GL₂ image and p ∤ y_K), which by itself gives rank 1 whenever one such p exists (e.g. E non-CM, by Serre). HE.7: "Prove the classical theorem that a non-torsion Heegner point in the stated modular setting yields rank one and finite entire Sha, including all coefficient primes." RankZeroOneBSD BSD.3 consumes it.

items.name: Theorem 1.3(2) (Kolyvagin): Ш finite with order dividing t_{E/K}·I_K²
items.statement: Theorem (Kolyvagin). Assume that the point y_K has infinite order in E(K). Then the group Ш(E/K) is finite, of order dividing t_{E/K}·(I_K)², where t_{E/K} is an integer ≥ 1 whose prime factors depend only on the curve E: they consist of 2 and the odd primes p where the Galois group of ℚ(E_p) is smaller than expected.
items.note: Quoted from [K1, Thm. A], not fully proved here. p.237 sketches the refinement: for p | y_K use that pⁿ ∤ y_K for n large; bound the p-primary part with Kolyvagin's ideal-class techniques ([R2]); when Gal(ℚ(E_p)/ℚ) ⊊ GL₂(ℤ/p) use Serre's result that Gal(ℚ(E_{pⁿ})/ℚ) has bounded index in GL₂(ℤ/pⁿ). HE.7: "Use the finite index of the non-torsion point in the rank-one Mordell–Weil lattice to prove that Sha[p∞] vanishes for all but finitely many p and has bounded exponent for each remaining p." HE.7s records that Gross's exposition covers only the clean odd-prime non-CM case. HE.6 plans the bound by the index at the primes satisfying Howard's hypotheses (p odd, p ∤ DN, G_K → GL₂(ℤ_p) surjective); the exact divisibility #Ш(E/K) | t_{E/K}·I_K² at odd full-image primes dividing ND is stated by neither HE.6 nor HE.7.

items.name: Example X₀(37)/w₃₇
items.statement: Let E = X₀(37)/w₃₇ be the curve y² + y = x³ − x and φ the modular parametrization of degree 2. Then c = 1 and m₃₇ = 1 in Conjecture 1.2(2), so one expects #Ш(E/K) = (I_K)² when y_K has infinite order. Kolyvagin shows that t_{E/K} is a power of 2 in this case, and t_{E/K} = 1 when I_K is odd. The point y_K lies in E(ℚ), which is infinite cyclic generated by P = (0,0); writing y_K = m_K·P one has I_K = ±m_K, and the integers m_K appear as Fourier coefficients of a modular form of weight 3/2 for Γ₀(4·37) [Z; §5].
items.note: Illustration that Theorem 1.3 reduces BSD to finite computation; to prove the full conjecture one must construct nontrivial elements of Ш(E/K) when I_K > 1 (cf. §11). Weight-3/2 statement cited from [Z]. RankZeroOneBSD BSD.9 plans rank-one test curves generally but not this curve or the weight-3/2 identity.

items.name: Serre: GL₂ image for p large (non-CM)
items.statement: Assume E does not have complex multiplication over ℂ (this excludes only thirteen j-invariants). Then the extension ℚ(E_p) generated by the p-division points of E has Galois group isomorphic to GL₂(ℤ/pℤ) over ℚ for all sufficiently large primes p.
items.note: Cited [S; Thm. 2]. Used to see that Prop. 2.1 applies to almost all p. HE.7: "For non-CM curves prove the required open-image/cohomological bounds and their uniformity".

items.name: Mazur: semistable curves have GL₂ image for p ≥ 11
items.statement: If E is semi-stable (i.e. N is square-free), the Galois group of ℚ(E_p)/ℚ is isomorphic to GL₂(ℤ/pℤ) for all p ≥ 11.
items.note: Cited [Ma; Thm. 4]. Not used in the proof; a source of explicit primes for Prop. 2.1. No stage plans Mazur's isogeny theorem for this use (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems explicitly avoids "the full Serre open-image theorem").

items.name: y_K is divisible by only finitely many n
items.statement: If y_K has infinite order in E(K), then, since E(K) is finitely generated, y_K is not infinitely divisible in E(K): there are only finitely many integers n such that y_K = nP with P ∈ E(K).
items.note: The 'crucial observation' of §2; it guarantees p ∤ y_K for almost all p. Input in the library: TauCeti MordellWeil/FinitelyGenerated.lean:129 `fg_point_of_numberField : AddGroup.FG W.Point` (Mordell–Weil); the divisibility corollary itself is not stated there.

items.name: Proposition 2.1(1): rank one from a p-indivisible Heegner point
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime such that the extension ℚ(E_p) has Galois group GL₂(ℤ/pℤ), and assume that p does not divide y_K in E(K). Then the group E(K) has rank 1.
items.note: Immediate from Prop. 2.3 and (2.2): dim E(K)/pE(K) = rank E(K) (no p-torsion) ≤ dim Sel(E/K)_p = 1, and y_K has infinite order since p ∤ y_K. HE.6 plans the clean version: "a nonzero bottom class yields a rank-one compact Selmer lattice" (under Howard's hypotheses, which include p ∤ D and surjectivity onto GL₂(ℤ_p); Gross needs only residual surjectivity).

items.name: Proposition 2.1(2): Ш(E/K)_p = 0
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime such that ℚ(E_p) has Galois group GL₂(ℤ/pℤ), and assume that p does not divide y_K in E(K). Then the p-torsion subgroup Ш(E/K)_p is trivial.
items.note: From Prop. 2.3 and (2.2): δy_K ≠ 0 generates Sel(E/K)_p, so the map E(K)/pE(K) → Sel(E/K)_p is onto. Consistent with Conjecture 1.2(2) because the hypotheses force p ∤ I_K. HE.6: "Identify the finite summands with Sha through the Kummer exact sequence, and prove the length bound by the index of the bottom class."

items.name: Proposition 2.1 applies to almost all p
items.statement: Assume, as throughout §2, that E does not have complex multiplication. When y_K has infinite order in E(K), Proposition 2.1 applies for almost all primes p; and the hypotheses imply that p does not divide the index I_K = [E(K) : ℤy_K].
items.note: Needs E non-CM (Serre, g-serre-open-image) together with g-yK-not-infinitely-divisible; for such E it gives rank E(K) = 1 and Ш(E/K)_p = 0 for all but finitely many p. It is the step from Prop. 2.1 toward Theorem 1.3.

items.name: p-descent exact sequence (2.2)
items.statement: The Selmer group Sel(E/K)_p sits in an exact sequence of ℤ/pℤ-vector spaces 0 → E(K)/pE(K) →^δ Sel(E/K)_p → Ш(E/K)_p → 0.
items.note: Standard. EllipticCurves Layer 7: "`0 → E(K)/mE(K) → Sel_m(E/K) → Ш(E/K)[m] → 0` from the Kummer sequence for `[m] : E → E`". The library has only the explicit 2-Selmer group (`WeierstrassCurve.Affine.selmerGroup₂`, MordellWeil/SelmerGroup.lean:104), not the cohomological Sel_p or Ш.

items.name: No p-torsion in E(K); dim E(K)/pE(K) = rank
items.statement: By the hypothesis Gal(ℚ(E_p)/ℚ) ≅ GL₂(ℤ/pℤ) (p odd), the group E(K) contains no p-torsion, and the dimension of E(K)/pE(K) over ℤ/pℤ equals the rank of E(K).
items.note: Stated without proof (a nonzero K-rational p-torsion point would give a vector fixed by an index ≤ 2 subgroup of GL₂(ℤ/p)). Strengthened in Lemma 4.3 to K_n. The rank = dimension step uses Mordell–Weil (library `fg_point_of_numberField`).

items.name: Proposition 2.3: Sel(E/K)_p is cyclic, generated by δy_K
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime such that the extension ℚ(E_p) has Galois group GL₂(ℤ/pℤ), and assume that p does not divide y_K in E(K). Then the group Sel(E/K)_p is cyclic, generated by δy_K.
items.note: The main result proved in the text (following Kolyvagin), in three steps: construct classes c(n) ∈ H¹(K,E_p) from Heegner points of conductor n (§§3–5), use Tate duality to control local components of Selmer elements (§§6–8), use Čebotarev to turn local information into an upper bound (§§9–10). Proof in §10: Claim 10.1 (Sel^{−ε} = 0) and Claim 10.3 (Sel^{ε} = ℤ/p·δy_K). Proposition 2.1 is an immediate corollary via (2.2). HE.6: "a nonzero bottom class yields a rank-one compact Selmer lattice". The §9 set-up also uses p ∤ D (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E39).

items.name: Heegner points x_n, y_n of conductor n
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1 be an integer prime to N and 𝒪ₙ = ℤ + n𝒪_K the order of index n in 𝒪_K. The ideal 𝒩ₙ = 𝒩 ∩ 𝒪ₙ is an invertible 𝒪ₙ-module with 𝒪ₙ/𝒩ₙ ≃ ℤ/Nℤ, so ℂ/𝒪ₙ with its cyclic N-isogeny to ℂ/𝒩ₙ⁻¹ defines a point xₙ ∈ X₀(N); by complex multiplication xₙ is rational over Kₙ, the ring class field of conductor n over K. Only square-free n are used, with yₙ = φ(xₙ) ∈ E(Kₙ), and every prime factor ℓ of n must satisfy (3.1) and (3.2).
items.note: HE.0 ("Construct orders O_c=ℤ+cO_K, proper invertible ideals, Pic(O_c) ... Derive ring class fields") and HE.1 ("prove descent to ring class fields by the main theorem of complex multiplication").

items.name: Galois structure of the ring class field tower
items.statement: In the tower ℚ ⊂ K ⊂ K₁ ⊂ Kₙ: Gal(K/ℚ) = ⟨1,τ⟩, Gal(K₁/K) ≅ Pic(𝒪_K), Gal(Kₙ/K₁) ≅ (𝒪_K/n𝒪_K)^×/(ℤ/nℤ)^×, and Gal(Kₙ/K) ≅ Pic(𝒪ₙ). Complex conjugation τ lifts to an involution of Kₙ and acts on Gal(Kₙ/K) by τστ⁻¹ = σ⁻¹.
items.note: Class field theory. HE.0: "Derive ring class fields and Artin maps ... including fields of definition, ramification, splitting, complex conjugation and the generalized-dihedral action. Compute the kernels of Pic(O_cℓ)→Pic(O_c)". The dihedral relation is used in Prop. 5.4 and Lemma 4.3.

items.name: Kolyvagin primes: conditions (3.1), (3.2)
items.statement: A prime ℓ is admissible (a prime factor of n) if (3.1) ℓ does not divide N·D·p — so ℓ is unramified in K(E_p) — and (3.2) Frob(ℓ) = Frob(∞) as conjugacy classes in Gal(K(E_p)/ℚ), where Frob(ℓ) is the class containing the Frobenius substitutions of the prime factors of ℓ and Frob(∞) the class of complex conjugation τ.
items.note: EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1 ("Construct the ray-class extensions K(q) ... and the squarefree-conductor category") and HE.4 ("For squarefree products n of Kolyvagin primes inert in K").

items.name: Infinitely many Kolyvagin primes (Čebotarev)
items.statement: There are infinitely many primes ℓ satisfying (3.2), by Čebotarev's density theorem.
items.note: Chebotarev roadmap Layer 10 derives "infinitude of every Frobenius class" from `hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet`; the library has only the Frobenius-prime-set infrastructure (TauCeti NumberTheory/Chebotarev/FrobeniusPrimeSet.lean), not the density theorem. HE.5: "Prove auxiliary-prime existence by Chebotarev applied to the actual residual representation".

items.name: Kolyvagin primes: ℓ inert in K and a_ℓ ≡ ℓ+1 ≡ 0 (mod p) (3.3)
items.statement: If ℓ satisfies (3.2), then Frob(ℓ) = τ in Gal(K/ℚ), so (ℓ) stays inert in K (let λ be its unique prime factor). The condition Frob(ℓ) = Frob(∞) in Gal(ℚ(E_p)/ℚ) is equivalent to the congruences a_ℓ ≡ ℓ + 1 ≡ 0 (mod p), where ℓ + 1 − a_ℓ = #Ẽ(𝔽_ℓ): the characteristic polynomial of Frob(ℓ) on E_p is x² − a_ℓx + ℓ, and that of Frob(∞) = τ is x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1).
items.note: The Frobenius characteristic polynomial is planned in ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6 ("Prove rank, continuity, Weil-pairing determinant, oddness over Q, and the good-reduction Frobenius polynomial"). The converse direction silently uses p odd, so that ±1 are distinct eigenvalues and Frob(ℓ) is semisimple.

items.name: Ẽ(F_λ)_p ≃ (ℤ/p)² with one-dimensional ± eigenspaces (3.4)
items.statement: Let F_λ be the residue field of K at λ (ℓ² elements). By (3.2), λ splits completely in K(E_p), so Ẽ(F_λ)_p ≃ (ℤ/pℤ)²; more precisely Ẽ(F_λ)^±_p ≃ ℤ/pℤ, where ± denotes eigenspaces for ⟨1,τ⟩. Here Ẽ(F_λ)⁺ has order ℓ + 1 − a_ℓ and Ẽ(F_λ)⁻ has order ℓ + 1 + a_ℓ, both divisible by p by (3.3).
items.note: Local input for the finite/singular comparison (Props. 6.2(2) and 8.1). The point count #Ẽ(𝔽_ℓ) = ℓ + 1 − a_ℓ is EllipticCurves Layer 3 (`frobeniusTrace`); the eigenspace statement is HE.5 (node HE.5/finite-singular-comparison-and-the-corrected-kolyvagin-system: 'the action of Fr_ℓ splits the p-Sylow subgroup of Ẽ(F) into cyclic eigencomponents whose lengths are the p-orders of ℓ + 1 − a_ℓ and ℓ + 1 + a_ℓ').

items.name: Gₙ = Gal(Kₙ/K₁) ≅ ∏ G_ℓ with G_ℓ cyclic of order ℓ+1
items.statement: For square-free n = ∏ℓ let Gₙ = Gal(Kₙ/K₁). Then Gₙ ≃ ∏_{ℓ|n} G_ℓ, where G_ℓ is the subgroup fixing K_{n/ℓ}; the subgroups G_ℓ ≃ F_λ^×/F_ℓ^× are cyclic of order ℓ + 1. Fix a generator σ_ℓ of G_ℓ; the augmentation ideal of ℤ[G_ℓ] is principal, generated by σ_ℓ − 1.
items.note: HE.0: "Compute the kernels of Pic(O_cℓ)→Pic(O_c) and extension degrees with the exceptional unit indices retained; ℓ+1 is only the inert, prime-to-conductor, ordinary-unit case" (the unit hypothesis D ≠ 3,4 is what makes the order exactly ℓ + 1).

items.name: Kolyvagin derivative operators D_ℓ, Dₙ (3.5)
items.statement: Let Tr_ℓ = Σ_{σ∈G_ℓ} σ ∈ ℤ[G_ℓ] and let D_ℓ be a solution in ℤ[G_ℓ] of (σ_ℓ − 1)·D_ℓ = ℓ + 1 − Tr_ℓ. D_ℓ is well defined up to adding elements of ℤ·Tr_ℓ (Kolyvagin uses D_ℓ⁰ = Σ_{i=1}^{ℓ} i·σ_ℓ^i). Define Dₙ = ∏_{ℓ|n} D_ℓ in ℤ[Gₙ].
items.note: ES.3: "Construct the cyclic group-ring norm N_q and derivative D_q, prove (sigma_q−1)D_q=|G_q|−N_q". The printed second expression for D_ℓ⁰ is off by a multiple of Tr_ℓ (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E33).

items.name: Proposition 3.6: [Dₙyₙ] is Gₙ-invariant mod p
items.statement: The point Dₙyₙ in E(Kₙ) gives a class [Dₙyₙ] in E(Kₙ)/pE(Kₙ) which is fixed by Gₙ.
items.note: Proof: it suffices that (σ_ℓ − 1)Dₙyₙ ∈ pE(Kₙ) for ℓ | n; with n = ℓm, (σ_ℓ − 1)Dₙyₙ = (ℓ + 1)D_m yₙ − D_m(Tr_ℓ yₙ), and ℓ + 1 ≡ 0, Tr_ℓ yₙ = a_ℓ y_m with a_ℓ ≡ 0 (mod p) (Prop. 3.7(1), (3.3)). HE.4: "Prove invariance of the differentiated Kummer class modulo that ideal".

items.name: Proposition 3.7(1): norm relation Tr_ℓ yₙ = a_ℓ y_m
items.statement: Let n = ℓ·m. Then Tr_ℓ yₙ = a_ℓ·y_m in E(K_m).
items.note: Proof: Tr_ℓ xₙ = T_ℓ(x_m) as divisors of degree ℓ + 1 on X₀(N) over K_m [G; §6] (T_ℓ the self-dual Hecke correspondence of bidegree ℓ + 1), and φ(T_ℓ d) = a_ℓ·φ(d) for any divisor d. HE.2: "For inert ℓ prime to cN prove the trace relation with a_ℓP_c".

items.name: Tr_ℓ xₙ = T_ℓ(x_m) and φ∘T_ℓ = a_ℓ·φ
items.statement: For n = ℓm: Tr_ℓ xₙ = T_ℓ(x_m) as an equality of divisors of degree ℓ + 1 on X₀(N) over K_m, where T_ℓ is the Hecke correspondence (self-dual of bidegree ℓ + 1); and φ(T_ℓ d) = a_ℓ·φ(d) for any divisor d on X₀(N).
items.note: First part cited from [G; §6]. HE.2: "Compute Hecke correspondences on CM points by classifying the local cyclic subgroups/optimal embeddings"; Hecke correspondences themselves in ModularCurvesPartII R14.1 ("Construct the isogeny correspondences at good and bad primes").

items.name: Proposition 3.7(2): yₙ ≡ Frob(λ_m)(y_m) (mod λₙ)
items.statement: Let n = ℓ·m. Each prime factor λₙ of ℓ in Kₙ divides a unique prime λ_m of K_m, and yₙ ≡ Frob(λ_m)(y_m) (mod λₙ).
items.note: Proof: λ splits completely in K_m/K (principal, generated by ℓ prime to m); λ_m = (λₙ)^{ℓ+1} is totally ramified in Kₙ, F_{λₙ} ≅ F_λ with ℓ² elements. The points of T_ℓ(x_m) are the K_m-conjugates of xₙ, all ≡ xₙ mod λₙ; by the Eichler–Shimura congruence T_ℓ ≡ Fr_ℓ + Fr_ℓ′ (mod ℓ) one of them is ≡ Frob(λ_m)(x_m), hence all are (also since α^ℓ ≡ α^{1/ℓ} in F_{ℓ²}). HE.2: "At primes above an inert auxiliary ℓ prove the reduction congruence relating P_cℓ to Frobenius on P_c".

items.name: Splitting of λ in K_m and total ramification in Kₙ
items.statement: For n = ℓm with ℓ as in (3.1)–(3.2): the prime λ = (ℓ) of K splits completely in K_m/K (it is principal, generated by an integer ℓ prime to m); the factors λ_m of λ in K_m are totally ramified in Kₙ: λ_m = (λₙ)^{ℓ+1}; the residue field F_{λₙ} has ℓ² elements and is canonically isomorphic to F_λ.
items.note: Class field theory for ring class fields. HE.0: "Derive ring class fields and Artin maps ... including fields of definition, ramification, splitting".

items.name: Eichler–Shimura congruence relation
items.statement: T_ℓ ≡ Fr_ℓ + Fr_ℓ′ (mod ℓ) (as correspondences on X₀(N) in characteristic ℓ, ℓ ∤ N).
items.note: Quoted without reference. HE.2: "Establish the Eichler–Shimura relation used in the proof in the appropriate geometric category."

items.name: {yₙ} is an Euler system; [Dₙyₙ] is independent of the D_ℓ choices
items.statement: The two properties of Proposition 3.7 make the collection {yₙ} an 'Euler system' in Kolyvagin's sense [K1; §1]. Since Tr_ℓ yₙ = a_ℓ y_m lies in pE(Kₙ), the class [Dₙyₙ] in E(Kₙ)/pE(Kₙ) does not depend on the choice of solutions D_ℓ of (3.5); it depends on the choice of generators σ_ℓ of G_ℓ only up to scaling by (ℤ/pℤ)^×.
items.note: HE.4: "Include the tensor of cyclic Galois groups in the coefficient of the Kolyvagin system, so changing a chosen generator has a proved transformation law." ES.2 plans the abstract Euler-system notion.

items.name: The points Pₙ (4.1)
items.statement: Let 𝒢ₙ = Gal(Kₙ/K), which sits in an exact sequence 0 → Gₙ → 𝒢ₙ → Gal(K₁/K) → 0. Let S be a set of coset representatives for Gₙ in 𝒢ₙ and define Pₙ = Σ_{σ∈S} σ(Dₙyₙ) in E(Kₙ). By Prop. 3.6 the class [Pₙ] ∈ E(Kₙ)/pE(Kₙ) is fixed by 𝒢ₙ. The same S is used to define P_m for m | n; P₁ = Σ_{σ∈S} σy₁ = Tr_{K₁/K}(y₁) = y_K. The class [Pₙ] is independent of S and depends on the generators σ_ℓ only up to scaling by (ℤ/pℤ)^×.
items.note: HE.4: "At n=1 recover the Kummer image of the trace P_1."

items.name: Diagram (4.2); Res : H¹(K,E_p) ≅ H¹(Kₙ,E_p)^{𝒢ₙ}
items.statement: From 0 → E_p → E →^p E → 0 one gets a commutative diagram (4.2) whose rows 0 → E(K)/pE(K) →^δ H¹(K,E_p) → H¹(K,E)_p → 0 and 0 → (E(Kₙ)/pE(Kₙ))^{𝒢ₙ} →^{δₙ} H¹(Kₙ,E_p)^{𝒢ₙ} → H¹(Kₙ,E)_p^{𝒢ₙ} are exact, with right column 0 → H¹(Kₙ/K,E)_p →^{Inf} H¹(K,E)_p →^{Res} H¹(Kₙ,E)_p^{𝒢ₙ} exact. The restriction H¹(K,E_p) → H¹(Kₙ,E_p)^{𝒢ₙ} is an isomorphism: its kernel is H¹(Kₙ/K,E_p(Kₙ)) and its cokernel injects into H²(Kₙ/K,E_p(Kₙ)) (Hochschild–Serre transgression), both trivial by Lemma 4.3.
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2 ("Identify the low-degree sequence with the existing inflation–restriction maps") and HE.4 ("then descend it to K using the actual inflation–restriction sequence").

items.name: Lemma 4.3: no p-torsion over Kₙ
items.statement: (p odd, Gal(ℚ(E_p)/ℚ) ≅ GL₂(ℤ/pℤ).) The curve E has no p-torsion rational over Kₙ.
items.note: Proof: otherwise E_p(Kₙ) = ℤ/p or (ℤ/p)². The first gives a cyclic subgroup scheme over ℚ (Kₙ is Galois over ℚ), putting Gal(ℚ(E_p)/ℚ) in a Borel; the second gives ℚ(E_p) ⊂ Kₙ and a surjection onto GL₂(ℤ/pℤ), impossible for p > 2 since GL₂(ℤ/pℤ) is not a quotient of a group of 'dihedral' type. HE.4: "If torsion invariants obstruct injectivity or uniqueness, retain them"; dihedral images in R01.4. The printed surjection has the wrong source group (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E34).

items.name: Kolyvagin class c(n) (4.4)
items.statement: Let c(n) be the unique class in H¹(K,E_p) such that Res c(n) = δₙ[Pₙ] in H¹(Kₙ,E_p)^{𝒢ₙ}.
items.note: Well defined by the restriction isomorphism of (4.2). HE.4: "construct the finite quotient coefficient ideal ... Prove invariance of the differentiated Kummer class ... then descend it to K".

items.name: Classes d(n) and d̃(n) (4.5)
items.statement: Let d(n) be the image of c(n) in H¹(K,E)_p. Since Res d(n) = 0 (commutativity of (4.2) and exactness of the bottom row), there is a unique class d̃(n) in H¹(Kₙ/K,E)_p = H¹(𝒢ₙ,E(Kₙ))_p with Inf d̃(n) = d(n) in H¹(K,E)_p.
items.note: d(n) is the class whose local behaviour (§6) drives the argument. HE.4.

items.name: McCallum's explicit cocycles (4.6)
items.statement: The class c(n) is represented by the 1-cocycle f(σ) = σ((1/p)Pₙ) − (1/p)Pₙ − ((σ − 1)Pₙ)/p on Gal(K̄/K), where (1/p)Pₙ is a fixed p-th root of Pₙ in E(K̄) and ((σ − 1)Pₙ)/p is the unique p-th root of (σ − 1)Pₙ in E(Kₙ) (which exists by Lemma 4.3). The class d̃(n) is represented by the 1-cocycle f̃(σ) = −((σ − 1)Pₙ)/p on 𝒢ₙ.
items.note: Attributed to W. McCallum. Used in Prop. 6.2(2) to compute d(n)_λ. HE.4.

items.name: Proposition 4.7(1): c(n) = 0 iff Pₙ ∈ pE(Kₙ)
items.statement: The class c(n) is trivial in H¹(K,E_p) if and only if Pₙ ∈ pE(Kₙ).
items.note: Proof: from the definitions and (4.2). HE.4.

items.name: Proposition 4.7(2): d(n) = 0 iff Pₙ ∈ pE(Kₙ) + E(K)
items.statement: The class d(n) is trivial in H¹(K,E)_p, and the class d̃(n) is trivial in H¹(Kₙ/K,E)_p, if and only if Pₙ ∈ pE(Kₙ) + E(K).
items.note: Proof: from the definitions and (4.2). Refined by Corollary 5.5. HE.4.

items.name: Note: c(1) and d(1)
items.statement: The class c(1) is trivial if and only if P₁ = y_K is divisible by p in E(K), and the classes d(1) and d̃(1) are always globally trivial.
items.note: c(1) = δy_K. HE.4: "At n=1 recover the Kummer image of the trace P_1."

items.name: Fricke eigenvalue ε and the sign of the functional equation (5.2)
items.statement: Let ε = ±1 be the eigenvalue of the Fricke involution w_N on the eigenform f = Σaₙqⁿ associated to E: f|w_N = ε·f. Then the L-function of E over ℚ satisfies a functional equation with sign −ε.
items.note: Standard, stated without proof. RankZeroOneBSD BSD.0: "Build the interface from the Euler product/Dirichlet series of E to its modular entire continuation and completed functional equation". The Fricke operator on modular forms exists in TauCeti (e.g. `TauCeti.frickeOperator_mem_modFormCharSpace`, NumberTheory/ModularForms/Fricke/CharacterSpace.lean:88), but not the sign relation. Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 6 pins 'The sign of the functional equation is i^k·ε_N' and Layer 7 derives the one-form functional equation with sign i^k·ε; for weight 2 this is −ε.

items.name: Proposition 5.3: complex conjugation on yₙ
items.statement: We have yₙ^τ = ε·yₙ^{σ′} + (torsion) in E(Kₙ), for some σ′ ∈ 𝒢ₙ.
items.note: Proof: from xₙ^τ = w_N(xₙ^{σ′}) for some σ′ ∈ 𝒢ₙ [G, §5], so (xₙ − ∞)^τ = w_N(xₙ − ∞)^{σ′} + (w_N∞ − ∞); w_N∞ is the cusp 0 and the class of (0 − ∞) is torsion in the Jacobian. HE.4: "the complex-conjugation parity".

items.name: Proposition 5.4(1): sign of [Pₙ] under τ
items.statement: The class [Pₙ] lies in the εₙ = ε·(−1)^{fₙ} eigenspace for τ in (E(Kₙ)/pE(Kₙ))^{𝒢ₙ}, where fₙ = #{ℓ : ℓ | n}.
items.note: Proof: τσ = σ⁻¹τ gives τPₙ = Σ σ⁻¹τDₙyₙ; applying τ to (σ_ℓ − 1)D_ℓ = ℓ + 1 − Tr_ℓ gives τD_ℓ = −σ_ℓD_ℓτ + kTr_ℓτ (k = ℓ for D_ℓ⁰; the text prints '+ kTr_ℓ', a misprint recorded by this review); Tr_ℓ yₙ ≡ 0 mod p; then Prop. 5.3 and Lemma 4.3 give τPₙ ≡ εₙ·Pₙ mod pE(Kₙ). For n = 1 it puts y_K in the ε-eigenspace, which §10 uses. HE.4 ("the complex-conjugation parity").

items.name: Proposition 5.4(2): sign of c(n), d(n)
items.statement: The class c(n) lies in the εₙ-eigenspace for τ in H¹(K,E_p), and the class d(n) lies in the εₙ-eigenspace for τ in H¹(K,E)_p (where H¹(K,E_p) = H¹(K,E_p)⁺ ⊕ H¹(K,E_p)⁻ since p is odd, (5.1)).
items.note: Immediate from (1): all maps in (4.2) commute with Gal(K/ℚ) = ⟨1,τ⟩. HE.4.

items.name: Corollary 5.5: d(n) = 0 iff Pₙ ∈ pE(Kₙ) + E(K)^{εₙ}
items.statement: The class d(n) is trivial in H¹(K,E)_p^{εₙ} if and only if Pₙ ∈ pE(Kₙ) + E(K)^{εₙ}.
items.note: Refinement of Prop. 4.7(2) using d(n) ∈ H¹(K,E)_p^{εₙ}. HE.4.

items.name: Ш(E/K)_p and Sel(E/K)_p (6.1)
items.statement: Ш(E/K)_p = ker(H¹(K,E)_p → ⊕_v H¹(K_v,E)_p), the sum over all places v of K. The Selmer group Sel(E/K)_p is the largest subgroup of H¹(K,E_p) which maps to Ш(E/K)_p in H¹(K,E)_p.
items.note: EllipticCurves Layer 7: "the Shafarevich–Tate group `Ш(E/K)` for the module `E(Kˢᵉᵖ)`, cut out by everywhere-local triviality". Remark: δₙ[Pₙ] lies in the Selmer group of E over Kₙ and is 𝒢ₙ-fixed, but restriction need not induce Sel(E/K)_p ≅ Sel(E/Kₙ)_p^{𝒢ₙ}, so whether c(n) is Selmer is decided locally (§6).

items.name: Proposition 6.2(1): d(n) is locally trivial away from n
items.statement: The class d(n)_v is locally trivial in H¹(K_v,E)_p at the archimedean place v = ∞, and at all finite places v of K which do not divide n.
items.note: Proof: v = ∞: K_v = ℂ. v ∤ n: d(n) is inflated from d̃(n) on Kₙ/K, which is unramified at v, so d(n)_v ∈ H¹(K_v^{un}/K_v,E), which is 0 for good reduction [M; Ch. I, §3]. v | N: H¹(K_v^{un}/K_v,E) injects into H¹(F_v,Φ) (Φ = E/E⁰ the component group) [M; Ch. I, Prop. 3.8]; the Heegner divisor (xₙ) − (∞) lies in J⁰ up to translation by the rational torsion point (0) − (∞) [GZ; III, 3.1], so yₙ ∈ E⁰ up to rational torsion; as E(ℚ)_p = 0, Pₙ lies in a subgroup E′ with (E′ : E⁰) prime to p, so d(n)_v = 0. HE.3: "At bad primes identify the local Kummer image and the precise component-group obstruction"; HE.5.

items.name: Proposition 6.2(2): d(n)_λ = 0 iff P_m ∈ pE(K_λ)
items.statement: If n = ℓm and λ is the unique prime of K dividing ℓ, the class d(n)_λ is locally trivial in H¹(K_λ,E)_p if and only if P_m ∈ pE(K_{λ_m}) = pE(K_λ) for one (and hence all) places λ_m of K_m dividing λ.
items.note: Proof: d(n)_λ is represented by σ ↦ ((σ−1)Pₙ)/p on Gal(K_{λₙ}/K_{λ_m}) ≅ G_ℓ; since E¹ is pro-ℓ, H¹(G_ℓ,E¹(K_{λₙ}))_p = 0, so d(n)_λ is trivial iff its image in Hom(G_ℓ,Ẽ(F_λ)_p) vanishes, i.e. iff Qₙ = ((σ_ℓ − 1)Pₙ)/p has trivial reduction mod λₙ; then the congruence of g-Qn-congruence and the ε_m-eigenspace argument. HE.5: "Use HE.2's reduction congruence to prove the finite/singular relation at every auxiliary prime".

items.name: Qₙ ≡ ((ℓ+1)Frob(λ_m) − a_ℓ)/p · P_m (mod λₙ)
items.statement: With n = ℓm and Qₙ = ((σ_ℓ − 1)Pₙ)/p: Qₙ = Σ_S σD_m(((ℓ+1)/p)yₙ − (a_ℓ/p)y_m), and ((ℓ+1)/p)yₙ − (a_ℓ/p)y_m ≡ (((ℓ+1)Frob(λ_m) − a_ℓ)/p) y_m (mod λₙ) at all places λₙ over λ; conjugating (using σ·Frob(σ⁻¹λ_m) = Frob(λ_m)·σ), Qₙ ≡ (((ℓ+1)(Frob λ_m) − a_ℓ)/p)·P_m (mod λₙ). The reduction P̃_m lies in the ε_m-eigenspace for Frob(ℓ) on Ẽ(F_λ)/pẼ(F_λ); since (ℓ+1)Frob(ℓ) − a_ℓ annihilates Ẽ(F_λ) and the ε_m-eigenspace of p-torsion is cyclic, Q̃ₙ = 0 iff P̃_m ∈ pẼ(F_λ), which (E¹ being p-divisible) is equivalent to P_m ∈ pE(K_{λ_m}).
items.note: The finite/singular comparison that ties the local class at λ to the next-lower class. Uses Props. 3.7(1),(2) and (3.4). ES.1: "Construct the finite–singular comparison including its cyclic-group tensor factor"; HE.5.

items.name: Note: the class d(ℓ) for n = ℓ prime
items.statement: d(1) is globally trivial, hence locally trivial everywhere, in accordance with Prop. 6.2(1). For n = ℓ prime: d(ℓ) is globally trivial iff P_ℓ ∈ pE(K_ℓ) + E(K) (Prop. 4.7); d(ℓ) is locally trivial at all places v ≠ λ of K, and locally trivial at λ iff P₁ = y_K ∈ pE(K_λ) (Prop. 6.2).
items.note: The worked example of 6.2; it is the case used in Claim 10.1. HE.5.

items.name: Unramified Kummer image (7.1)
items.statement: Let K_λ be a local field with ring of integers 𝒪_λ and finite residue field F_λ of characteristic ℓ, E/K_λ an elliptic curve with good reduction over 𝒪_λ, and p ≠ ℓ a prime. Then E_p is a finite étale group scheme of rank p² over 𝒪_λ, and the Kummer sequence induces an isomorphism E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ) ≅^δ H¹(𝒪_λ,E_p), as H¹(𝒪_λ,E) = 0. Since E¹(K_λ) is p-divisible (it is a pro-ℓ group and p ≠ ℓ), E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ) ≅ Ẽ(F_λ)/pẼ(F_λ), so has dimension ≤ 2 over ℤ/pℤ, with equality if all the p-torsion of E is rational over K_λ.
items.note: Standard (cited [T, §2], [M, Ch. I]). 'ℓ-divisible' should read 'p-divisible' (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E35). No stage explicitly plans the unramified local condition for elliptic curves at p ≠ ℓ; nearest are EllipticCurves Layer 7 ("unramified local cohomology" among missing interfaces) and SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1 ("calculate their unramified/bad-prime comparison terms").

items.name: Local Tate pairing on H¹(K_λ,E_p) (7.2)–(7.3)
items.statement: The Weil pairing {,} : E_p × E_p → μ_p induces a cup-product pairing H¹(K_λ,E_p) × H¹(K_λ,E_p) → H²(K_λ,μ_p); the invariant map gives H²(K_λ,μ_p) = Br(K_λ)_p ≅ (1/p)ℤ/ℤ = ℤ/pℤ, and (Tate's local duality theorem) the resulting pairing ⟨,⟩ : H¹(K_λ,E_p) × H¹(K_λ,E_p) → ℤ/pℤ is non-degenerate. It is symmetric: the text calls it alternating, which is false for odd p (new source issue on (7.3) recorded by this review).
items.note: Cited [M, Ch. I, Cor. 2.3]. ClassFieldTheory Layer 5: "Construct local Tate duality from the evaluation pairing `Hom(A,μ_n) × A → μ_n`. The exported theorem `tateDualityPairing_perfect_mixed`" (not yet in the library); Weil pairing in EllipticCurves Layer 2 ("`e_N : E[N] × E[N] → μ_N` ... alternating, nondegenerate").

items.name: Local Kummer sequence (7.4); the unramified image is isotropic
items.statement: The Kummer sequence gives a short exact sequence 0 → E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ) → H¹(K_λ,E_p) → H¹(K_λ,E)_p → 0, and the subspace E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ) ≅ H¹(𝒪_λ,E_p) is isotropic for ⟨,⟩, as H²(𝒪_λ,μ_p) = 0.
items.note: Standard local fact. It is half of Prop. 7.5 (g-prop-7.5) and the unramified special case of Rubin I.4.3(ii) (r1-prop-4.3ii-orthogonal-WM, planned at ES.0 and L1); HE.6's verification of Howard's H.4 ('F is its own exact orthogonal complement ... at every v') covers it for T_p(E).

items.name: Proposition 7.5: local pairing E(K_λ)/p × H¹(K_λ,E)_p → ℤ/p
items.statement: The pairing ⟨,⟩ of (7.3) induces a non-degenerate pairing of ℤ/pℤ-vector spaces (of dimension ≤ 2) ⟨,⟩ : E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ) × H¹(K_λ,E)_p → ℤ/pℤ.
items.note: Proof: H¹(𝒪_λ,E_p) must be maximal isotropic, i.e. dim H¹(K_λ,E)_p = dim E(K_λ)_p (g-local-H1-dimension). The pairing identifies E(K_λ)/p with the dual of H¹(K_λ,E)_p, i.e. Tate local duality for E. SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1 ("identifying the actual annihilator of each chosen local condition"); ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 for the underlying duality.

items.name: dim H¹(K_λ,E)_p = dim E(K_λ)_p; H¹(K_λ,E)_p ≅ Hom(μ_p,E_p)^{Frob(λ)}
items.statement: For E with good reduction at λ and p ≠ ℓ: restriction gives H¹(K_λ,E)_p ≅ H¹(K_λ^{un},E)_p^{Frob(λ)} (since H¹(K_λ^{un}/K_λ,E) = H¹(𝒪_λ,E) = 0) ≅ H¹(K_λ^{un},E_p)^{Frob(λ)} (E(K_λ^{un}) p-divisible) = Hom(Gal(K̄_λ/K_λ^{un}),E_p)^{Frob(λ)} ≅ Hom(μ_p,E_p)^{Frob(λ)} (the homomorphism kills wild inertia and factors through ℤ_p(1) = T_p𝔾_m); this has the same dimension as Ẽ(F_λ)_p ≃ E(K_λ)_p, by the Weil pairing.
items.note: A general theorem of Tate [T, §2] ([M, Ch. I, Thm. 2.6]); Gross gives this tame proof. The isomorphism is the singular-quotient description of Rubin I.3.2(ii) and I.4.7(i) (items r1-lem-3.2ii-singular-quotient, r1-lem-4.7i-finite-singular-iso), planned at SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1 and EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1.

items.name: Kolyvagin's formula for the local pairing (7.6)
items.statement: Assume the p-torsion of E is rational over K_λ (so the spaces of Prop. 7.5 have dimension 2). For c₁ ∈ E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ) let e₁ = ((1/p)c₁)^{Frob(λ)−1} ∈ E(K_λ)_p; for c₂ ∈ H¹(K_λ,E_p) let φ₂ : μ_p → E_p(K_λ) be the associated homomorphism (tame local class field theory), fix a primitive p-th root of unity ζ ∈ K_λ^× and put e₂ = φ₂(ζ). Then ζ^{⟨c₁,c₂⟩} = {e₁,e₂}, where {,} is the Weil pairing on E_p.
items.note: Due to Kolyvagin; proof in the appendix of [W]. Gives an independent proof of non-degeneracy; used only as an alternative in Prop. 8.1(2). It is Rubin's Lemma I.4.7(ii) for T = T_pE and M = p (r1-lem-4.7ii-pairing-compatibility, planned at ES.1), where Rubin leaves the sign unspecified.

items.name: Proposition 8.1(1): ± eigenspaces are lines
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, λ = (ℓ) an inert prime, K_λ the completion, E defined over ℚ so that Gal(K_λ/ℚ_ℓ) = ⟨1,τ⟩ acts; assume p odd and a_ℓ ≡ ℓ + 1 ≡ 0 (mod p) (3.3), and that the p-torsion of E is rational over K_λ. Then the eigenspaces (E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ))^± and H¹(K_λ,E)_p^± for Gal(K_λ/ℚ_ℓ) each have dimension 1 over ℤ/pℤ.
items.note: Proof: E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ) ≅ E(K_λ)_p and H¹(K_λ,E)_p ≅ Hom(μ_p(K_λ),E(K_λ)_p) as Gal(K_λ/ℚ_ℓ)-modules; since ℓ + 1 ≡ 0, μ_p(K_λ) = μ_p(K_λ)⁻, so E(K_λ)_p^± ≃ (E(K_λ)/p)^± ≃ H¹(K_λ,E)_p^∓, and (3.4). Not explicitly planned; HE.5 plans "the twisted conjugation pairing required by Howard's Heegner version".

items.name: Proposition 8.1(2): the ± local pairings are perfect
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of 8.1(1), the pairing ⟨,⟩ induces non-degenerate pairings of ℤ/pℤ-vector spaces ⟨,⟩^± : (E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ))^± × H¹(K_λ,E)_p^± → ℤ/pℤ. In particular, if d_λ ≠ 0 lies in H¹(K_λ,E)_p^± and s_λ ∈ (E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ))^± satisfies ⟨s_λ,d_λ⟩ = 0, then s_λ ≡ 0 (mod pE(K_λ)).
items.note: Proof: the + and − eigenspaces are orthogonal, because ⟨c₁^τ,c₂^τ⟩ = ⟨c₁,c₂⟩ (τ acts trivially on H²(K_λ,μ_p) = ℤ/p) and p is odd; alternatively via the Weil pairing and (7.6). The text cites 'the pairing ⟨,⟩ of (2.3)', meaning (7.3) (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E36). HE.5: "Verify the self-dual/cartesian local-condition hypotheses and the twisted conjugation pairing".

items.name: Proposition 8.2: a class ramified only at λ kills Selmer classes at λ
items.statement: Assume the class d ∈ H¹(K,E)_p^± is locally trivial for all places v ≠ λ of K, but that d_λ ≠ 0 in H¹(K_λ,E)_p^±. Then for any class s in the subgroup Sel(E/K)_p^± ⊂ H¹(K,E_p)^± we have s_λ = Res_{K_λ}(s) = 0 in H¹(K_λ,E_p)^±.
items.note: Proof: s_λ ∈ (E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ))^± by the Selmer condition, so by 8.1 it suffices that ⟨s_λ,d_λ⟩ = 0. Lift d to c ∈ H¹(K,E_p); the global cup product ⟨s,c⟩_K ∈ H²(K,μ_p) = Br(K)_p is determined by its local components; ⟨s_v,c_v⟩ = 0 for v ≠ λ since d_v = 0 (both classes then lie in the isotropic Kummer image); by the reciprocity law (sum of local invariants is zero) ⟨s_λ,c_λ⟩ = ⟨s_λ,d_λ⟩ = 0. Uses 'the full power of global class field theory'. ClassFieldTheory Layer 10 (`sumLocalInv`, `eq_zero_of_localInv_eq_zero`); ES.4: "Apply Poitou–Tate to strict/relaxed modifications".

items.name: Set-up of §9: L = K(E_p), 𝒢 ≅ GL₂(ℤ/p), homotheties Z
items.statement: Assume p odd and Gal(ℚ(E_p)/ℚ) ≅ GL₂(ℤ/pℤ) ≃ Aut(E_p). Let L = K(E_p) and 𝒢 = Gal(L/K). The only quadratic subfield of ℚ(E_p) is ℚ(√((−1)^{(p−1)/2}p)), so K and ℚ(E_p) are disjoint and 𝒢 ≅ GL₂(ℤ/pℤ) unless D = p; if D = p, 𝒢 is the index-2 subgroup of elements of square determinant. In either case 𝒢 contains SL₂(ℤ/pℤ) and the central subgroup Z ≃ (ℤ/pℤ)^× of homotheties of E_p. Since #Z = p − 1 is prime to p, Hⁿ(Z,E_p) = 0 for n ≥ 1; since p is odd, Z ≠ 1 and E_p^Z = H⁰(Z,E_p) = 0.
items.note: The text says 'the hypothesis that D is prime to Np implies that the numberfields K and Q(E_p) are disjoint'; p ∤ D is not among the stated hypotheses of Props. 2.1/2.3, and disjointness fails exactly when D = p (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E39). The statement above is the corrected one. The vanishing via the homotheties is planned in HE.6 (node HE.6/clean-rank-one-descent-theorem-A, verification of H.2 'applied to the diagonally embedded μ_{p−1}').

items.name: Proposition 9.1: Hⁿ(𝒢,E_p) = 0 and restriction to L
items.statement: We have Hⁿ(𝒢,E_p) = 0 for all n ≥ 0. Restriction gives an isomorphism of Gal(K/ℚ)-modules Res : H¹(K,E_p) ≅ H¹(L,E_p)^𝒢 = Hom_𝒢(Gal(ℚ̄/L),E_p(L)).
items.note: Proof (attributed to Serre): the spectral sequence H^m(𝒢/Z,Hⁿ(Z,E_p)) ⇒ H^{m+n}(𝒢,E_p) with Hⁿ(Z,E_p) = 0 for all n ≥ 0; kernel of restriction is H¹(𝒢,E_p), cokernel injects into H²(𝒢,E_p). Hochschild–Serre is ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2 ("Build the spectral sequence for a closed normal subgroup").

items.name: The pairing [,] : H¹(K,E_p) × Gal(ℚ̄/L) → E_p(L) (9.2)
items.statement: From Prop. 9.1 one obtains a pairing [,] : H¹(K,E_p) × Gal(ℚ̄/L) → E_p(L), satisfying [s^σ,ρ^σ] = [s,ρ^σ] = [s,ρ]^σ for all s ∈ H¹(K,E_p), ρ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/L), σ ∈ 𝒢 = Gal(L/K). If [s,ρ] = 0 for all ρ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/L), then s ≡ 0 (injectivity of restriction).
items.note: Kummer-theoretic pairing on which the Čebotarev argument of §10 rests. Closest plan: ES.1 "Use upstream Chebotarev on the finite extensions cut out jointly by T modulo powers and a finite collection of cohomology classes".

items.name: The field L_S cut out by a finite S ⊂ H¹(K,E_p)
items.statement: Let S ⊂ H¹(K,E_p) be a finite subgroup (a finite-dimensional ℤ/pℤ-vector space). Let Gal_S(ℚ̄/L) be the subgroup of ρ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/L) with [s,ρ] = 0 for all s ∈ S, and L_S its fixed field. Then L_S is a finite normal extension of L.
items.note: Used with S = Sel(E/K)_p (M = L_S) and with S = ⟨δy_K⟩, ⟨c(ℓ′)⟩ (L_{(δy_K)}, L′). ES.1 is the nearest plan.

items.name: Proposition 9.3: Kummer duality Gal(L_S/L) ≅ Hom(S,E_p(L))
items.statement: The induced pairing [,] : S × Gal(L_S/L) → E_p(L) is non-degenerate: it induces an isomorphism of 𝒢-modules Gal(L_S/L) ≅ Hom(S,E_p(L)), as well as an isomorphism of Gal(K/ℚ)-modules S ≅ Hom_𝒢(Gal(L_S/L),E_p(L)).
items.note: Proof: the pairing gives injections Gal(L_S/L) ↪ Hom(S,E_p) ≃ E_p^r (r = dim S) and S ↪ Hom_𝒢(Gal(L_S/L),E_p); E_p is a simple 𝒢-module, so E_p^r is semisimple and Gal(L_S/L) ≅ E_p^s with s ≤ r; then Hom_𝒢(Gal(L_S/L),E_p) ≃ (ℤ/p)^s contains S ≃ (ℤ/p)^r, forcing s = r. (Hom_𝒢(E_p,E_p) = ℤ/p uses absolute irreducibility, implicit.) ES.1 is the nearest plan.

items.name: M = L_Sel, H = Gal(M/L), I = Gal(M/L(y_K/p)) (9.4)
items.statement: Apply Prop. 9.3 to S = Sel(E/K)_p; put M = L_S and H = Gal(M/L) = Gal(L_S/L) ≃ Hom(Sel(E/K)_p,E_p). Assume y_K is not divisible by p in E(K), and let δy_K be its non-zero image in Sel(E/K)_p. Let I be the subgroup of H fixing the subfield L((1/p)y_K) = L_{(δy_K)} of M (so H/I ≃ E_p). Let τ be a fixed complex conjugation in Gal(M/ℚ), and H⁺, I⁺ the +1 eigenspaces for τ (acting by conjugation) on H and I.
items.note: Data for the Čebotarev argument of §10.

items.name: Proposition 9.5(1): H⁺ = {(τh)²}, I⁺ = {(τi)²}, H⁺/I⁺ ≃ ℤ/p
items.statement: We have H⁺ = {(τh)² : h ∈ H}, I⁺ = {(τi)² : i ∈ I}, and H⁺/I⁺ ≃ ℤ/pℤ.
items.note: Proof: p odd, so H⁺ = H^{τ+1} = {h^τ·h}; h^τ = τhτ⁻¹ = τhτ, so h^τh = (τh)²; similarly for I⁺; H⁺/I⁺ = (H/I)⁺ ≅ E_p^ε ≃ ℤ/p, where ε is the τ-sign of δy_K (the text prints E_p⁺, which is right only when ε = +1; a misprint recorded by this review). This is what lets Čebotarev produce primes with Frob(λ) = ρ for any ρ ∈ H⁺.

items.name: Proposition 9.5(2): a signed Selmer class vanishing on H⁺ − I⁺ is zero
items.statement: Let s ∈ Sel(E/K)_p^±. The following are equivalent: (a) [s,ρ] = 0 for all ρ ∈ H; (b) [s,ρ] = 0 for all ρ ∈ H⁺; (c) [s,ρ] = 0 for all ρ ∈ H⁺ − I⁺; (d) s = 0.
items.note: Proof: (d)⇔(a)⇒(b)⇒(c) is clear. (c)⇒(b): s is a homomorphism on H⁺ and I⁺ ≠ H⁺. (b)⇒(a): s induces a 𝒢-homomorphism H → E_p mapping H⁺ → E_p^± and H⁻ → E_p^∓; if s vanishes on H⁺ then s(H) ⊂ E_p^∓ is a proper 𝒢-submodule of the simple E_p, so s(H) = 0.

items.name: Frob(λ) in H for λ split in L
items.statement: Let λ be a prime of K not dividing Np, so λ is unramified in M/K; assume further λ splits completely in L/K and let λ_M be a prime factor of λ in M. The Frobenius substitution of λ_M in Gal(M/K) lies in H, and its 𝒢-orbit, denoted Frob(λ), depends only on λ. Write [s,Frob(λ)] = 0 iff [s,ρ] = 0 for all ρ ∈ Frob(λ).
items.note: Connects the pairing (9.2) with localization at λ.

items.name: Proposition 9.6: [s,Frob(λ)] = 0 iff s_λ = 0
items.statement: For s ∈ Sel(E/K)_p ⊂ H¹(K,E_p) the following are equivalent: (a) [s,ρ] = 0, where ρ is the Frobenius substitution associated to the factor λ_M of λ in Gal(M/L) = H; (b) [s,Frob(λ)] = 0; (c) s_λ ≡ 0 in H¹(K_λ,E_p).
