items.note: Proof: (a)⇔(b) as [s,ρ^σ] = [s,ρ]^σ. For (a)⇔(c) write s_λ ≡ P_λ in E(K_λ)/pE(K_λ) ↪ H¹(K_λ,E_p); (1/p)P_λ is rational over M_{λ_M} and [s,ρ] = ((1/p)P_λ)^{ρ−1} in E(M_{λ_M})_p ≃ E(M)_p, so [s,ρ] = 0 iff P_λ ∈ pE(K_λ).

items.name: y_K lies in the ε-eigenspace
items.statement: The Heegner point y_K = P₁ lies in the ε-eigenspace for complex conjugation on E(K)/pE(K) (ε the eigenvalue of the Fricke involution on f); hence δy_K lies in the ε-eigenspace of Sel(E/K)_p.
items.note: Case n = 1 of Prop. 5.4(1) (ε₁ = ε). HE.4 ("the complex-conjugation parity").

items.name: Claim 10.1: Sel(E/K)_p^{−ε} = 0
items.statement: (p odd, Gal(ℚ(E_p)/ℚ) ≅ GL₂(ℤ/pℤ), y_K not divisible by p in E(K).) Sel(E/K)_p^{−ε} = 0.
items.note: Proof: by 9.5 it suffices that [s,ρ] = 0 for ρ ∈ H⁺ − I⁺, ρ = (τh)². Take ℓ unramified in M/ℚ with a factor λ_M whose Frobenius is τh in Gal(M/ℚ) (positive density, Čebotarev); then (ℓ) = λ is inert in K, splits completely in L, and the Frobenius of F_{λ_M}/F_λ is (τh)², so by 9.6 it suffices to show s_λ = 0. The class d(ℓ) is in the −ε-eigenspace (Prop. 5.4) and locally trivial except at λ (Prop. 6.2); d(ℓ)_λ ≠ 0 because by 6.2 it vanishes iff y_K ∈ pE(K_λ), i.e. iff λ splits completely in L((1/p)y_K), i.e. iff ρ ∈ I⁺ = I ∩ H⁺, which is excluded. Prop. 8.2 with d = d(ℓ) gives s_λ = 0. HE.6; ES.4 ("Construct the Selmer graph ... Apply Poitou–Tate").

items.name: Proposition 10.2: equivalent vanishing conditions for c(ℓ)
items.statement: Assume y_K is not divisible by p in E(K). Let ℓ be a rational prime unramified in M/ℚ with a factor λ_M whose Frobenius substitution is τh in Gal(M/ℚ), h ∈ H. Then (ℓ) = λ is inert in K and λ splits completely in L = K(E_p). The following are equivalent: (1) c(ℓ) ≡ 0 in H¹(K,E_p); (2) c(ℓ) ∈ Sel(E/K)_p ⊂ H¹(K,E_p); (3) P_ℓ is divisible by p in E(K_ℓ); (4) d(ℓ) ≡ 0 in H¹(K,E)_p; (5) d(ℓ)_λ ≡ 0 in H¹(K_λ,E)_p; (6) P₁ = y_K is locally divisible by p in E(K_λ); (7) h^{1+τ} lies in the subgroup I⁺ = H⁺ ∩ I of H⁺.
items.note: Proof: (1)⇔(2) since c(ℓ) ∈ H¹(K,E_p)^{−ε} and Sel^{−ε} = 0 (10.1); (1)⇔(3) by Prop. 4.7; (1)⇔(4) since (E(K)/pE(K))^{−ε} = 0; (4)⇔(5) since d(ℓ) is locally trivial except perhaps at λ and Ш(E/K)_p^{−ε} = 0; (6),(7)⇔(5) by Prop. 6.2. Used to choose ℓ′ in Claim 10.3. HE.5/HE.6. In (4) and (5) the text prints H¹(K,E_p) and H¹(K_λ,E_p) (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E37).

items.name: Claim 10.3: Sel(E/K)_p^{ε} ≃ ℤ/p·δy_K
items.statement: (p odd, Gal(ℚ(E_p)/ℚ) ≅ GL₂(ℤ/pℤ), y_K not divisible by p in E(K).) Sel(E/K)_p^{ε} ≃ ℤ/pℤ·δy_K.
items.note: Proof: for s ∈ Sel^ε it suffices that [s,ρ] = 0 for ρ ∈ I, for then s ∈ Hom_𝒢(H/I,E_p) ≃ ℤ/p·δy_K; by the argument of 9.5 it suffices for ρ = (τi)² ∈ I⁺. Choose ℓ′ with Frobenius conjugate to τh, h^{1+τ} ∉ I⁺, so c(ℓ′) ≠ 0 and ∉ Sel (10.2); L′ = L_{(c(ℓ′))} has group E_p over L and is disjoint from M/L; λ splits in L′ iff P_{ℓ′} is locally a p-th power at λ. Choose ℓ with Frobenius τi in Gal(M/ℚ), i ∈ I, and τj in Gal(L′/ℚ) with j^{1+τ} ≠ 1 (possible since L′ ∩ M = L). Then d(ℓℓ′) ∈ H¹(K,E)_p^ε is locally trivial at v ≠ λ, λ′ (6.2); at λ′ trivial since i ∈ I gives c(ℓ) = 0, so P_ℓ ∈ pE(K_ℓ) (10.2); d(ℓℓ′)_λ ≠ 0 since otherwise λ would split in L′, i.e. (τj)² = j^{1+τ} = 1. Prop. 8.2 with d = d(ℓℓ′) gives s_λ = 0, so [s,(τi)²] = 0; hence s(I⁺) = s(I) = 0. With 10.1 this proves Prop. 2.3. HE.6.

items.name: When p | y_K the classes d(n) land in Ш(E/K)_p
items.statement: When y_K has infinite order but is divisible by p in E(K): P₁ ∈ pE(K) is equivalent to c(1) = 0, which implies, by Prop. 6.2, that the classes d(ℓ) all lie in Ш(E/K)_p. Similarly, if c(ℓ₁) = c(ℓ₂) = 0 then d(ℓ₁ℓ₂) lies in Ш(E/K)_p; if c(ℓ₁ℓ₂) = c(ℓ₁ℓ₃) = c(ℓ₂ℓ₃) = 0 then d(ℓ₁ℓ₂ℓ₃) lies in Ш(E/K)_p, etc.
items.note: Offered as the source of candidate non-trivial elements of Ш needed for the full Conjecture 1.2 when I_K > 1. Not planned.

items.name: Question: which subgroup of Ш(E/K)_p do the d(n) generate?
items.statement: Question: What subgroup of Ш(E/K)_p can be constructed in this manner (from the classes d(n) of §11)?
items.note: Open question, recorded for completeness; answered later in the literature by Kolyvagin's structure theorem for Selmer groups. Not planned.

items.name: Question: some c(n) is non-zero (Kolyvagin's conjecture)
items.statement: Question: Assume that p does not divide the integer c·∏_{q|N} m_q in Conjecture 1.2. Can one show that the class c(n) is non-zero in H¹(K,E_p) for some value of n = ℓ₁ℓ₂⋯ℓ_r?
items.note: An early form of Kolyvagin's conjecture on non-triviality of the Kolyvagin system. EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.5 plans the resulting notion: "Define residual primitivity and the index of a system"; HE.6: "Instantiate Zhang's indivisibility theorem".

items.name: Generalization to RM abelian varieties: order of vanishing
items.statement: Let A be an abelian variety of dimension d ≥ 1 over ℚ with End_ℚ(A) ⊗ ℚ a totally real number field of degree d; assume (a generalization of the Taniyama–Weil conjecture) that there is a surjective homomorphism φ : J₀(N) → A, and define y₁ = φ((x₁) − (∞)) ∈ A(K₁) and y_K = Tr_{K₁/K} y₁ ∈ A(K). Then the L-function of A over K vanishes to order ≥ d at s = 1, and [GZ; V, 2.4] the order of vanishing equals d if and only if y_K has infinite order in A(K).
items.note: Cited. GZ.8: "A totally real extension concerns the precise parametrized strict-GL₂-type abelian variety and coefficient-character component".

items.name: Generalization to RM abelian varieties: rank d and finite Ш
items.statement: In the setting of §12, assuming y_K has infinite order in A(K), Kolyvagin's method shows that the finitely generated group A(K) has rank d and that Ш(A/K) is finite.
items.note: Printed citation is [K2]; the abelian-variety result is [K3] (Kolyvagin–Logachev) (PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90/E38). HE.7: "The same construction supplies the Kolyvagin–Logachev extension for the specified admissible RM quotients of quaternionic Jacobians".

items.name: Bertolini–Darmon: χ-components over the Hilbert class field
items.statement: Let χ be a complex character of Gal(K₁/K) and define y_χ = Σ_σ χ⁻¹(σ) y₁^σ in (E(K₁) ⊗ ℂ)^χ. Following Kolyvagin one can show [B-D] that y_χ ≠ 0 implies the complex vector space (E(K₁) ⊗ ℂ)^χ has dimension one.
items.note: Cited from [B-D]. Not planned (HE.8 treats anticyclotomic families, not this statement).

items.name: Poitou–Tate exact sequence at H¹ (Rubin's (10))
items.statement: Let K be a number field, T a p-adic representation of G_K ramified at only finitely many primes, M ∈ O nonzero, and Σ a finite set of places of K containing all infinite places, all primes above p and all primes where T is ramified (so that S^Σ(K, W_M) = H¹(K_Σ/K, W_M) and S^Σ(K, W*_M) = H¹(K_Σ/K, W*_M) by Lemma 5.3). Then the sequence H¹(K_Σ/K, W_M) →(loc_Σ) ⊕_{v∈Σ} H¹(K_v, W_M) →(loc_Σ^∨) Hom_O(H¹(K_Σ/K, W*_M), O/MO) is exact, where loc_Σ^∨ sends (x_v)_v to d ↦ Σ_{v∈Σ} ⟨x_v, d_v⟩_v, the local pairings being those of Theorem 4.1.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. I §7, proof of Theorem 7.3(ii), display (10), p. 18 (cited from [Mi] Theorem I.4.10 and [T1] Theorem 3.1)
items.note: Planned by packet node ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4/poitou-tate ('Poitou–Tate duality and the nine-term exact sequence', exactness im β^r = ker γ^r for r = 0, 1, 2, for finite M whose order is a unit in R_{K,S}; here Σ contains the primes above p). The O/MO-valued form uses the O-linear local pairings of Theorem 4.1 (item r1-thm-4.1b-local-duality-WM) in place of Hom(M, μ). Added by the review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): This cited global duality theorem is the input of Theorem I.7.3, Rubin's 'main tool'; it appears only inside the note of r1-thm-7.3ii-poitou-tate-orthogonality, not as an item.

items.name: Leopoldt's conjecture for a number field
items.statement: For a number field L and the fixed prime p, Leopoldt's conjecture for L is the assertion that the p-adic completion of the global unit group O_L^× injects into (L ⊗ Q_p)^× (equivalently, into (O_L ⊗ Z_p)^×, the product of the local unit groups at the primes above p).
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. I §6.3, proof of Corollary 6.4, p. 16; also Ch. II §3, Hypothesis Hyp(K_∞/K), p. 27
items.note: Polylogarithms:P.6: 'state Leopoldt as injectivity of the correctly defined completed global-unit map to local units/logarithms'. The abelian case (Brumer) is IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4. Hypothesis of r1-cor-6.4-leopoldt, r2-rem-2.7-leopoldt and r2-hyp-Kinf-over-K, and used (as known for real abelian fields) in Proposition III.2.6 and Theorem III.2.7. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): A hypothesis of three items in the range; it has no item of its own.

items.name: Teichmüller character ω and ⟨ε⟩
items.statement: For p fixed and F a field of characteristic ≠ p, the Teichmüller character ω : G_F → (Z_p^×)_tors gives the action of G_F on μ_p if p is odd, or on μ_4 if p = 2; ω has order at most p − 1 (resp. 2), with equality if F = Q, and ⟨ε⟩ = ω^{-1}ε_cyc takes values in 1 + pZ_p (resp. 1 + 4Z_2).
items.note: Split from r0-notation-cyclotomic-character, whose library declaration (mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter) gives ε_cyc only. ω and ⟨ε⟩ are ε_cyc followed by the two projections of the Teichmüller decomposition Z_p^× = μ_{p−1} × (1 + pZ_p) (resp. {±1} × (1 + 4Z_2)), which DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 plans ('Use Teichmuller decomposition to define the branches'; the roadmap README: 'The dyadic branch uses ±1×(1+4Z₂)'). Not in the library at the pin: Mathlib has no Teichmüller decomposition of ℤ_[p]ˣ, and TauCeti.teichmuller (TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100) is the residue-field lift k^× → O^× of a local field, not a Galois character. Used in Theorem III.2.9. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): Part of the notation item that was marked library although only ε_cyc is in the library.

items.name: Iwasawa: Y_∞^χ is torsion-free of Λ-rank one ([Iw3] Theorem 25)
items.statement: In the setting of Ch. III §2 (χ even, nontrivial, of finite order prime to p; L the field cut out by χ; Y_∞ = lim_← (L_{n,p}^×)^ for the norm maps): Y_∞^χ is a torsion-free, finitely generated Λ-module of rank one. Hence every nonzero Λ-submodule, in particular (E′_∞)^χ, is torsion-free, finitely generated and of rank one.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §2.5, proof of Theorem 2.7, p. 38 (citing [Iw3] Theorem 25)
items.note: Cited without proof. The EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture packet (node L2/lambda-index-of-cyclotomic-units) lists it as a hypothesis 'requested from IntegralIwasawaTheory; it is not read here'; IntegralIwasawaTheory I.2 plans finite generation of the unit and local-unit limits but not this rank statement. Natural route: source of IntegralIwasawaTheory I.2 (or EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture L2). Added by the review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): Key input to Theorem 2.7 (item r3-thm-2.7): it gives ind_Λ(c) = char((E′_∞)^χ/C_{∞,χ}). It appears only inside that item's note.

items.name: Rohrlich: nonvanishing of cyclotomic twists of L(E,s)
items.statement: Suppose E/ℚ is modular. Then L(E,χ,1) ≠ 0 for all but finitely many characters χ of finite order of Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ); equivalently, for E with good ordinary or multiplicative reduction at p, the p-adic L-function ℒ_E of Theorem 5.13 is nonzero.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §5.5, proof of Corollary 5.6, p. 49, and §5.9, proof of Theorem 5.16, p. 53 (citing [Ro])
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L4: 'Prove the analytic twist-nonvanishing theorem required to show the localized/global class is nonzero, including the cyclotomic-family theorem used in Kato's argument'; the packet node KatoEulerSystems:L4/nonvanishing-of-the-zeta-submodule-at-height-zero states Rohrlich's theorem (Kato Thm. 13.5(2)). The equivalence with ℒ_E ≠ 0 is via the interpolation formula of Theorem 5.13. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): Used in Corollary 5.6 and Theorem 5.16 (ℒ_E ≠ 0 is what makes Z_∞ torsion); it appears only in item notes.

items.name: Descent from Z_∞ to ℚ in the good ordinary case (proof of Corollary 5.18)
items.statement: Suppose E is modular with good ordinary reduction at p, and let χ_0 be the trivial character. (a) If Z_∞ has no nonzero finite submodules and char(Z_∞) divides ℒ_EΛ, then |S(ℚ_∞,E_{p^∞})^{Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ)}| divides χ_0(ℒ_{E,N}) = (1 − α^{-1})² ∏_{q|N} ℓ_q(q^{-1}) L(E,1)/Ω_E. (b) The restriction map S(ℚ,E_{p^∞}) → S(ℚ_∞,E_{p^∞})^{Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ)} is injective with cokernel of order divisible by (1 − α^{-1})².
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §5.9, proof of Corollary 5.18, p. 54
items.note: Rubin only sketches this ('The idea is that ...') and refers to [PR1] §6 and [Schn] §2. (b) is Mazur's control theorem at the trivial character with its local correction at p; SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 plans control generically ('Prove control statements with explicit kernels/cokernels expressed through H^0, inertia and local quotient terms'). (a) is the standard evaluation of a torsion Λ-module without finite submodules at the trivial character. If the lead reads L3 as not planning this instance, the status is missing and the route is a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 or RankZeroOneBSD. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): The step from Theorem 5.16 and Corollary 5.17 to Corollary 5.18 in the ordinary case; no item states it.

items.name: Theorem 5.4(ii) for L ⊂ ℚ_∞ (partial proof)
items.statement: Suppose E is modular, E does not have complex multiplication, and E has good ordinary or multiplicative reduction at p. If L ⊂ ℚ_∞ is a finite extension of ℚ, χ is a character of Gal(L/ℚ) and L(E,χ,1) ≠ 0, then E(L)^χ and Ш(E/L)_{p^∞}^χ are finite.
items.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §5.9, after Remark 5.19, p. 54
items.note: Proof: by Theorem 5.16 the χ-specialisation of char(Z_∞) is controlled by L(E,χ,1)/Ω_E, so S(ℚ_∞,E_{p^∞})^χ is finite; the kernel of S(L,E_{p^∞}) → S(ℚ_∞,E_{p^∞}) lies in the finite group H¹(ℚ_∞/L, E_{p^∞}^{G_{ℚ_∞}}). Rubin prints that χ(char(Hom(S(ℚ_∞,E_{p^∞}),ℚ_p/ℤ_p))) 'is a nonzero multiple of L(E,χ,1)/Ω_E'; Theorem 5.16 gives the reverse relation (it divides a nonzero multiple of L(E,χ^{-1},1)/Ω_E), which is what the argument needs. Same planning as Theorem 5.4(ii) (item r3-thm-5.4-ii). Added by the review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): The only part of Theorem 5.4(ii) that Rubin proves; item r3-thm-5.4-ii mentions it only in its note.

items.name: Corollary A.2.6: kernel and cokernel of q(σ) on W_M are bounded by 2b
items.statement: Let O be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field Φ, T a free O-module of finite rank, and σ an O-linear automorphism of T with p(x) = det(1 − σ^{-1}x|T) satisfying p(1) = 0; let q(x) ∈ O[x] be the unique polynomial with p(x) = (1 − x)q(x). Put V = T ⊗ Φ, W = V/T and, for nonzero M ∈ O, W_M = ker(M : W → W). Suppose dim_Φ(V/(σ − 1)V) = 1. Then the O-modules T^{σ=1}/q(σ)T, T^{q(σ)=0}/(σ − 1)T, (T/(σ − 1)T)_tors, W^{σ=1}/q(σ)W, W^{q(σ)=0}/(σ − 1)W and W^{σ=1}/(W^{σ=1})_div have finite and equal length b (Proposition A.2.5), and for every nonzero M ∈ O the kernel and cokernel of the map q(σ) : W_M/(σ − 1)W_M → W_M^{σ=1} have length at most 2b.
items.locator: Rubin, App. A §2, Corollary 2.6, p. 148 (with Proposition 2.5, p. 147)
items.note: Proof: Herbrand quotients of O[x]/p(x)-modules (Proposition A.1.3, Lemma A.2.1, Proposition A.2.3) give the equal lengths of Proposition A.2.5; then compare q(σ) on W_M with q(σ) on W, whose kernel and cokernel are (v) and (iv). Tau Ceti's Herbrand quotient (TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient, TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/HerbrandQuotient.lean:59) is the group-cohomology one for a representation of a finite group, not this O[x]-module version; no atlas stage names it (ES.1 plans the exact finite–singular isomorphism, ES.4 'retains ... bounded local torsion'). Its error-free special case Corollary A.2.7 underlies item r4-cor-5.5-fs-isomorphism. Natural route: source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.4. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): The proof of Theorem II.2.3 (Ch. V §3, p. 88) uses it with σ ↔ Fr_q to get order((κ_{q,M})_q, H¹_s(K_q, W_M)) ≥ order((κ_{1,M})_q, H¹_f(K_q, W_M)) − 2b, with b = ℓ_O(W^{τ=1}/(W^{τ=1})_div) as in item r5-thm-II.2.3-exponent-bound. This is the only place the error 2b in the exponent bound comes from, and Appendix A was not read, so no item states it.

items.name: Finiteness of Sel(E/K)_p
items.statement: Sel(E/K)_p is a finite subgroup of H¹(K,E_p), i.e. a finite-dimensional ℤ/pℤ-vector space.
items.locator: Gross, §9, p. 251 ('We apply Proposition 9.3 to the finite subgroup S = Sel(E/K)_p of H¹(K,E_p)')
items.note: Used without proof (weak Mordell–Weil). EllipticCurves Layer 7 plans 'the finiteness of Sel_m(E/K) (AEC X.4.2)'. The pinned Tau Ceti has only the explicit 2-Selmer group WeierstrassCurve.Affine.selmerGroup₂ (MordellWeil/SelmerGroup.lean:104), not the cohomological Sel_p. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): Proposition 9.3 is applied to S = Sel(E/K)_p and needs S finite: finiteness makes M = L_S a finite extension of L, which the Čebotarev arguments of §10 require. No item states it (g-field-diagram-9.4 applies 9.3 to Sel without it).

items.name: Global reciprocity for H²(K,μ_p)
items.statement: H²(K,μ_p) = Br(K)_p. A class in H²(K,μ_p) is determined by its local components in Br(K_v)_p, and the sum over all places v of K of its local invariants is zero.
items.note: ClassFieldTheory Layer 10 plans 0 → Br(K) → ⊕_v Br(K_v) → ℚ/ℤ → 0 ('eq_zero_of_localInv_eq_zero is exactness at Br K (Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether), sumLocalInv_eq_zero is exactness in the middle'); ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9 plans H²(G_K,μₙ) inside the Brauer group ('h2KummerToUnits is injective by Hilbert 90, with image the n-torsion'). At the pinned commits only TauCeti.kummerShortExact (FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Coefficients.lean:195) exists; neither statement is in the library. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): This is 'the full power of global class field theory' that Proposition 8.2 uses: the global cup product lies in H²(K,μ_p) = Br(K)_p, it is determined by its local components, and the sum of the local invariants is zero. Item g-prop-8.2 cites ClassFieldTheory Layer 10 only in its planned list; the theorem itself is not an item.

items.name: Unramified cohomology of E and the component group
items.statement: Let v be a finite place of K. If E has good reduction at v then H¹(K_v^{un}/K_v, E) = 0. In general H¹(K_v^{un}/K_v, E⁰) = 0, where E⁰ is the identity component of the Néron model, so H¹(K_v^{un}/K_v, E) injects into H¹(F_v, Φ), where Φ = E/E⁰ is the group of components.
items.locator: Gross, §6, proof of Proposition 6.2(1), p. 245 (citing [M, Ch. I, §3] and [M, Ch. I, Prop. 3.8]); also §7, (7.1) and proof of Proposition 7.5, pp. 247–248 ('H¹(𝒪_λ,E) = 0', 'H¹(K_λ^{un}/K_λ,E) = H¹(𝒪_λ,E) = 0')
items.note: Cited from Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems (Lang's theorem for the connected component over the finite residue field). No stage plans it. NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.2 constructs the component group but no Galois cohomology. HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.3, 'identify the local Kummer image and the precise component-group obstruction', is its nearest consumer, and it would join route 4 (source, HeegnerPointEulerSystems, stage HE.3). EllipticCurves Layer 7 lists 'unramified local cohomology' only among the prerequisites it lacks. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): It is the key input of Proposition 6.2(1), which shows d(n)_v = 0 for every finite v ∤ n (good and bad reduction alike), and of (7.1) and Proposition 7.5. The extraction mentions it only inside the notes of g-prop-6.2-away-from-n and g-local-H1-dimension.

prerequisites.citation: V. A. Kolyvagin, Finiteness of E(Q) and Ш(E,Q) for a subclass of Weil curves, Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR Ser. Mat. 52 (1988); Math. USSR-Izv. 32 (1989), 523–541
prerequisites.why: Kolyvagin's first Heegner-point descent ([Ko1] in Rubin): rank and Sha bounds from a nontorsion Heegner point, the argument Gross expounds.

prerequisites.citation: F. Thaine, On the ideal class groups of real abelian number fields, Ann. of Math. 128 (1988), 1–18
prerequisites.why: Thaine's method with cyclotomic units, which Kolyvagin's Euler systems generalise (Rubin, Introduction and III §2).

prerequisites.citation: M. Bertolini, H. Darmon, Kolyvagin's descent and Mordell–Weil groups over ring class fields, J. reine angew. Math. 412 (1990), 63–74
prerequisites.why: The χ-component extension of Kolyvagin's descent over ring class fields (Gross §12, Rubin IX.4).

prerequisites.citation: B. Mazur, Rational isogenies of prime degree (with an appendix by D. Goldfeld), Invent. Math. 44 (1978), 129–162
prerequisites.why: Full GL₂ image mod p for semistable curves and p ≥ 11, the hypothesis of the clean case in Gross §2.

prerequisites.citation: J.-P. Serre, Propriétés galoisiennes des points d'ordre fini des courbes elliptiques, Invent. Math. 15 (1972), 259–331
prerequisites.why: §4 (Théorème 3 and Corollaire 1): the open-image theorem, which makes the Euler-system hypotheses hold for almost all p (Rubin III.5.8–5.9, Gross Prop. 2.1). Serre 1972 is already an atlas source (Serre72), but only §§1–2 have been read; this extraction needs §4.

prerequisites.citation: R. Greenberg, Iwasawa theory for p-adic representations, in Algebraic Number Theory — in honor of K. Iwasawa, Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 17 (1989), 97–137
prerequisites.why: Rubin's [Gr2]: the dual Selmer group over the cyclotomic Z_p-extension has no nonzero finite submodule, behind Corollary III.5.17 (route 9).

prerequisites.citation: D. E. Rohrlich, On L-functions of elliptic curves and cyclotomic towers, Invent. Math. 75 (1984), 409–423
prerequisites.why: Nonvanishing of L(E,χ,1) for almost all characters of the cyclotomic tower, behind Corollary III.5.6 (finite generation of E(Q_∞)), route 2.

routes.reason: ES.0–ES.4 plan Kolyvagin's method in the form of Rubin's book: the Euler-system module and norm relations (ES.2), derivative operators and Kolyvagin classes (ES.3), and the core descent bound, which ES.4 cites as 'Rubin II.2.2'. What they do not name, and what this route adds, are the steps of that method. They are the universal Euler system and its freeness (Rubin IV §§2–3, with the Ext¹ vanishing), the connecting map δ_L and the induced modules (IV §4), and unramifiedness of Euler-system and derivative classes away from p𝔯 with the local lifts (IV §6). They also include the lifted telescoping identity and Lemma IV.7.3, and Kolyvagin's congruence condition, which Rubin recovers as Corollary IV.8.1 (Remark II.1.5). They include the finiteness of H¹(Ω/K, W) (Lemma V.3.2), the universal-norm lemmas of Appendix B §3, and the variants of Chapter IX: rigidity, finite depth, χ-anticyclotomic Euler systems with Theorem IX.4.3 (the abstract setting of Heegner points), and triviality at Σ. Kolyvagin's article introduced the method, and Rubin's book is the public text that states it; together they should be the sources of these stages. Review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): Appendix B §3 (Lemma B.3.2, Proposition B.3.3, Corollaries B.3.4–B.3.5) is planned in SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 and leaves the route; Remark II.2.7, Lemma IV.3.3 and Remark IV.3.5 go to their own routes; Example IX.6.2 goes to route 3. The route takes the general-χ derivative classes of IX.4 and Remark IX.4.4 (HE.4 plans only the Heegner case) and Appendix A Corollary 2.6, the source of the 2b error term in Chapter V §3, under ES.3–ES.4. Proposition IV.4.5(ii)–(iii) (the cocycle formula for δ and its compatibility with restriction and corestriction) is in the Tau Ceti library, and Proposition IV.6.1 is planned in SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3; they leave the route.

Rubin III §5 applies the method to Kato's Euler system for an elliptic curve over Q. It proves rank zero and finiteness of Sha when L(E,1) ≠ 0 (III.5.4), and the p-part of the BSD upper bound over the cyclotomic Z_p-extension (III.5.17–5.18). Rubin credits the first proof of III.5.4(i) to Kolyvagin. The missing items are that application's local inputs: the image of the singular quotient under exp* (III.5.1), finite generation of E(Q_∞) (III.5.6), the image hypotheses (III.5.8–5.10), the split multiplicative case (III.5.14(b)), and Greenberg's no-finite-submodule result and the p-part of BSD (III.5.17–5.18). KatoEulerSystems L3–L4 (explicit reciprocity, nonvanishing and the Euler-system divisibility) are where they belong.

Kolyvagin's article applied the method first to cyclotomic units, bounding χ-eigenspaces of ideal class groups. Rubin IX.1 revisits this with the Euler system c̃_m = (ζ_m − 1)(ζ_m^{-1} − 1) and proves |A_L^χ| = [E_L^χ : C_{L,χ}] for even χ (Theorem IX.1.2). EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture L1 (finite-level descent) and L3 (equality) plan exactly this. Review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90): Theorem IX.1.2 is planned in L4, whose packet node plans the class-number equality for real abelian fields (Greither, Theorem 4.14 and Corollary 4.15), so it is not routed. L0 owns the constructions of Examples IX.1.1 and IX.6.2 ('Construct the cyclotomic example from actual norm-compatible cyclotomic p-units'). L2 (Iwasawa divisibility) takes Iwasawa's theorem that Y_∞^χ is torsion-free of Λ-rank one, used in Theorem III.2.7.

Gross states the conjectural exact order of Ш(E/K) in terms of the Heegner index (Conjecture 1.2(2)), which is BSD.5's 'Heegner index formula'. The worked example X₀(37)/w₃₇ (curve 37a) is a natural BSD.9 comparison test.
The Selmer-group form of Leopoldt's conjecture for T = O (Remark II.2.7); Corollary I.6.4, one direction of it, is already planned in L4. Added in review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90).

Generic completed-group-ring algebra: finite-index restriction and coinduction for R[[G]] (L1), and self-injectivity of (O/M)[G] for finite G with its failure for (O/M)[[Γ]] (L6, which the EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems README names as the owner of self-injective Artinian reductions). Added in review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90).
The split-multiplicative property of the Coleman map Col_∞, whose construction (Proposition III.5.14(a)) is planned in L3; the non-crystalline case is L4. Added in review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90).
Greenberg's theorem that the dual Selmer group X = Z_∞ has no nonzero finite submodule, for the module L0 defines and whose structure it proves. Added in review (REV-PAPER-KOLYVAGIN-90).

sourceIssues.locator: Rubin, Ch. I §6, proof of Proposition 6.7, p. 17, lines 1-2 of the proof (Rubin, 1999 author draft of Euler systems); final version: proof of Proposition 1.6.8, p. 28
sourceIssues.printed: Under v ∤ p, the proof takes ℓ as the rational prime lying below p and asserts that A(K_v) contains a pro-ℓ subgroup with finite index.
sourceIssues.correction: If ℓ is the rational prime below v, then …
sourceIssues.reason: The residue characteristic ℓ of v is meant (ℓ ≠ p since v ∤ p). The prime below p is p itself, and then the pro-ℓ claim would contradict the conclusion that the p-adic completion is finite. The author's final version (p. 28, Proposition 1.6.8) reads 'below v'.

sourceIssues.locator: Rubin, App. B §2, Remark 2.6, p. 153 (Rubin, 1999 author draft of Euler systems); final version: Remark B.2.6, p. 197 (unchanged)
sourceIssues.printed: The source says that applying Proposition 2.5(ii) requires finiteness of H^i(G,S) for all i and all finite G-modules S of p-power order. It claims that topological finite generation of the pro-p-part of G suffices.
sourceIssues.correction: Finite generation (of a pro-p Sylow subgroup, or of G itself) gives finiteness of H¹ only. Finiteness of all H^i needs a p-cohomological finiteness condition, e.g. a pro-p Sylow subgroup that is finitely presented in all degrees (type p-FP_∞), as in the arithmetic cases of Proposition 2.7.
sourceIssues.reason: For a pro-p group P, dim H¹(P,F_p) is the generator rank and dim H²(P,F_p) the relation rank. Finitely generated pro-p groups that are not finitely presented exist, and for them H²(P,F_p) is infinite. If instead 'pro-p-part' means the maximal pro-p quotient, take G = ∏_{n≥1} A_5 with p = 2: that quotient is trivial, but H²(G,F_2) ⊇ ⊕_n H²(A_5,F_2) = ⊕_n Z/2 is infinite, by Künneth, since H¹(A_5,F_2) = 0 and H²(A_5,F_2) = Z/2. The remark is only illustrative (Proposition 2.5(ii) is applied via Proposition 2.7), so nothing downstream is affected. The author's final version (Remark B.2.6, p. 197) has the same wording.

review.reason: Verified on draft p. 153 (PDF p. 163), wording as quoted. The claim is false for i ≥ 2. If 'pro-p-part' means a pro-p Sylow subgroup P, then H^i(G,S) ↪ H^i(P,S), but topological finite generation of P only bounds H¹. dim H²(P,F_p) is the relation rank, and finitely generated pro-p groups of infinite relation rank exist (e.g. the pro-p lamplighter group F_p[[Z_p]] ⋊ Z_p). If it means the maximal pro-p quotient, the extraction's example G = ∏_{n≥1} A_5, p = 2 is right: every finite quotient ∏_{n≤N} A_5 is perfect, so the maximal pro-2 quotient is trivial; H¹(A_5,F_2) = 0 and H²(A_5,F_2) = Hom(H_2(A_5),F_2) = Z/2, so Künneth gives H²(G,F_2) = ⊕_n Z/2. Proposition 2.5(ii) is always applied through Proposition 2.7, so affects 'nothing' is right. Unchanged in the final version. Final version: p. 197, Remark B.2.6: 'To apply Proposition B.2.5(ii) we need to know when a group G has the property that H^i(G,S) is finite for every i and every G-module S of finite p-power order. For example, this is true whenever the pro-p-part of G is (topologically) finitely generated.' Unchanged.

sourceIssues.correction: … which is zero if ρ_{E,p}(G_Q) = GL_2(Z_p) and p is odd (the scalar c = 2, or any c with c − 1 ∈ Z_p^×, kills it by Sah's lemma). The vanishing of H¹(Q(E_{p^∞})/Q, E_{p^∞}) in Proposition 5.8(ii) needs p > 2, since for p = 2 the group H¹(GL_2(Z_2),(Q_2/Z_2)²) is nonzero; the conclusion that T_p(E) satisfies Hyp(Q_∞,T) holds for p = 2 too.
sourceIssues.reason: Let G = GL_2(Z_2), K = ker(G → GL_2(F_2) = S_3) = 1 + 2M_2(Z_2), and V = F_2². Then H¹(S_3,V) = H²(S_3,V) = 0 (V is projective), so inflation–restriction gives H¹(G,V) ≅ Hom_{S_3}(K^{ab}/2, V). K surjects S_3-equivariantly onto K/(1+4M_2) ≅ M_2(F_2) with the conjugation action, and M_2(F_2) ≅ V ⊗ V* ≅ V ⊕ P(1) as S_3-modules, so Hom_{S_3}(M_2(F_2), V) = F_2 ≠ 0. Hence H¹(G,V) ≠ 0 (a direct linear-algebra computation gives dim H¹(GL_2(Z/4),F_2²) = dim H¹(GL_2(Z/8),F_2²) = 1, and inflation is injective). Since H⁰(G,(Q_2/Z_2)²) = 0, the sequence 0 → V → (Q_2/Z_2)² →×2 (Q_2/Z_2)² → 0 gives H¹(G,V) ↪ H¹(G,(Q_2/Z_2)²), which is therefore nonzero. Surjective 2-adic images occur, so (ii) fails as stated at p = 2. The vanishing is used only in Theorem 5.11(ii), whose hypotheses exclude p = 2 and which applies Theorem II.2.10(ii) (stated for p > 2); Theorem 5.16 uses Proposition 5.8(ii) only for Hyp(Q_∞,T), which holds at p = 2. The author's final version (hEulerSystems.pdf, Annals-Studies pagination) has the same statement and proof at pp. 67–68, Proposition 3.5.8(ii).

review.reason: Quote verbatim at draft p. 50 (proof of Proposition 5.8). Checked independently: with G = GL_2(Z_2), K = 1+2M_2(Z_2), V = F_2^2, V is the projective simple F_2[S_3]-module, so H^1(G,V) = Hom_{S_3}(K,V) ⊇ Hom_{S_3}(M_2(F_2),V), and M_2(F_2) = V⊗V* ≅ V ⊕ P(1) as S_3-module, so this is F_2 ≠ 0. A direct F_2-linear-algebra computation of crossed homomorphisms gives dim H^1(GL_2(Z/4),F_2^2) = dim H^1(GL_2(Z/8),F_2^2) = 1 (and 0 for GL_2(Z/2)); inflation to GL_2(Z_2) is injective, and D^G = 0 for D = (Q_2/Z_2)^2 makes H^1(G,V) → H^1(G,D) injective. So the vanishing fails at p = 2; Sah's lemma with the scalar 2 proves it for p odd. The finiteness claim for open image is fine for all p. Kind error, affects a stated result: correct. Two refinements: (a) only the vanishing needs p > 2 (Hyp(Q_∞,T) holds at p = 2 with x = 1); (b) the downstream sentence is inexact: the vanishing is used in Theorem 5.11(ii), which assumes p ∤ 2r_E|Ẽ(F_p)| and applies Theorem II.2.10(ii), stated for p > 2; Theorem 5.16 uses Proposition 5.8(ii) only for Hyp(Q_∞,T) via Theorem II.3.8(ii), which holds at p = 2. Nothing downstream is affected. Final version: Still present: final version Proposition 3.5.8(ii), p. 67 ('Suppose that ρ_{E,p} is surjective. Then H^1(Q(E_{p^∞})/Q, E_{p^∞}) = 0 and T_p(E) satisfies hypotheses Hyp(Q_∞,T).'), with proof on p. 68: '... which is zero if ρ_{E,p}(G_Q) = GL_2(Z_p), and finite if ρ_{E,p}(G_Q) is open in GL_2(Z_p) (see also Corollary C.2.2).' No p > 2.

sourceIssues.reason: The formal logarithm is an isomorphism Ê(p^rZ_p) ≅ p^rZ_p only for r > 1/(p−1), so for p = 2 only from r = 2. Counterexample at p = 2: for E with split multiplicative reduction at 2, E_1(Q_2) ≅ 1 + 2Z_2 (Tate curve) contains −1, and λ_E(E_1(Q_2)) = log(1+2Z_2) = 4Z_2. Then exp*_{ω_E}(H¹_s(Q_2,T)) is off by a factor 2 from the stated value. The proposition is stated for all p in the 1999 draft. The later applications (Theorem 5.11(ii) and Corollary 5.18 have p ∤ 2) are unaffected. The author's final version adds the hypothesis p > 2 (Proposition 3.5.1, p. 65).

review.reason: Quote verbatim at draft p. 48 (proof of Proposition 5.1, including the unbalanced bracket). For p = 2 the formal logarithm is an isomorphism Ê(2^r Z_2) ≅ 2^r Z_2 only for r ≥ 2; λ(Ê(2Z_2)) ⊆ 2Z_2 contains 4Z_2 with index 2/|Ê(2Z_2)_tors|, so it is 2Z_2 if E_1(Q_2) is torsion-free and 4Z_2 if it has a point of order 2. Tate-curve example: split multiplicative reduction at 2 gives E_1(Q_2) = E_0(Q_2) ≅ Z_2^× ∋ −1 and λ_E = ±log, with image log(1+4Z_2) = 4Z_2; then exp*(H¹_s(Q_2,T)) = idx·2^{-2}Z_2, not idx·2^{-1}Z_2. Kind error, affects a stated result (the draft states Proposition 5.1 for all p): correct. Rubin himself added the hypothesis in the final version. Final version: Corrected: final version p. 65, Proposition 3.5.1: 'With notation as above, if p > 2 then exp*_{ω_E}(H¹_s(Q_p,T)) = [E(Q_p) : E_1(Q_p) + E(Q_p)_tors]p^{-1}Z_p', and the proof reads 'If p > 2 then λ_E(E_1(Q_p)) = pZ_p and, since rank_{Z_p}E(Q_p) = 1, we see that ...'.

sourceIssues.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §5.9, proof (sketch) of Corollary 5.17, p. 53 (Rubin, 1999 author draft of Euler systems); final version: Corollary 3.5.18, pp. 71–72
sourceIssues.printed: The proof takes Σ to comprise the places of Q dividing Np∞ … For v | q with q ∈ Σ and q ≠ p, it claims p ∤ |E(Q_q)_tors| implies absence of p-torsion in E(Q_{∞,v}); it then invokes Proposition 2 of [Gr2] to conclude H¹(Q_{∞,v}, E_{p^∞}) = 0.
sourceIssues.correction: Treat v | ∞ separately. H¹(R, E_{p^∞}) = 0 for p odd, so assume p odd in Corollary 5.17 (or handle the real places when p = 2).
sourceIssues.reason: Σ contains ∞, and the hypothesis only concerns q | N. For p = 2, H¹_s(R,E_{2^∞}) = H¹(R,E_{2^∞}) ≅ H¹(R,E) ≅ π_0(E(R))^∨, which is Z/2 when Δ_E > 0. Then the local terms at the archimedean places of Q_∞ (totally real for p = 2) do not vanish and the dual sequence written is not justified. Nothing in Corollary 5.17 excludes p = 2 (good ordinary reduction at 2 is allowed). The author's final version (Corollary 3.5.18, pp. 71–72) rewrites the sketch via local duality, Hom(H¹_s(Q_{∞,v},E_{p^∞}),Q_p/Z_p) ≅ lim_← E(Q_{n,v})^, but still treats only finite v | q with q ≠ p; at a real place and p = 2 this limit is E(R)^ ≅ Z/2 when Δ_E > 0, so the gap remains.

review.reason: Quote correct at draft p. 53 (the '…' elides the definition of Q_Σ and the sequence (17)). Σ contains ∞ and the only hypothesis is on q | N; for p odd H¹(R, E_{p^∞}) = 0 trivially, but Q_∞ is totally real for p = 2 and, with Rubin's conventions (H¹_f at a real place is the image of H¹_f(R,V) = 0), H¹_s(R,E_{2^∞}) = H¹(R,E_{2^∞}) ≅ H¹(R,E) ≅ π_0(E(R))^∨ = Z/2 when Δ_E > 0. So the archimedean terms of (17) are not shown to vanish, and Corollary 5.17 does not exclude p = 2. Kind gap, affects the proof: correct (whether the corollary survives at p = 2 is not settled by the finding, and it does not claim so). Final version: Still present (renumbered): final version Corollary 3.5.18, pp. 71–72. The sketch is rewritten via local duality, 'for every place v of Q_∞, Hom(H¹_s(Q_{∞,v},E_{p^∞}),Q_p/Z_p) ≅ lim_← E(Q_{n,v})^', then 'If v | q for some q ≠ p, and E(Q_q) has no p-torsion, then ... E(Q_{n,v})^ = 0 for every n. Thus for p as in the statement of the corollary, the Pontryagin dual of (3.17) is lim_← E(Q_{n,p})^ → ...'. Real places are still not treated; for p = 2 and v real, lim_← E(R)^ = Z/2 when Δ_E > 0.

(m,b) = 1, including the p-powers), and their compositum is the maximal abelian extension unramified at p (resp. at b), by Kronecker–Weber. 'Unramified outside p' is Q(μ_{p^∞}), which contains Q_∞, contradicting 'condition (ii)′(a) does not hold', and contains no Q(μ_ℓ), ℓ ≠ p. On p. 42, 'unramified outside b' would exclude Q(μ_{p^n}), yet c̃_{p^n} is used. Misprint, affects nothing. The reason's cross-reference 'C9' is a stale id for E9. Final version: p. 178, Example 9.1.1: "c = c̃^{χ^{-1}} is an Euler system for (Z_p(1)⊗χ^{-1}, Q^{ab,p}, fp), where Q^{ab,p} is the maximal abelian extension of Q unramified outside p"; p. 58 (§3.4, 'An Euler system for Z_p'): "Q^{ab,b} denotes the maximal abelian extension of Q unramified outside b". Not corrected. The same slip is in §9.1, p. 175: "K is the maximal abelian extension of K unramified outside N (so K does not contain a Z_p-extension of K)".

sourceIssues.locator: Rubin, Ch. IX §3, Theorem 3.3, p. 137 (Rubin, 1999 author draft of Euler systems); final version: Theorem 9.3.3, pp. 179–180
sourceIssues.printed: The source takes n to be the order of mc_K in H¹(K,W_M) and asserts nS_{Σ_p}(K,W*_M) = 0. It concludes that mc_K ≠ 0 implies finiteness of S_{Σ_p}(K,W*).
sourceIssues.correction: As in the author's final version (Theorem 9.3.3): with 𝔞₁ = ⋂_{q∤p} Ann_O(W^{I_q}/(W^{I_q})_div) (in place of the integer m) and 𝔞₂ = Ann_O(𝔞₁c_K) (in place of n), (M/𝔞₂)𝔞₁ S_{Σp}(K,W*_M) = 0. The stronger (M/n)S_{Σp}(K,W*_M) = 0, without the factor 𝔞₁, is what the argument of Ch. V §3 suggests but is not the author's statement.
sourceIssues.reason: As printed the statement fails for the zero Euler system c = 0 (still an Euler system for W_M): then n = 1 and the theorem would force S_{Σ_p}(K,W*_M) = 0 whenever the hypotheses hold. The method of Ch. V §3 (with n_W = n*_W = 0) gives order(η) + order((κ_𝔮)_𝔮) ≤ ord M with order((κ_𝔮)_𝔮) ≥ order(mc_K), which is the corrected annihilator. Only the corrected form yields the 'in particular': if S_{Σ_p}(K,W*) were infinite, S_{Σ_p}(K,W*_M) would contain elements of order M (Lemma I.5.4), impossible when M/n is a proper divisor of M, i.e. when mc_K ≠ 0. The author's final version (Theorem 9.3.3, p. 179) replaces nS = 0 by (M/𝔞₂)𝔞₁S = 0, with 𝔞₂ the annihilator of 𝔞₁c_K; this is weaker than the correction above by the factor 𝔞₁, and with it the 'in particular' follows directly only when 𝔞₁²c_K ≠ 0.

review.reason: Quote and locator verified (draft p. 137, Theorem IX.3.3). The printed annihilator is wrong: Definition 3.1 lets c = 0 be an Euler system for W_M (Rubin's own Remark II.2.8 notes the trivial system), the hypotheses (Hyp(K,T), n_W = n*_W = 0, W_M^{G_K} = 0) constrain only T and M, and then mc_K = 0 has order 1, so the theorem would force S_{Σp}(K,W*_M) = 0 for every such T, which fails whenever the Selmer group is nonzero (e.g. T = Z_p(1)⊗χ^{-1} over Q with A_L^χ/P ≠ 0). Reading 'order' as the integer exponent (as in Ch. V §3) does not rescue it either. The author changed the statement in the final version, but not to the extraction's form: final Theorem 9.3.3 bounds by (M/𝔞₂)𝔞₁, i.e. with the extra factor 𝔞₁ (the draft's m) on the Selmer group. The extraction's (M/n)S = 0 is what the single-prime argument of Ch. V §3 suggests when mκ_q is used (m kills H¹_ur/H¹_f as in Corollary IV.6.5), but it is stronger than the author's final statement and I have not verified it, so the correction should follow the final version. Observation (not checked further): with the final bound, the 'in particular' (𝔞₁c_K ≠ 0 ⇒ S_{Σp}(K,W*) finite) follows directly only when 𝔞₁²c_K ≠ 0, e.g. when 𝔞₁ = O (T unramified at all q ∤ p); the extraction's stronger form would give it as stated. Final version: p. 179–180, Theorem 9.3.3: 'Let 𝔞₁ = ⋂_{primes q of K, q∤p} Ann_O(W^{I_q}/(W^{I_q})_div) and let 𝔞₂ ⊂ O be the annihilator of 𝔞₁c_K in H¹(K,W_M). Then (M/𝔞₂)𝔞₁S_{Σp}(K,W*_M) = 0. In particular if 𝔞₁c_K ≠ 0 then S_{Σp}(K,W*) is finite.' — corrected by the author, in a weaker form than the extraction's correction.

sourceIssues.locator: Rubin, Ch. IX §4, Remark 4.2, p. 138 (Rubin, 1999 author draft of Euler systems); final version: Remark 9.4.2, p. 181, same text
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims that for a modular elliptic curve with Tate module T, the extra hypothesis χ(q) = 1 at every q dividing χ’s conductor makes Heegner points over anticyclotomic extensions of K′ into a χ-anticyclotomic Euler system for T.
sourceIssues.correction: … χ(q) = 1 for every q dividing the conductor of E (the Heegner hypothesis: all primes of bad reduction split in K′) …
sourceIssues.reason: χ is ramified at the primes dividing its own conductor, so 'χ(q) = 1' there is impossible or meaningless. Heegner points on X_0(N_E) require every q | N_E to split in K′, i.e. χ(q) = 1 for q | N_E. The author's final version (Remark 9.4.2, p. 181) has the same text. As printed the hypothesis is unsatisfiable, so the remark is vacuous rather than false; as intended it is correct.

review.reason: Quote and locator verified (draft p. 138). χ is the odd quadratic character of K′, ramified at every prime dividing its conductor, so χ(q) = 0 there as a Dirichlet character; the intended hypothesis is the Heegner hypothesis χ(q) = 1 for q | N_E. review.reason: Quote verified (the theorem starts on draft p. 140, the n*_W display is on p. 141). In the proof of Theorem II.2.2 (Ch. V §2, p. 86) the error term comes from Lemma V.2.3(iv): ι_m(S_{Σ∪Σp}(K,W*_m)) ⊂ H¹(Ω/K,W*) ∩ S_{Σp}(K,W*). Run with the Selmer group S^Σ_{Σp}(K,W*) (relaxed at Σ, which is what the classes κ ∈ S^{Σpr}_Σ(K,W_M) of Theorem 5.2 bound by duality), the same step lands in H¹(Ω/K,W*) ∩ S^Σ_{Σp}(K,W*). This contains the printed group. Equality holds when T is unramified at Σ: then Ω/K = K(1)K(W)K(μ_{p^∞},(O_K^×)^{1/p^∞}) is unramified at Σ and inflated classes are unramified, hence in H¹_f = H¹_ur there. So 'gap' affecting 'a stated result' is right: the printed bound is not proved when T ramifies at Σ, and I found no reason it should hold. Note n_W in the same theorem was adapted (S^{Σp}_Σ(K,W)), n*_W was not. Unchanged in the final version. Final version: p. 184, Theorem 9.5.3: 'n*_W = ℓ_O(H¹(Ω/K,W*) ∩ S_{Σp}(K,W*))' with the bound ℓ_O(S^Σ_{Σp}(K,W*)) ≤ ind_O(c) + n_W + n*_W — unchanged.

sourceIssues.printed: The source says D_ℓ is determined modulo the subgroup Z·Tr_ℓ. It reports Kolyvagin’s choice D_ℓ⁰ = Σ_{i=1}^{ℓ} i·σ_ℓ^i = −Σ_{i=1}^{ℓ+1} (σ_ℓ^i − 1)/(σ_ℓ − 1), while claiming this choice offers little benefit over alternatives.
sourceIssues.reason: Σ_{i=1}^{ℓ+1}(σ^i−1)/(σ−1) = Σ_{k=0}^{ℓ}(ℓ+1−k)σ^k, whose negative is Σ_k kσ^k − (ℓ+1)Tr_ℓ. Both sides satisfy (σ−1)D = ℓ+1−Tr_ℓ, so they agree only modulo Z·Tr_ℓ, which is harmless as D_ℓ matters only modulo Z·Tr_ℓ.

review.reason: Read at 300 dpi on p. 239: 'D⁰_ℓ = Σ_{i=1}^{ℓ} i·σ_ℓ^i = −Σ_{i=1}^{ℓ+1} (σ_ℓ^i − 1)/(σ_ℓ − 1)'. Reading (σ^i − 1)/(σ − 1) as 1 + σ + … + σ^{i−1}, the difference of the two sides is (ℓ+1)·Tr_ℓ, checked by direct computation in ℤ[C_{ℓ+1}] for ℓ = 2, 3, 4, 6, 10. review.reason: Printed as quoted (p. 242). On p. 241 𝒢_n = Gal(K_n/K), the Galois group of a ring class field, which is abelian, so it cannot surject onto GL₂(ℤ/pℤ). The argument's appeal to a 'group of dihedral type' fits Gal(K_n/ℚ), a generalized dihedral group, which surjects onto Gal(ℚ(E_p)/ℚ) ≅ GL₂(ℤ/pℤ) once ℚ(E_p) ⊂ K_n. For p odd GL₂(ℤ/pℤ) is not such a quotient: quotients of a generalized dihedral group are generalized dihedral or abelian, and SL₂(ℤ/pℤ) is non-abelian.

sourceIssues.locator: Gross, §9, first paragraph, p. 249 (Gross, published text, scanned copy)
sourceIssues.printed: The source sets L = K(E_p) and claims that D being coprime to Np makes K disjoint from Q(E_p). It concludes 𝒢 = Gal(L/K) is isomorphic to GL₂(Z/pZ).
sourceIssues.correction: Add to Propositions 2.1/2.3 the hypothesis D ≠ p (implied by p ∤ D; it has content only when p ≡ 3 mod 4, where it says K ≠ ℚ(√−p)), or note that if D = p then 𝒢 is the index-2 subgroup of GL₂(Z/pZ) of elements with square determinant. That subgroup still contains the homotheties Z and SL₂(Z/pZ), so E_p is still absolutely irreducible for 𝒢 (End_𝒢(E_p) = Z/pZ) and the rest of the argument goes through.
sourceIssues.reason: Nothing in §1–§2 assumes p ∤ D. §1 only assumes the primes of N split (so (D,N) = 1), and (3.1) concerns the auxiliary primes ℓ. With Gal(Q(E_p)/Q) ≅ GL₂(Z/pZ), the only quadratic subfield of Q(E_p) is Q(√(−1)^{(p−1)/2}p), so K and Q(E_p) fail to be disjoint exactly when K = Q(√−p) (p ≡ 3 mod 4, D = p). Then 𝒢 ≇ GL₂. The later steps use only Z ⊂ 𝒢 and irreducibility of E_p, so the conclusions survive. The printed claim 'D prime to Np' is not among the hypotheses, and p | D is weaker than the actual failure condition D = p.

review.reason: §1 assumes only that the primes dividing N split in K, which gives (D,N) = 1. Nothing in §§1–2 assumes p ∤ D; (3.1) concerns the auxiliary ℓ. For p ≥ 3 the commutator subgroup of GL₂(ℤ/pℤ) is SL₂(ℤ/pℤ), so ℚ(E_p) has the unique quadratic subfield ℚ(√((−1)^{(p−1)/2}p)), and K ∩ ℚ(E_p) ≠ ℚ exactly when D = p (p ≡ 3 mod 4). Then 𝒢 is the index-2 subgroup of square-determinant elements. It contains all homotheties (det(aI) = a²) and SL₂(ℤ/pℤ), so Prop. 9.1 (via Z), the simplicity of E_p and End_𝒢(E_p) = ℤ/pℤ (Props. 9.3, 9.5, Claim 10.3), Lemma 4.3 (which uses Gal(ℚ(E_p)/ℚ) only) and the Čebotarev choices of §10 all survive. The conclusion is not affected, but the printed justification is. One imprecision in the recorded correction: 'K ≠ ℚ(√−p), i.e. D ≠ p' are not equivalent for p ≡ 1 mod 4, where ℚ(√−p) has D = 4p and is harmless.

sourceIssues.locator: Rubin, Ch. II §1, Remark 1.2, third paragraph, p. 22 (1999 author draft, PDF p. 32); unchanged in the 2001 version as Remark 2.1.2, p. 34
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims its definition makes Euler system classes universal norms along K∞/K: for K ⊂f F ⊂f F′ ⊂ F′K∞, it says Σ(F′/F) is empty and consequently Cor_{F′/F}(c_{F′}) = c_F.
sourceIssues.correction: … i.e., if K ⊂_f F ⊂_f F′ ⊂ FK_∞, then Σ(F′/F) is empty so Cor_{F′/F}(c_{F′}) = c_F.
sourceIssues.reason: F′ ⊂ F′K_∞ holds for every F′, and then the conclusion is false: by Definition 1.1(i) 𝒦 contains K(𝔮) for every 𝔮 ∤ 𝒩; take 𝔮 ∤ 𝒩 unramified in F with K(𝔮) ≠ K(1), so that K(𝔮)/K(1) is ramified at 𝔮, and F′ = FK(𝔮): then Σ(F′/F) = {𝔮}. With F′ ⊂ FK_∞ the extension F′/F lies in FK_∞/F, which is unramified outside p because K_∞/K is a Z_p^d-extension, and p | 𝒩, so Σ(F′/F) = ∅. This is the reading used for c_{K,∞} in Definition II.3.1 and in item r2-rem-1.2-universal-norms.

sourceIssues.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §5.9, partial proof of Theorem 5.4(ii) (after Remark 5.19), p. 54 (1999 author draft)
sourceIssues.printed: The source invokes Theorem 5.16 to claim that χ(char(Hom(S(Q∞ , Ep∞ ), Qp /Zp ))) equals L(E, χ, 1)/ΩE times a nonzero factor.
sourceIssues.correction: by Theorem 5.16, χ(char(Hom(S(ℚ_∞,E_{p^∞}),ℚ_p/ℤ_p))) divides p^t χ(ℒ_{E,N}), which is a nonzero multiple of L(E,χ^{-1},1)/Ω_E when L(E,χ,1) ≠ 0 and χ is nontrivial.
sourceIssues.reason: Theorem 5.16 gives char(Z_∞) | p^t ℒ_{E,N}Λ, so the χ-specialisation of char(Z_∞) divides χ(p^t ℒ_{E,N}); by Theorem 5.13 and (16), for χ of conductor p^n > 1 this is p^t α^{-n} τ(χ) ∏_{q|N, q≠p} ℓ_q(q^{-1}χ^{-1}(q)) L(E,χ^{-1},1)/Ω_E, and τ(χ), α and these Euler factors are nonzero. The divisibility runs the other way from the print, and the L-value is at χ^{-1} (L(E,χ^{-1},1) is the complex conjugate of L(E,χ,1), so the two vanish together). The conclusion that S(ℚ_∞,E_{p^∞})^χ is finite is unaffected. For χ trivial and split multiplicative reduction the specialisation vanishes (factor 1 − α^{-1} = 0), but that case is Theorem 5.11.

sourceIssues.locator: Gross, §7, (7.3), p. 247 (Gross, published text, scanned copy)
sourceIssues.printed: The source attributes to Tate’s local duality theorem the assertion that (7.3) ⟨,⟩ : H¹(K_λ,E_p) × H¹(K_λ,E_p) ⟶ Z/pZ is both alternating and non-degenerate as a pairing of Z/pZ-vector spaces, citing [M, Ch. I, Corollary 2.3].
sourceIssues.correction: … is symmetric and non-degenerate.
sourceIssues.reason: For 1-cocycles a, b with coefficients in A, B one has a∪b = −s_*(b∪a) − d(c), where c(σ) = a(σ)⊗b(σ) and s swaps the factors. The Weil pairing is skew (e(y,x) = −e(x,y)), so e_*(a∪b) = e_*(b∪a): the pairing is symmetric. For odd p a non-degenerate symmetric form on a nonzero F_p-space is not alternating. Concretely, at a Kolyvagin prime λ (where Gross uses it, μ_p ⊂ K_λ and E_p ⊂ E(K_λ)), choose P, Q with e(P,Q) = ζ. Then H¹(K_λ,E_p) = H¹(K_λ,ℤ/p)² and ⟨x,y⟩ = x₁∪y₂ − x₂∪y₁, since the cup product on H¹(K_λ,ℤ/p) is alternating. So ⟨x,x⟩ = 2·x₁∪x₂, which is nonzero for x₁ the unramified class and x₂ a ramified class, by non-degeneracy of that cup product (the Hilbert symbol).

sourceIssues.locator: Gross, §5, proof of Proposition 5.4, p. 244 (Gross, published text, scanned copy)
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts that an integer k ∈ Z gives τD_ℓ = −σ_ℓD_ℓτ + kTr_ℓ because (σ_ℓ − 1) annihilates τD_ℓ + σ_ℓD_ℓτ. It specifies k = ℓ for D⁰_ℓ = Σ_1^ℓ iσ_ℓ^i.
sourceIssues.correction: τD_ℓ = −σ_ℓD_ℓτ + kTr_ℓτ (= −σ_ℓD_ℓτ + kτTr_ℓ).
sourceIssues.reason: τD_ℓ = D_ℓ*τ, where D* is the image of D under σ ↦ σ⁻¹, so τD_ℓ + σ_ℓD_ℓτ = (D_ℓ* + σ_ℓD_ℓ)τ lies in ℤ[G_ℓ]τ. It is killed by σ_ℓ − 1 exactly when D_ℓ* + σ_ℓD_ℓ ∈ ℤ·Tr_ℓ, so the correction term is kTr_ℓτ. The printed kTr_ℓ lies in ℤ[G_ℓ], not in ℤ[G_ℓ]τ, so for k ≠ 0 the identity is false. For D⁰_ℓ, D* + σD⁰ = ℓ·Tr_ℓ (computed in ℤ[C_{ℓ+1}] for ℓ = 2, 3, 4, 6, 10), so k = ℓ as printed. The next step is unaffected: Tr_ℓ commutes with τ and with 𝒢_n, so the extra terms are τ(…)Tr_ℓ yₙ, which lie in pE(Kₙ) because Tr_ℓ yₙ = a_ℓ y_{n/ℓ} with a_ℓ ≡ 0 mod p.

sourceIssues.locator: Gross, §9, proof of Proposition 9.5(1), p. 251 (Gross, published text, scanned copy)
sourceIssues.printed: The source finishes by asserting H⁺/I⁺ = (H/I)⁺ = E_p⁺ ≃ Z/pZ.
sourceIssues.correction: H⁺/I⁺ = (H/I)⁺ ≅ E_p^ε ≃ Z/pZ, where ε is the eigenvalue of complex conjugation on δy_K (the Fricke sign, §10).
sourceIssues.reason: H/I = Gal(L((1/p)y_K)/L) is identified with E_p by ρ ↦ ρ(Q) − Q, where pQ = y_K. Since y_K^τ = εy_K + (torsion) (Prop. 5.3 with n = 1; §10), τQ = εQ + t with t ∈ E_p, and a direct computation gives τρτ(Q) − Q = ε·τ(ρ(Q) − Q). So conjugation by τ on H/I corresponds to e ↦ ετ(e) on E_p, and (H/I)⁺ corresponds to E_p^ε. This is the same twist Gross states in the proof of 9.5(2): s ∈ Sel^± maps H⁺ → E_p^±. The printed E_p⁺ is right only when ε = +1. Both eigenspaces of τ on E_p are lines, so H⁺/I⁺ ≅ ℤ/p holds either way.

sourceIssues.locator: Rubin, Ch. III §2.1, equation (2), p. 34, and Remark 2.1, p. 34 (Rubin, 1999 author draft of Euler systems); final version: §3.2, equation (3.2) and Remark 3.2.1, p. 48, same text
sourceIssues.printed: The source gives (2): N_{Q(μ_{mℓ})/Q(μ_m)}(ζ_{mℓ} − 1) = (ζ_m − 1) for ℓ | m; (ζ_m − 1)^{1−Fr_ℓ^{-1}} for ℓ ∤ m and m > 1; (−1)^{ℓ−1} ℓ for m = 1. Remark 2.1 then claims that when p | m, equation (2) yields c̃_{m∞} = ζ_m − 1.
sourceIssues.correction: The first two cases hold only up to the sign (−1)^{ℓ−1}: N(ζ_{mℓ} − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ−1}(ζ_m − 1) if ℓ | m, and (−1)^{ℓ−1}(ζ_m − 1)^{1−Fr_ℓ^{-1}} if ℓ ∤ m, m > 1. Equivalently use 1 − ζ_m: N(1 − ζ_{mℓ}) = 1 − ζ_m (ℓ | m), (1 − ζ_m)^{1−Fr_ℓ^{-1}} (ℓ ∤ m, m > 1), ℓ (m = 1), exactly; define c̃_{m∞} = N_{Q(μ_{mp})/Q(μ_m)}(1 − ζ_{mp}). Remark 2.1 then reads c̃_{m∞} = 1 − ζ_m for p | m; the printed ζ_m − 1 is right only for p odd.
sourceIssues.reason: For ℓ | m the conjugates of ζ_{mℓ} over Q(μ_m) are ζ_{mℓ}ζ_ℓ^j (0 ≤ j < ℓ), so N = ∏_j(ζ_{mℓ}ζ_ℓ^j − 1) = ζ_ℓ^{ℓ(ℓ−1)/2}(ζ_{mℓ}^ℓ − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ−1}(ζ_m − 1). For ℓ ∤ m write ζ_{mℓ} = uv (u ∈ μ_m, v ∈ μ_ℓ); the conjugates are uv^i (1 ≤ i < ℓ), so N = v^{ℓ(ℓ−1)/2}(u^ℓ − 1)/(u − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ−1}(ζ_m − 1)^{1−Fr_ℓ^{-1}}, since u^ℓ = ζ_m and u = Fr_ℓ^{-1}(ζ_m). E.g. N_{Q(μ_8)/Q(μ_4)}(ζ_8 − 1) = 1 − ζ_4, and ζ_6 − 1 = −(ζ_3 − 1)^{1−Fr_2^{-1}} (here Q(μ_6) = Q(μ_3)). Checked numerically: the ratio of the true norm to the printed value is −1 for (m,ℓ) = (4,2), (6,2), (3,2), (5,2) and +1 for (3,3), (6,3), (4,3), (5,3), (9,3). For odd p the sign is invisible, since −1 is trivial in (F^×)^ = H¹(F,Z_p(1)), so the Euler-system claim and Theorems 2.3–2.10 are unaffected. For p = 2, which §2 allows ('Theorem II.3.3 also applies when p = 2', draft p. 37, for Theorem 2.7), the sign is visible in (F^×)^. For m odd, Q(μ_{2m}) = Q(μ_m), and the definition gives both c̃_{m∞} = ζ_{2m} − 1 and c̃_{2m,∞} = N_{Q(μ_{4m})/Q(μ_{2m})}(ζ_{4m} − 1) = −(ζ_{2m} − 1) for the same field. So the collection must be renormalised (1 − ζ) before the relations can be claimed. The renormalisation changes each class by ±1, which dies in the χ-parts for nontrivial χ used in Theorems 2.7–2.10, so the stated results survive.
sourceIssues.known: Loeffler and Zerbes, Euler systems (Arizona Winter School 2018 notes), https://swc-math.github.io/aws/2018/2018LoefflerZerbesNotes.pdf, §1.4b, footnote 8, p. 14: 'This is stated in Rubin's book "Euler Systems", §3.2, but with a sign error: he sets u_m = ζ_m − 1, which doesn't quite work, since norm^{Q(μ_8)}_{Q(μ_4)}(ζ_8 − 1) ≠ ζ_4 − 1'. They use u_m = 1 − ζ_m. Not corrected in the author's final version (§3.2, (3.2), p. 48). The atlas already records it as EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture/E1 (cyclotomic packet), with affects 'nothing'. This review says 'the proof' because the draft allows p = 2 in III §2 ('Theorem II.3.3 also applies when p = 2', p. 37), and for p = 2 the sign survives in (F^×)^.

sourceIssues.locator: Rubin, Ch. V §1, definition of R_M, p. 79 (Rubin, 1999 author draft of Euler systems); final version: §5.1, p. 105 (corrected there)
sourceIssues.printed: The source uses R_M = R_{K,M}, citing Definition IV.1.1, for ideals in R whose prime divisors q satisfy q ∤ N, M | [K(q) : K], M | P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; 1), and complete splitting of q in K(1).
sourceIssues.correction: … M | [K(q) : K(1)], M | P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; 1) …, as in Definition IV.1.1.
sourceIssues.reason: Definition IV.1.1 (draft p. 57) reads 'for every prime q dividing r, M | [K(q) : K(1)], M | P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*;1), and q splits completely in F(1)/K', and the sentence says it restates that definition. Since K(1) ⊂ K(q), [K(q):K] = [K(q):K(1)]·[K(1):K], so M | [K(q):K] does not give M | [K(q):K(1)] when p divides [K(1):K]. The latter is what Lemma IV.1.2(iii)–(iv), Lemma IV.7.3 and the use of these primes in Ch. V require. The same slip is E17 in the proof of Lemma IV.7.3. The author's final version, §5.1, p. 105, reads 'both [K(q) : K(1)] and P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*; 1) are divisible by M'.
sourceIssues.known: corrected in the author's final version of the book (https://www.wstein.org/people/rubin/book/hEulerSystems.pdf, Annals-Studies pagination), p. 105, §5.1: 'both [K(q) : K(1)] and P(Fr_q^{-1}|T*;1) are divisible by M'

sourceIssues.locator: Rubin, Ch. V §2, proof of Lemma 2.1, p. 81 (Rubin, 1999 author draft of Euler systems); final version: proof of Lemma 5.2.1, p. 107 (repaired there)
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts κ(G_L) is G_K-stable inside W_{𝔭^d} but lies outside W_{𝔭^{d−1}}. It uses Hyp(K, T)(ii) to claim irreducibility of W_𝔭 = T ⊗ k, then concludes 𝔭^{d−1}κ(G_L) = W_𝔭 and hence κ(G_L) = W_{𝔭^d}.
sourceIssues.correction: Replace κ(G_L) and κ(J) by their O-spans. 𝔭^{d−1}·Oκ(G_L) = W_𝔭 gives Oκ(G_L) = W_{𝔭^d} (Nakayama over O/𝔭^d). Then Oκ(J) lies in W_{𝔭^{d−1}} + (τ−1)W_M, and with E22's correction Oκ(J) ≠ Oκ(G_L). So J ≠ G_L, and J has index at least p.
sourceIssues.reason: κ(G_L) is the image of a homomorphism G_L → W_M. It is a G_K-stable subgroup, hence a Z_p-module, but not in general an O-module when O ≠ Z_p. If k ≠ F_p, the irreducible k[G_K]-module W_𝔭 can have proper G_K-stable F_p-subspaces (an F_p-form, when the residual representation is realised over a smaller field). So the step '𝔭^{d−1}κ(G_L) = W_𝔭, therefore κ(G_L) = W_{𝔭^d}' is not justified as written; only the O-span is forced. The lemma's conclusion survives with O-spans. The author's final version (p. 107) makes exactly this repair: 'therefore Oκ(G_L) = W_{𝔭^d} … Oκ(J) ⊂ W_{𝔭^{d−1}} + (τ − 1)W_M'. The chain written there still has the slip of E22.
sourceIssues.known: corrected in the author's final version of the book (https://www.wstein.org/people/rubin/book/hEulerSystems.pdf, Annals-Studies pagination), p. 107, proof of Lemma 5.2.1: 'therefore 𝒪κ(G_L) = W_{𝔭^d}'
